Risk of Rain is an intense rogue like. The game play is fantastic classic 8/16 bit platformer action. You have four abilities to aid you in the journey of survival. Twelve different characters you can play. Three game modes that scale well, the easiest of which does not allow the saving of progress. Combine all this with TONS of items that offer passive and on use advantages. The item combos can get crazy, like in The Binding of Issac. AND if you get more than one of an item it will stack.
This game is great if you have only 15min to play or 5 hours to play. Easy to pick up and get the hang of, but difficult to master no doubt. If you are new to rogue like games this is a great intro to the genre. Overall I would rate this game 8/10. It is a must play for any rogue like fan.

TLDR:
Atmosphere: 10.5/10 - An always beautiful landscape with an overwhelming tone of dread that seeps through the pores with every step. With a real-world cycle of Day and Night, the threats are forever changing keeping the game's atmosphere fresh and terrifying. Side missions do an excellent job of making the world feel alive, even if mostly everyone around you is dead.
Sound: 10/10 - Being surrounded by the infected, sounds have never been more important. Techland did a beautiful job rendering the effects. You can hear every distant gargle, every faint scream, every angry grunt. The sounds for this game are prominent, crisp and clear.
Gameplay: 9/10 - Crafting items and weapons has always been a core element in open-world games, but the way Techland presents it makes it accessible to anyone, which isn't always easy to do. While the amount of Blueprints are abundant, the weapon variety is not very diverse. After putting about 10 hours in I had seen every weapon I was going to see for the rest of my playthrough, which was dissapointing. The free running is the biggest aspect of this game because it is such a new concept to include in a zombie genre title. It really brings the mechanics full-circle and makes the feel of surviving and traversing the landscape more realistic and in your control. That being said, it would have been nice to have implemented your parkour into your fighting a little more. Also, some of the story missions tend to miss the mark on occasion. You'll even find that some of the side missions are more enjoyable than some of the story missions. That is a little unfortunate. However, the ever awesome new game plus unlocks once you complete the main story and it lets you carry over everything except main/side mission progress, increasing the overall games difficulty to a more suitable zombie apocalypse. It is truly an awesome feature that I am highly glad they added.
OVERALL: 9.5/10 - It is a grand zombie-slaying experience and it is also the pinnacle of zombie gaming thus far. The amount of content you get for the price is no doubt worth it. I recommend it for any gamer and for just plain fans of zombies. This is just a must have title.
HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.
Good night. Good luck.
________________________________________________________________
BIGGEST STRENGTHS:
Free Running - The city of Harran is literally your playground. You have complete freedom of movement, which is everything in crucial situations...like a zombie apocalypse. You can scale brick walls, thirty story buildings, giant fences, city bridges; jump over vehicles, rooftops, even crowds of zombies in order to stay alive. You can upgrade to use a grappling hook and get to hard to reach places or get inventive with your parkour! The movement if very fluid, it just takes some getting used to. It has a real weighted feel to it which adds a very nice dynamic to the gameplay that I dig alot, personally.
Day / Night Cycle - This is my favorite thing about this game, hands down. During the day you have an advantage because the zombies are slowed down by bright light so they act and react lethargically. But at night...everything changes for the worse. Common infected become stronger and more aggressive, while Virals get even angrier and tend to hunt you down in packs. The stars of the show are clearly the Volatiles, though. With their mandible jaws and mutated nude appearances, they look like they were ripped straight from a Clive Barker short story. They only emerge from their hives at night to stalk the city streets in search of prey. They actively pursue you and if they catch you in their sights they will alarm the others. This is when you either stand your ground or you run like you're on fire.
Online Zombie Mode / Co-op - You or others can invade games as a Unique Infected called a Hunter. It is PVP, but you have the entire environment to stalk them. Like the humans, this Infected comes with a skill tree to upgrade it's zombie abilties to become the ultimate predator. Online can be played with up to four players, including the story line...which is pretty groovy.
**NEW GAME PLUS** - I could not stress how important this is in an open world game. It was such a nice surprise. New game plus unlocks upon 100% main story completion and it lets you carry over your stats and inventory while resetting your campaign / side story progress. This does quite a few interesting things to the AI. Not only do they all act more aggressive all around, there are way more of them. Each kind, too. I've been finding Bomber's and Goon's left and right just filling the streets. At night time, I thought the original campaign was enough Volatiles. Apparently not. On NG+ it's like a Volatile BREEDING GROUND up in this ♥♥♥♥♥, I swear to God. It's the most amazing thing ever. After plugging 40 hours into the original I was no longer threatened. I could kill anything I wanted and not worry about taking too much damage. With the enemy's newfound strength and population...I can actually feel my heart beating again....
OTHER STRENGTHS:
Crafting - Collect a large amount of blueprints by exploring the city and doing missions. Collect the necessary items on the blueprint to create badass weapons of mass destruction...or different medicines to give you advantages in battle. Not only does it give you another excuse to explore the maps, it gives more depth to the melee system that is the core of this game.
*Mission Structure - This is a special case for me. As far as story's "writing" goes, they knocked this out of the park. I was almost always on the edge of my seat and ready for the next mission to see where they will take it. The story has a lot of depth and a lot of heart, the Dev's clearly wanted that to come first. But as far as the mission structure goes...it varies. While they were fun and definitely a joy to play, albiet may be for the initial excitement of the first playthrough, but overall it felt a little underwhelming at some parts....In my own opinion I sometimes felt a little restrained by the game itself. When there were times that screamed for me to take action the character was set on autopilot for narrative's sake. I do understand why, but it's still unfortunate because it took away some of the immersion. This game has quite a bit of innovation as far as gameplay mechanics and zombie killing, but there was also some missed potential that you could feel under the surface. It's definitely a gigantimous skyscraper of an improvement over it's predecessor and I highly reccomend it to anyone who games. I just sometimes find myself looking forward to what they are going to do next more than what they gave us. The side missions were worked on really hard and that also is very apparent. They are usually multi-layered and the voice acting is spot on. You can feel there is a lot of emotion and when the story is mixed altogether with the base game it feels a lot more comfortable and wholesome. Techland did an outstanding job at making the environment around us a living and breathing world. I dig it alot and I can get lost in it for hours on end.
Skill Tree - Like a lot of open world games, this one has skills to unlock the more you progress. Each skill makes you more of a bad♥♥♥♥♥and there are a lot of cool skills here to play with.
In this you have three medium sized trees to choose between: Survivor, Agility and Power.

The Batman: Arkham series is among my favorite super-hero game franchises, and Arkham Knight is a great conclusion to the saga. While Arkham City still remains as my favorite game in the series, Arkham Knight has many great things about it that make it a solid game.
: 8/10
Arkham Knight's story is great and enjoyable from beginning to the end. Scarecrow as the main villain was menacing throughout the story, and I liked what they did with him. I thought the Arkham Knight was interesting side villain, even if the plot twist on his identity wasn't too surprising and his grudge against Batman made him whiny at times. Besides them, there is also Joker who still torments Batman as an inner demon even after his death. I thought that the side quests however, were hit or miss. While some were great such as the Riddler's mission where you have to save Catwoman, or Penguin's where you team up with Nightwing; other missions such as most of the Militia ones I found tedious (
).
: 8/10
Arkham Knight's gameplay is one the best in the entire series. Fighting, stealthing and flying around as Batman has never felt any better. Batman has new combos and finishing animations that are satisfying to watch, and there a couple of new gadgets that are fun to use. A major addition to the series is the ability to now drive around in the Batmobile, which has a tank mode which allows it to fight the Militia's drone tanks. I found the Batmobile fun to drive around and fight in, and while it did feel unnecessary and overused at times, it still didn't ruin the my experience with the game. Besides the main story and side missions, there are also various VR missions and challenge modes to play as well.
: 7/10
The game's graphics look great, as I was running it on Medium/High settings on my PC. But while the majority of the performance issues and bugs were fixed from launch, I still had some FPS drops or freezes  in certain parts of the game and while driving the Batmobile. Also occasionally, the game's audio would cut out and I would have to pause it to make it return. Although this didn't affect my experience that much, it was still annoying to deal with at times.
: 9/10
I played through the entire game with an Xbox One controller, so I can't speak for the mouse and keyboard controls. The controls felt great and I had no problems with them. The only issue I had was not being able to rebind or change the actions for the controller.
:
Batman: Arkham Knight is a great game, although it doesn't surpass Arkham City in my opinion. If you've played the previous Arkham games and were waiting for it to be fixed, I definitely recommend you pick it up. Rocksteady did an amazing job with the Arkham series and I'm excited to see what their next project is.

This game is the combination of the original game Toukiden: Age of Demons and the expansion Kiwami. The story mode has 13 chapters with most chapters having around 20 missions.
You play as a SLAYER who has recently come to the village as a new recruite. Off the bat monsters start attacking and you quickly prove you are no normal fighter. As you progress you find out why these monsters are attacking and the backstory to all the other slayers in the village. As far as story goes, the game does a great job. Chapters 3 and 4 are probably my favorite for how intence the situation becomes.
The game has several side missions that can be done to earn extra items or unlock certain gear. There is also the multiplayer mode where you can go online and join up with others to do missions. There is even a good training mode for each weapon and special ability.
The graphics are good but nothing special. The framrate is locked to 30 if you are concerned about that. The levels are nicely detailed with asian locations that have been ravaged from battle and taken from their original locations. These locations will send you through grassy, lava filled, ice covered, and desert environments/ At the beginning, the game lets you create your character and choose your weapon style. Throughout the game you can change most of these features at will. The NPCs all have distinct looks which add to the realism.
Gameplay is quite repetative. At the beginning you start out by clearing the surrounding locations. Going from section to section until you have killed so many of a type of creature. Later they add a boss at the end that must be hunted. The maps are extremely repetative in the begining and slowly start to varry as you move on in chapters.
The weapons and armor in the game is vast and can look really goos to downright horrid. There was one set of armore that looked like a jester outfit with a forest theme. Then there was something that was red and black and looked all cyberpunk-like. As much as there was variety, I felt that they did not give that much a change in attack and defence until you reach the really good items towards the end.
The bosses of this game are very destinctive in regards to the type. There are clones of almost every one of them, however they do posses different or more abilities. As you fight these bosses, you sever their limbs to weaken them. This is where these fights get long and boring. You have to break off several pieces and then stop fighting to purify the part so it does not retain as much of a defence. The body part does come back but the creture does not maintail (ALL) of its ability.
As far as bugs go, I can say that I was very lucky to not have any issue while playing for 40+ hours. I have a custome made Micro-ITX PC sporting an I7 cpu with a GTX 980Ti playing on a 55" 4K TV. Not a beast of a system by any way but still not a simple one either. As many have mentioned, the controls pretty much require a controller and not a keyboard to actually play the game and have any amount of fun.
If you are looking for a good hack and slask type of game similar to "Monster Hunter", this is a game for you. The storyline is good, the graphics are good, music is repetative but not anoying. The only thing that really kills this game is the amount of repetativeness it contains.

If this was a movie it'd be a Michael Bay film, violent, explosive and some story that is just sorta there. Now don't get me wrong, it's a great game and the strategy durring fights can prove challenging. The enemy AI is where the game loses me.
You can do a tutorial for the game and if you have the Enemy Within dlc you get another tutorial but both can be skipped without losing anything. You'll spend most of the game in the base researching things, building facilities to build new things, with the Enemy Within dlc you'll also spend a good bit of time modding your soldiers, and towards the end of the game you will also spend plenty of time finding out just how many of your soldier's are psychic and powerful. The big thing here is that you cannot craft items of buildings without certain materials that you get in fights, sometimes you will go long periods of time without any fights or maybe you needed cash and sold the items you needed without knowing you needed them.
Now after you get past all the base stuff you'll eventually get into a fight with the aliens, there are a few different types of fights but most play out the same: Drop in, kill all the aliens, sometimes you will need to deactivate something, plant something or save civilians which is by far the hardest. Durring missions where you have to save civillians you run into aliens that hit hard, poison, and can run across that map in just 2 or 3 turns, and when they kill a civ they turn it into a zombie that has near the most health in the game, kills in one hit and can move several spaces in one turn. Durring every mission you will run into several different aliens from the canon fodder, to the posionus sentries, to the massive brutes and then towards the end the giant hard hitting drones.
The biggest problem in my eyes with this game is that no matter what difficulty the AI seems to be on top of it's game, some of the hardest i've seen in a strategy game, they move, attack and use special abilities with a certain level of thought. The worst part of the AI is that when you find them they get a free move, i personally used a mod to remove that to help make the fights a bit more fair.
Now a very important part of any media is story and this game certainly has one, you're not allowed to forget that, but it's not a very good one.

Aside from the few problems XCOM: Enemy Unknown is a fantastic game that you never really need to end, as far as i am aware there is no deadline for you to do the final mission, simply keep fighting aliens. If i was a critic i would give this game an 8/10, fun to play but the AI needs some serious balancing with the difficulty, a bit more fairness and a better story.

I can only agree with other reviews, this game does indeed feel like a bad Monster Hunter clone. It brings a few cool ideas, like the spirits you can put into your weapons which give you several buff skills. But in the end, nothing really changes no matter what you do. Killing a monster while abusing its elemental weakness takes about as long as with a 'normal' weapon. Killing a monster with a club that should've dealt about 400 damage more than my dual blades at that point made no difference, either. I mean.. why even bother with the slowest weapon that SHOULD hit like a truck if in reality it doesn't give you any noticeable advantage compared to the fastest weapon?
All in all it is a very simple game compared to Monster Hunter, which is fine by me, since I haven't played much of this genre yet. But after almost 15 hours of playtime, I've only encountered three(!) different monsters, over and over again. They weren't very exciting for the first time, and only became much more boring with every single fight. I guess this is the single most huge flaw a 'hunting game' can have.
Still, I might have even continued playing one hour or two every once in a while if it weren't for the crashes. About every second time you try to change the area, the game just gives you a CTD. Only need to secure one more zone? Nope, crash, you can restart the whole mission. Or, even better, a boss kicks you out of the area? Well, better be lucky and hope you can even get back to him.
TL;DR: Toukiden is a simple and repetetive hunting game with several gameplay issues and becomes boring quickly. Combined with being another infamous Koei Tecmo PC port, neither fans of the genre nor newcomers should waste their time with this, especially not with God Eater being right around the corner.

Buyer beware: This game is very hardware intensive, riddled with bugs (pun intended), and full of CONSTANT crashes unless you satisfy every condition the game requires to stay stable.
All that being said, the game itself is really fantastic. Piloting the Batmobile is extremely fun and easy and the combat is simple and very satisfying. A good handful of combat and predator mechanics have been added, and they really add to the game feel and flow of fighting. Gliding over the (gigantic) city is effortless. The city and environments themselves are absolutely gorgeous and almost entirely destructible. This did come with a price, however, in that I lost frames all the time even running a pretty mid to high end rig.
As for the story, an M rating is exactly what this franchise needed. The villains are very threatening and have a lot to say about Batman's inner demons. The narrative is dark and tackles a lot of shady segments of the Dark Knight's past, which was very engrossing as someone who doesn't necessarily know a ton about the Batman mythos. The game has a decent pace but it feels like you're running in circles sometimes. Luckily, the game isn't padded out with an unnecessary amount of collectibles: the game has half the Riddler challenges as City.
Overall, this game is a worthy ending to the Arkham series.

The Shivah is a visual novel point & click mystery adventure.  The protagonist is a rabbi who is doing his best to hold his synagogue together.  He tries very hard to stay true to his religious beliefs while his congregation is falling apart, but finds himself in a complicated moral dilemma when he is forced to accept a cashed in life insurance policy.  The police start investigating him, his fellow rabbis are shunning him, and shadows are creeping behind him.
The story, plot, and script is well written with extra attention to making every decision a challenging moral dilemma.  Each moral decision affects the end of the story, similar to Telltale games like The Walking Dead and The Wolf Among Us.  Outside of the story based decisions, the puzzles are very detail oriented, and I recommend keeping a notepad on the side to write down clues.  Not every clue is going to be obvious, but each scene is pretty limited as far as interaction goes.  I completed the entire game in about two hours without any outside help.  If there was more to explore in each environment, the overall experience might have been a little more compelling.  Some type of pillow shots would have been welcome to build up suspense and reflection.
The graphics are a bit on the simple side, but are well visualized none the less.  The voice acting is decent, and the ambient music helps flesh out each situation without feeling too contrived.  You’re not going to play the game for the audio and visual effects, or be compelled to download the soundtrack, but the game does well with what is provided.  The main focus is on the story anyways.
Overall, despite it being short and simple, the moral dilemmas really made the game well worth the price I paid for it.  I do have to give a warning to those devout of any religion.  The game touches on subjects that could be interpreted as being sacrilegious, and may be very upsetting to some.  The environment and circumstances do touch on real life situations that are not completely unheard of.  I hope that anyone who plays it realizes it is a story of fiction first and foremost.  I do recommend this to anyone who enjoys a good whodunnit mystery.

Intense and repetitive
* The Port
This game consists of Toukiden: Age of Demons and it's expansion Kiwami. Even though Toukiden: Kiwami was released on PS4 as well, this is a PS Vita port. The graphics are not bad, but could look better, and the game is locked at 30fps. It also lacks some screen resolutions
* The Story
Age of Demons uses the "monsters are attacking the world" story, and aside of some happenings, it's really generic. Kiwami's story, on the other hand, has much more mystery to it and a few plot-twists. And overall, the characters have solid personalities and there's a fair bit of humor
* The Gameplay
It is the non-Nintendo Monster Hunter, with a few upgrades. The weapon variety is big, and each one is very unique in its combat style. Mitamas - souls of past warriors - gives you passive and active skills that make a huge difference in battle. There is a lack in mission diversity - most of them are either kill the boss or kill a few enemies in some zones
Which brings us to the bosses. Fighting them is really exciting for the first few times: you learn what are their breakable parts (breaking them let you hit through their shield, reduces their damage and some lose abilities), attack patterns and how to fight them when they rampage. On the other hand, they are all HP sponges, so expect to spend 10 minutes smashing buttons on every fight
* Final Thoughts
Toukiden Kiwami could be a great game, but it is just good. Kiwami is a great improvement to the base game in every way: story, bosses, weapons and kinds of mitama
Once again Koei failed to provide a good port, choosing the Vita version instead of PS4
The story paces well and, for most part, gives you a new challenge. But as you progress, the "new" bosses are just recycled versions of past ones with a few different attacks. As you get closer to the end, you may feel bored to hell to fight the closely same bosses every mission
This game is, by no means, worth $60 - simply because of the poor port. Luckily, it goes on sale every now and then, and $30 is enough for the many hours of fun it can provide

This is definitely one of my favorite turn-based strategy games.

(Note: There's DLC available for more missions and marine gear!)

Toukiden Kiwami ("TK") is perfect for Monster Hunter ("MH") fans.
Here are the similarities and differences that I find between TK and MH:
Similarities:
- Hunt monsters for body parts to craft stronger armors and weapons
- MH have water, thunder, fire, and ice elements. TK have all of them with additional elements such as earth, wind, and sky.
- Complete quest, each phase introduce new and stronger monsters.

tl;dr: This game is very challenging, but it's a lot of fun if you stick with it.
Fundamentally, CitD is an old-school 2D platformer in the Metroidvania style. The story is paper-thin, but you're not playing it for the gripping plot: you're playing because the game offers hardcore challenges that never stop coming. Make no mistake: this game is hard. Be prepared to die a lot every time you enter a new area. If the enemies don't get you, there's no shortage of instant-death spikes that will. Still, if you have the patience to learn each new area and keep practicing until you can make every jump, there's a lot of cool stuff to find.
The world is pretty big overall; I've seen bigger, but there's definitely enough area to keep you going for quite a few hours. Nearly every area has something new to find if you come back with later upgrades (particularly the double-jump), and it's very hard to find everything a given zone has to offer on the first run through.
The bosses range from trivial to excruciatingly hard. Some of them went down on the first or second try (even relatively late in the game), while some of them took me days to beat. I do wish the difficulty curve was a bit smoother for some of the bosses, and there are a couple bosses that are all but impossible to beat without specific items or spells, which feels like it could be fairer. Still, none of them are truly impossible (especially if you find every single upgrade possible), and it's really satisfying to beat one that's been giving you hell. (Just make sure that you save immediately afterward!)
The game is jam-packed with references to other games (mostly classic, but some more recent). I don't really consider this to be especially good or bad; it can be entertaining to see references you recognize, but the game seems to hardly have anything that isn't inspired by something else, so it can get a little tiresome. (Some of the references are really darn obscure, too—I was expecting the Zelda references and the Castlevania references, but I was shocked to see a reference to Magic Sword, the 1992 Capcom game on the SNES.) They're cute if you like that sort of thing, but they can get old even if you get most of them. Still, I wouldn't count this as a reason not to play the game.
There are some places where the game lacks polish. If there's a way to pause (especially while using a controller), I haven't found it, which just seems like a huge oversight. There's no map screen or minimap, so you have to have a pretty good memory if you want to remember where all the alternate paths lead (or where you need to come back to once you have more mobility upgrades). While none of the challenges are downright unfair (in the style of, for example, I Wanna Be The Guy), some of them can feel a little underhanded if you're not prepared for them. You do collect gold to buy upgrades, but the opportunities to spend money don't come evenly; you have quite a few at the beginning, and then you go for the bulk of the game before you find the next ones, which feels choppy. There's basically no invulnerability period after taking damage, so if you're used to having a chance to get away from danger that way, you might be in for a rude awakening. And like I said, some of the bosses will have you tearing your hair out, especially if you haven't found every single upgrade possible. Finally, the final boss is really disappointing (I beat him on the first or second try, no problem), which feels like a letdown after such a challenging game. (Yes, I know that I just said that some bosses are too hard, and then I complained that the final boss is too easy. My point is that the curve is off.)
Overall, though, I really enjoyed this game. It really is punishingly hard, but there's no part of it that's truly impossible. It's challenging from the get-go and never lets up, but with the exception of one or two bosses, there's never a crazy difficulty spike that makes you feel like you've hit a wall. Aside from the lack of an accessible pause button, the controls are simple and responsive, It's hard enough to make me feel challenged, but it's got enough hidden items (and even just save points) to continually reward you for trying. If you grew up on 2D platformers and you're willing to practice a new one until you master it, you can have a lot of fun with Castle in the Darkness. I recommend it.

Don't buy this thinking it's KF1 updated to look pretty and nothing else, there are a few small changes that make a big impact on the overall feel and play style - not to everyone's taste but enjoyable if you can get over the fact that this is KF1’s younger sibling.
The most notable change is movement speed, no longer are you forced to make in the moment decisions about whether to stand and fight or push forward to another part of the map because you are now able to sprint, this coupled with the Medics movement speed talent allows one to go full Sanic mode, which means you can out run a lot of the Zeds in the game, that coupled with the larger more open and “flowing” maps make for less stressed and easier matches even on harder difficulty.
Maps are larger with more open areas and choke points, entry/exit point's making it harder to get overwhelmed by Zeds, unless you are a “Sticky Feet” player who refuses to move.
They are on the whole good looking and interesting (excluding Containment Station), it was also nice of Tripwire to top up the meter and turn the lights on in most maps such as Catacombs as dark maps generally (for me) aren't fun to play and add no amount of spookiness to a non-spooky game.

The Medic gun's now shoot darts which lock onto a player below maximum health and in your line of sight making it far easier for casual scrubs like myself to keep at least one quarter of the team alive.

We had a nostalgic blast as we experienced the corny charm of Freddi Fish. And I am pleased to say that after over fifteen years...I finally completed Freddi Fish. Ha ha!

Another Humongous Entertainment franchise done and done with. And I finished both in the same day!
But... yeah, I think as a whole, Freddi Fish just isn't a great series of games. Not when compared to Spy Fox and Pajama Sam. The series keeps suggesting this whole "mystery-detective" angle to the Humongous formula, but never really delivers (save partially for Freddi Fish 3, which I can now say is the best of the series).
However, I'd say Freddi Fish 5 is a great contender for second-best Freddi Fish game!
What a wonderful title.
Freddi Fish 5 follows Freddi and Luther on, yet again, another big mystery to be had. There's a sea monster roaming around Coral Park and the detective duo are out to find out just what is going on at the park. And you know what? I think for once, Humongous understood how to make an actual mystery out of their story. It isn't the best attempt like Freddi Fish 3's but it's still good enough. The story takes some slightly interesting twists and turns with its development, and I was left wondering what was going on.
But, the biggest problem with this story is that you know who it'll be everytime. The culprit and explanation for the crime is the same each time. You can argue that this is better writing as opposed to Freddi Fish 3, where it's just a random clue and random culprit every time and even THAT can be predictable after a while, too, but I still prefer 3 to 5 in that regard personally.
The story does have a lot of cheesey and convenient moments. The dialogue and writing aren't as atrocious as Freddi Fish 4 (and not as many weird glitches, to boot), but there are plenty of moments that made me raise my eyebrow and wonder why the hell the characters in the story would do certain things. Especially on the Sea Monster and main villain's actions in the story.
However, the aesthetic design and music are probably at their best here, specifically the music being the biggest update. Infogrames got to handle this project and their excellent control on sound design in the Spy Fox series really translates well to Freddi Fish (it might be why there was an improvement in writing, too). And the world is actually colorful and enjoyable to explore. I wouldn't say it's as beautiful as the massive locations you enter in Freddi Fish 3, but it's still well lit and well-colored.
Beyond that, Freddi Fish 5 concludes the kinda drab series with a pretty decent send-off. Will 1, 2, and 4 are absolute cattle fodder in my opinion, Freddi Fish 3 and 5 are the two slightly better games in the series. Not perfect, by any stretch, but simple fun for you to waste an afternoon with. Hell, I bet you could play all 5 games in a day if you had the gumption to. And I'm giving Freddi Fish 5 a fitting 5/10.

Died because of the ugly brown senseless pixellated art style disguising an insta-death trap rather than running low on resources and getting mobbed by hundreds of flesh-eating beasties in the height of hardcore survival deaths.
Not exactly what was advertised.
The next time I died because one shapeless blob enemy not all that different from the others suddenly started shooting at me and I learned pretty quick that my character doesn't take any more bullets than the enemies do.
Naturally, I could not make out that he had a gun and was about to fire. Nor had I the components for armor by then.
More to the point, Teleglitch isn't bad. It just isn't good. The game revels in the old System Shock 2 pacing with loads of stuff to collect and fiddle with all bouncing around your inventory, but just like System Shock 2, there's a lot of time consuming fiddle and very little in the way of meaningful decisions there. A bunch of crafting components but only one or two clearly useful items to build. Oh, I could make my gun fire twice as many bullets? In a game where ammo is scarce and accuracy is essential? Next you'll offer me an upgrade for that awful knife at the cost of all my cans.
Unlike SS2, this game is actually hard. Combat is brutal and quick. You don't die fast (except for when you do) so it plays to a long haul survival, which I like. Problem is, it's the sort of game you need to repeat over and over and have a wiki open in the other window until you finally manage that perfect run and it just isn't fun enough to carry the game. It has the worst collectathon inventory fiddle of SS2 mixed with the same combat we've seen since Crimsonland and Nation Red only with higher stakes and nothing else that makes those games interesting. The first couple of swarms are fun but once you fight the same swarm a dozen times it's a bit tiresome.
The graphic design is ugly ugly UGLY UGLY! There's no charm in these wretched pixel blobs, which kills any atmosphere of survival dead. The levels themselves bring just as little to the table as the graphics. Big room, room, hallway, room, room with loot, swarm room, ooh loot? no another friggen text log etc etc. This normally wouldn't be bad but the whole game is conspiring to be as charmless and plodding as possible and wants to drag out your time with it with so much repetition so every one of these faults ends up magnified.

I actually really like this game, it got the second Neptunia game out of my mouth.
In basic terms yes it is very similar but with good differences.
The combat system has changed the element of striking enemies into a selective area.
You won't get all your skills from just leveling it up but by unlocking them with these sort of "perk" points used to buff damage, defense, range, your Fairy form "transformation" and  giving you more combos, that's right you don't get your entire combo from the start.
1st The transformation has a subtle change, whenever you get hit or hit an enemy out of form you have a bar representing tension that will rise, after a certain amount filled up you nca fairize which does not cost anything and basically turns you into a badass, thing is it's not permenant, whenever you take a hit the bar falls hard, so no more permanent powerup.
Each character has an actual move specified to them Fang the main character can buff his attack and skills for an extra energy cost to each attack and multiplier to the cost of skills.
Tiara can put up a barrier around herself to reflect a large portion of damage but is unable to attack.
Every character can transform, you are all Fairy Fencers, you can all Fairize.
The story still has comedy but at certain parts the story can and will take a turn for the dark, people actual will die, somtimes you will even see it happen (as much as a virtual novel can without drawing an entire portrait).
There are psychotic crazed murders, some characters do have dark backgrounds.
You can now remove "furies" from two statues which will be used for world forming, which adds buffs and penalties to you like 30% more EXP and -10% Magic Defense, everyone and every mob deals double damage, or disable your skills, etc.
I think there are actually multiple endings which came as quite the suprise to me.
You have challenges for each character which will buff their stats like "Lone Fencer" Battle a # of battles alone.
Now lets get to some of the dirty bussiness.
There are indeed still copy paste monster if not at least less.
Sometimes the game just comes out cliche and the timing of some things are inappropriate.
English has barely any lines for combat, you may be listening to "Fang/Pain don't hurt" I don't think any of us can figure out what the ♥♥♥♥ Fang is trying to say, either way he needs a lesson in grammar.
I like the combat but I can see it getting repetetive for others and you still indeed need to farm extensively but at least world forming will help with that at the same time it seems more difficult to farm.
There are skills that become literally useless further into the game.
Lets get into some more nuetral grounds.
They indeed have removed your ability to change weapons for lore sake but they have replaced it with a system where you equip a second fairy next to your main fairy which resides in your weapon. Anyways this secondary fairy will give you stronger and more passive buffs the more you train them because they do indeed level and I believe cap at 10 though they do take a bit more EXP than most characters.

X-COM (or XCOM) Enemy Unknown (EU) brings a new experience to the previous titles with a long gap in technology for hardware, software and media which results in a explosion of improved graphics, special effects, great audio and animation that are unparalleled when compared to its predecessors, which I might add it honours quite admirably.
XCOM EU orbits around a stregetically turn-based driven combat experience built INTO a railway-linear economy/anagement driven "on-top" game, with a few forks and choices as you go along the path. Most of these choices on the top-layer are to make life berable in the combat layer (in my opinion anyway, X-COM Apocalyps(e) had a much more interesting World-Map combat system and even the first in the series had more options than "send craft", "pray", "win/lose"). The integration betweem the two layers in the game is otherwise nearly seamless as the two affect each other greatly but leave you to your own devices to ensure you succeed in both, or fail miserably in the long run creating a highly sophisticated environment which also encompasses fair balanced combat.
The game has a tangent on difficulty level, which can be edited in the second wave options and possible expansion or a few mods out there leaving you with a strong story driven epic strategy game with good replay value and a satisfying reward as you celebrate victory too soon and quickly return to paying attention when the enemy decides to throw in units with insane hitpoints and near-1-shot-fatal killing abilities. You will have an easier time mostly because you get better. The game itself tries to keep you sharp and I find it does so well enough, better than its predecessors in any case which dropped down to "boringly easy" relatively quickly once you gained tech/ranks.
My only serious concern is for the Iron Man mode Hardcore Classic/Impossible player that wants to drool over achievement and glory (Iron man means no loading game, unless you enjoy killing the task/thread in your OS and revert to auto-save which completely nullifies the point of Iron-Man but the rule means, no loading game for easy wins).  My concern is this; The time-Unit (TU) system you were used has been replaced for a "few actions" driven system. This is valid for the length of the game but NOT in this particular case. If you payed attention during statistics, you want to have more than 1, 99% chance to hit shot because that 1% miss chance over 50 missions will eventually and inveitably become a point of frustration. There is no bell curve on 2 shots, failure is likely on brutally unfair situations with 5 guys on a ledge with better weapons dying to a "lucky crit" from someone you planned for 5 steps before he even knew you were sneaking up on him. Albeit a fair device for simulating a proper war scenario, I find it lacking for the enjoyability of a special high-end challenge. That being the only thing I ever hated about the game and everything else keeping me busy for over tens if not hundreds of hours with a smile a cheer and a laugh....it's well worth the money and is a great honour to modern gaming, which is comparatively a saddening, depressing disappointment on so many cases compared to this incredibly pearl for your collection.

Batman Arkham Knight is far from a bad game...
but my god it's disappointing.
I was so hyped for this game, Batman Arkham Asylum and City and one of my best games of all time, so I was obviously hyped from Arkham Knight. Maybe that's what led me to hate it for months after release and playing it. Well, I bought it on PC now to give my opinion that's not so biased compared to what it would've been at release.
Arkham Knight's gameplay feels much more refined than previous games. It works much better, combat is much much more satisfying, defintely with the addition of being able to use the environment to help (even though I'm 99% sure Batman would've killed someone by putting their head into a power box... but what the heck do I know). Car combat is fun... but it's also the games biggest negative. Whoever thought having car combat in every ♥♥♥♥ing mission, in every side mission, every bloody where should be fired. It was the worst idea, sure there is hand-to-hand combat everywhere, but that's sort of become the standard for these games. Car combat is used beyond the word "tedious", and that's the issue with this whole game, it's tedious as ♥♥♥♥. If car combat was used less then this game could've been brilliant. But it's everywhere, they used it for many boss battles. So believe it or not, this game has the worst boss battles in the whole series, even worse than Arkham Origins! It's a massive setback from the superb Mr. Freeze boss battle in Arkham City. There is just nothing close to that in this game.
The story in this game... well it's alright, but it's predictable at times. The thing this game tries to use to shock us is the Arkham Knight. Well let's put it like this, the Arkham Knight has the most predictable plot twist I have ever witnessed in any game ever. He is the biggest let down of any game ever, if you have ever bothered to look into the lore of Batman you will not be shocked by the plot twist at all. It's so♥♥♥♥♥♥ they tried to best their plot twist of Arkham City and failed miserably, if you want shock value, you won't get it from the Arkham Knight himself. BUT, if you exclude that, the story in this game is actually quite well done, the threat Scarecrow presents is done brilliantly, the connections to other villains makes sense, the Riddler, whilst being overused with the bloody trophies, is done superbly, and actually makes sense why he is trying so hard to scatter loads of trophies, it shows the chronology of his hate towards Batman. I hated how easy it was to get trophies (well data packs) in Arkham Origins, but this game makes that make sense, by showing it's all done to show the Riddlers' increasing hatred towards Batman.
And the ending, the ending actually isn't that much of a let down. But there is an issue, to get the real ending, you must complete the game 100%, then complete the game 100% in New Game +. It's annoying, especially by the fact there are over 250 riddler trophies and a ♥♥♥♥ton of side missions. It can be slightly tedious, so you'd be best off finishing the game 100% once then watching the real ending on YouTube, though if you like the idea of 100%ing the game again, then go for it.
Finally, this has to be put here, the PC port. At release the game was a mess. Now, after 2 years, the game is stable, there are a few stutters, I ran the game on High settings with a GTX 980, i7 4790k, 16GB RAM, but overall the FPS was stable, I think the lowest FPS I reached was about 25FPS, but that was also during a pretty big  moment of the game, though I will update on this as I haven't completed the game on PC as of yet.
Overall, buy the game only if you have played Arkham Asylum and City, possibly Origins if you want the whole lore. It does the series justice in the end, and is a fitting way to end the series, but be warned, it can be tedious as all heck.
TL;DR
+ Fitting end to a superb series
+ The graphics
+ Brilliant use of villains
+ Hand-to-Hand Combat...
~ PC Port
~ Real ending requires to finish the game 100% twice
-...The overuse of Car Combat.
- The Arkham Knight
Overall: 7/10

IGNORE NEGATIVE REVIEWS - Read the bottom of this to see why ...   This game is GENIUS, I love it, This deserves to become more popular and get bigger, from the creators of Dynasty warriors , this even outdoes their other games. I really thought this was a weak monster hunter clone at first, it unlocks everything allot later into the game, so at first it seems very empty and featureless... But after you play for a while you'll see it has a HUGE amount of content, I'll even list them.
FEATURES:
- Good Character Customization - Easily Equal to Monster Hunter full RGB hair color, lots of hairstyles faces etc, no body Build or size sliders but characters still look good, Voices are all Japanese and sound pretty cool as you do moves ingame.
- Incredible Fighting System , Dynasty warriors style with Ultimate Attacks and Team Ultimate attacks, Love it.
- Pet system - And its not a Pig like in Monster Hunter!, finally! - Change Clothing, Color, Voice, etc, your pet can even resurrect you in battle and gather items for you.
- Romances - LGBT friendly even, gain affection from many characters with no discrimination, and hot tub romance em.
- Weapon And Armor Crafting and Upgrading - Similar to Monster Hunter Games with allot of extras on the weapons because of the soul weapon system.
- Customizable Spirit Weaponry - Feel like a Shinigami with a Zanpakuto weapon talking to you lol for Bleach fans.
- Incredible Friendly AI - Some of the best friendly/team unit AI I've seen in any game period, maybe too strong, they can do it all for you, and follow orders like elite soldiers flawlessly... The monsters I feel need an AI boost, they are strong but not as smart as your team.
- Command Units - Later on you get to command followers and send them on missions as well as take them on yours, while using united super attacks and bonding with some romantically.
- Real Lore - The spirits in this game are real people from Japanese lore just like the Heroes from Dynasty Warriors... love these guys for doing this!. If you do your homework and know the connection between characters the spirits even get bonus combinations!.
- Nice Music - Enjoyable Soundtrack with lots of Japanese themes that adjusts to the mood of gameplay and stops when combat starts, Oni spotted, emotions run High or low etc
- LOTS of story - Cinematic story that goes on for Hours, (so far among my friends its over 50+ hours RPG style, and thats with one who plays constantly and doesn't work) very long campaign, you'll have tons to do, with even more DLC content... The story makes you feel like the main character and hero of an anime saga , and you have to make decisions often that will decide if you are loved or hated by the characters you spend time with.
- Training System is good for new players to hunter style games, it explains the moves very well. With training rooms that you can test out every single weapon and practice rooms that you can cut loose in.
CONS:
- Easy Gameplay : Personally I havent seen much challenge to this game yet, at the very least my friends who play and enjoyed monster hunter have been alittle bored with the monster strength, but theres still more gameplay to see, maybe they get harder later...
- DLC armor cant be customized and you cant wear one piece or another, just the entire set, wich ruins any fun of mixing and matching... but at least you get set bonuses I guess.. = \
- Missing translations - This actually annoys me, certain parts of the game especially character phrases in combat are not translated. Even characters you romance you wont know what they're saying in combat.. even if its about you... = (
- Simple Weaponry - Weapons don't get exotic and fancy, no energy blades or swords on fire, etc. As far as I've seen and looked up, the weapons stay plain.
- Unbalanced Weapons - This was probably designed for Team Play but some weapons just don't allow jump attacks, like the Katana, and Fists/Gauntlets, so you need friends or AI to hit the upper monster parts... not good, would highly recommend changing that.
Technical Issues:
WARNING - There are issues the Negative reviews are true, so before you enjoy please understand there are some problems.
1 - Theres a framerate bug, theres a setting in the launcher all the way on the rightmost tab that stabilizes this so it runs well again. And the game must run in fullscreen, if not, you will suffer a weird 30 fps cap... this needs be fixed, but as long as your in Fullscreen and have the setting enabled, you'll be fine.
2 - You need a controller... sorry to say this has some of the worst Keyboard controls I've ever seen.... it was designed for controller play, and really doesn't give any mercy.
3 - Very Japanese, traditional olschool music, sounds, characters, names, everythings subtitled, except some mid battle phrases, so be sure you love Japanese culture allot. And know a few words here and there.
4 - Multiplayer has 2 modes, English and ALL, if you select ALL, and your friends are on ENGLISH, you will never be able to connect to them... without any error or warning, this plus the lack of story in Multiplayer has made it pretty empty most of the time in Multiplayer, If you want to support the game , please host some Multiplayer games.
CONCLUSION:
Worth buying this game!, On sale though, $60 is too much with all the technical issues honestly... but you will enjoy it if you give it time, especially if you love anime, Japanese culture, Koei/W-Force , Want something that will keep you busy for a long time with lots of story. Looking for a different feel from Monster Hunter style games etc. Just be flexible and keep it fullscreen, and only play if you have a controller. Avoid if you don't like story or are only going to play for the multiplayer experience. You need to do story in this, and that is the best experience. Besides that have fun. Oni out Fortune In..

Fairy Fencer F is an interesting game, it somewhat appears in the shadow of the Hyperdimension series and with the polish that those games had you should have high expectations for this one.
In the end those expectations are met. It certainly is fun and hilarious, you really cant go wrong with it, there is a pretty nice bang for buck with this title.
Storyline: At first its pretty linear and well it drags you along with what seems like a cookie cutter story. Well things change and things happen which arent expected. The various endings are a bit lack luster though, they are bitter sweet but leave you wanting more. Though im not sure if this is getting a sequel, not even sure how they could do a sequel with the storyline this has. Its a lot more serious then hyperdimension but its still full of various jokes.
Combat: The combat is very similar to that of hyperdimension's, by that i mean its got nice effects, nice moves, variation etc etc. Unless hyperdimension you have to earn the combats and the amount of attacks you can do, personally i think its a bit of a pain, it can become a grind fest. You control three charecters in this game.
The port: The port is good, no crashes at all, audio lag for a few seconds if you tab out but that fixes itself very quickly. Textures are serviceable, they could be higher res but i cant complain, they are good enough. The game runs at a solid 60fps. It uses the windows resolution system which means you can go nuts with the resolution options, you want 4k thats fine, want 8k yeah it works(suprisingly well with my 680 20fps at 8k isnt bad).
Overall: If you like anime, rpgs, funny storys, bang for buck, multiple endings, hack n slash etc then this is a really nice game to buy.
Side note this game is optimized for a controller which honestly you guys need, many games work a lot better with controllers and this is one of them. it would be nice for it to be optimized for mouse and keyboard, id say that is currently the biggest issue.

"Yo dude. What's happening?"
"Um...Hi."
"I have a question for you. What does the 'B' in Susan B. Anthony stand for?"
"Uhhhh"
"BOOYAH!" I pull a silver dollar out of my shirt pocket and present it and my car keys to the confused valet.
"Take good care of it and I'll throw in another Susanna." I remark with a chuckle. My name's PepsimanVsJoe and apparently I'm supposed to write a review for Fairy Fencer F. The problem is-
"The problem is you just gave your keys away!" My partner cuts in.
"Huh? That was the valet."
"Have you ever heard of a Taco Bell having valet parking?!" He looks at me like I'm an idiot. "God you're dumb. Yet somehow you can manage to put two words together. I mean for crying out loud you don't even play videogames. I don't even play videogames! I hate them!" He sighs, cracks his knuckles for an eternity, and continues. "Luckily for us, there are three people that enjoyed playing Fairy Fencer F, and they're interested in talking about it."
"Really? Wow. I'd love to hear from them."
"...They're right over here." He leads me to a booth near the back of the high-class restaurant.
A young man extends a hand, which I promptly shake. "Hi PepsimanVsJoe! My name is Piven. My favorite games include Halo, Call of Duty, and Gears of War."
"And you like Fairy Fencer F? Really?"
"Yes...well okay yeah it sounds strange when you think about it. Fairy Fencer F is an anime RPG about fairies and crap, but I think it's a well-done game. It reminds me of...well...Taco Bell. It's comfort food, the kind you never really get tired of. Playing online multiplayer gets pretty stressful, so it's nice having something I can chill with. The protagonist, Fang, is an interesting guy. He talks about eating and sleeping a lot, but he also has a strong sense of justice."
"I stopped listening after you compared the game to Taco Bell." said a voice hiding behind a Playstation Vita. Ignoring my meager attempts at a handshake, he introduces himself: "The name is Joss. I play all of the RPGs. I'm an RPG sponge."
"What would you say is Fairy Fencer F's most admirable quality?" I ask.
"Piven merely glossed over the storyline, which is actually pretty well done. It shows a surprising amount of ambition, even if it can be uneven at times. Thankfully the well-written characters make the far-fetched aspects of the plot easier to swallow. Also, unlike the Neptunia series, Compile Heart's bread & butter, this game isn't as light-hearted, which makes for a good change of pace."
"Yeah, The Neptunia games are pretty cool." Piven cuts in. "But you missed the reason why someone would prefer Fairy Fencer F."
"Oh really?" Joss frowns. Actually I'm just guessing he's frowning. It's hard to tell since he hasn't moved his face from behind that Vita.
"Playing FFF really highlights the pacing issues the Neptunia games can sometimes have. In those games you can spend a lot of time repeating certain dungeons, or going to multiple locations just to view more cut-scenes. Sometimes I just want to play the game, or at least get some new characters and have them stick around for more than a dungeon or two."
"...You have a point, FFF does seem a bit fresher, despite sharing many of the same qualities as the Neptunia series. However, FFF lacks the unique personality of the Gamindustri's culture and lore. That's not even considering the complete lack of amusing references and characters designed after your favorite games."
"My favorite games? Last I checked. Most of the NPCs in Neptunia are Merio, Looigi, and a bunch of other random nonsense from Japanese magazines that I've never heard of. They don't have anything to say, but I have to read every ridiculous comment that flies way over my head, just so I don't miss a plan or whatever else I need to 100% complete the game. At least Fairy Fencer F keeps everything focused. It tells a story I can relate to...at least as far as fairies transforming into weapons that are pulled out of the ground will allow." Before Joss can argue, he's cut off by -
"Name's Pam. I like 2D shooters, anything with a lot of action, and I'm weak for MMOs and Diablo-clones. You two fail to realize - or are completely ignoring -  the real problem with Fairy Fencer F: It's too easy! Sure, I can't go into these games expecting a level of depth comparable to hardcore dungeon-crawlers like Wizardry, but FFF is less challenging than the Neptunia games. At least those titles have the neat combo-systems, the three kinds of attacks, and so on. All I did in this game was mash buttons. The only fights I lost were when I was severely underleveled, and that was the DLC."
I cut in "You said you liked the game...didn't you?"
"Of course I did! Compile Heart doesn't create challenging RPGs, but they deserve all the love in the world for making it so effortless to get through battles quickly. I can watch the flashy special moves, then just skip through everything for the real content: the characters and story."
"I agree." Piven speaks up. "Compile Heart knows how to cater to its fans. They've captured an audience that ignores Visual Novels...by creating Visual Novels with RPG elements."
"Hate to say it, but I agree with dudebro." Joss admits. "What makes this game enjoyable is that it allows the player to enjoy as much - or as little - of an RPG they want. They can avoid grinding and focus on equipment as well as tactics, or simply focus on what matters to them. Overall, I think we all just wanted a relaxing game, that didn't demand a lot from us."
"Psh...Grinding." Pam grumbles. "The grind in this game is the worst. I think it's a law somewhere that Compile Heart has to include a couple ridiculous achievements that take forever. I think they do it just to sell DLC. Also this game has a plethora of minor cheevos. They're the kind where you get a little stat boost if you jump a thousand times or get the first strike in however many battles. It just seems like content for the sake of it, but at this point I'm just nitpicking."
"Hold up. Did I just admit to playing a Visual Novel?" Piven looks like he wants to lie down and cry.
My partner, lulled to sleep by this incredibly fascinating dialogue, suddenly snaps awake. "Well. There you have it PepsimanVsJoe. That was Piven, Joss, and Pam with their thoughts on the game. I expect a full write-up by tomorrow morning."
"I have the concluding paragraph already in my head." I tell him as I wave goodbye to everyone else. "Thanks Mr. E"

This game devolves very early on into a super meat boy clone-style frustration-platformer where 100% of the challenge/difficulty comes from not dying to unforgiving instant-kill spike, falling spike and buzzsaw obstacles by flawlessly performing various jump sequences. The game is not difficult otherwise - enemies and bosses are trivially easy, in fact. They follow simplistic and predictable patterned ais and have obvious weaknesses. Most bosses can be defeated handily by jumping around haphazardly while blasting off the same single spell over and over and with regular enemies the best course of action usually is to jump over and proceed past them unharmed. When one-hit kill spike obstacles are the only real threat to the player it renders the majority of the game's already somewhat meager action-adventure-rpg elements irrelevant - it doesn't matter what armor, magic, weapon and relics you wield if the only dangerous obstacles kill you outright, regardless, whenever you don't time a jump perfectly. Buy and play it if you want finnicky platforming and nostalgia-inducing references and easter eggs. Pass on it if you want any semblance of even a vague storyline, worthwhile hidden collectibles, rpg elements that have even a modicum of depth to them, cool gameplay-altering weapons and spells, interesting characters, varied gameplay, or challenging, rewarding monster and boss encounters. Still addictive if you're a masochist but nothing like the vastly superior Cave Story.

I have almost 200 hours in this game so it's probably about time I wrote a review. I'll try to keep it fairly short.
I love this game because it's relaxing to jump in and pop a few Zed skulls , or blow up a few Fleshpounds with grenades. The harder difficulties are very challenging, which is great for people who want a challenge but I prefer Normal or Hard to relax a little more. Though even in Normal it's quite easy to get cornered by zeds if you're not fully paying attention.
The visual and sound design are some of the best parts of the game. The guns look, sound and feel very cool and realistic to use: each has it's own unique character and pros and cons of use. The graphics, while not cutting edge, are great looking and surprisingly detailed. The music is great if you're into heavy metal and very fitting for the game's theme, and the gunshot noises and headshot noises, etc, are very clear and well done. I think this is part of what makes it so satisfying to play.
The gameplay itself is lots of fun, especially with friends, and quite arcade-y. The downside of being arcadey though is that it gets repetitive after a while, but it's still good fun. I've never had significant lag issues when playing online either, even when connecting to slightly further away servers like Ukraine (I live in the UK). The maps are all well-done and distinct from each other for the most part, so there's quite a bit of variation in that regard. You can be playing in an Arctic base one match, then apocalyptic Paris, and then a tropical jungle on the beach. There are quite a few player-created custom maps too if you get bored of the official ones.
My main gripes with the game are loading times and levelling times, and some issues playing with friends. The game generally takes quite a long time to load, and the levels themselves also do. I don't understand why, because other games don't take as long to load on my PC, and once the game has loaded it runs perfectly smoothly for me. I also own the game on PS4 and it loads much quicker on there.
As I mentioned, it also takes a very long time to level up your classes (perks), which wouldn't be so bad if it weren't for bonuses and upgrades requiring you to level up. If you want to fully level everything up to level 25, you're gonna have to sink some serious time into the game for grinding or just use custom made levelling maps. I have almost 200 hours in the game and I am still only level 25 on two or three of the classes.
Finally I sometimes have issues inviting friends to parties and joining games with them. I'll get weird error messages saying I am not in a game when my friend tries to join, or that my friend is not in a game when I try to join them. I can't figure out why this happens but thankfully it's a fairly rare occurence.
Overall though I would definitely recommend this for the price if you like fast paced arcade-like FPS games, especially if you don't mind the lack of a story in favour of more refined gameplay.

I am a fan of Dave Gilbert's work. I am grateful that he's putting effort into a genre that isn't getting as much attention anymore as it used to in the good old "Monkey Island"-days.
While reviewing this game, it's good to point out that it was originally made as an entry to an adventure game making competition, apparently, so while it has a short length and low production values (slightly raised by the newer version's graphical improvements among other things) it still stands out as a very enjoyable experience.
This is one of those adventure games that would prefer you keep a pen and paper handy, writing down clues and names so that you can check up on them later - feeling like an actual detective, even if for just a short while.
The voice acting is not very good, bordering on annoying with the sound quality being slightly amateurish at times, but I can easily forgive that. You can just turn the voices off if it bothers you too much. Looking at Gilbert's later games, he often mentions that he slowly got the hang of recording more "proper" voice acting and also got a lot of great talent for it.
As I said, the game is short, and I got through it the first time in two hours, hardly ever stuck even for a moment (which I would have if I hadn't kept notes) and I also got to see the rest of the optional endings with an extra fifteen minutes of reloading saves and doing things differently, earning me the rest of the Steam achievements in the progress as well. Being short is not necessarily a bad thing, though. It was a very unique persepective on a story, for one, and it also made me feel like I was doing a good job since the puzzles weren't in any way illogical and made me keep track of the information.
If you are a fan of adventure games, you can easily spare a few hours to play this one through. If you are not a fan of adventure games, you probably didn't bother to read the reviews anyway.

It's very much a sequel to KF1 if you've played that game. I had over 400 hours in 1 but even on the highest difficulties the robotic nature of the gameplay got tedious. When all the wacky dlc items came out and unbalanced everything I lost interest. The limitations of the old Unreal 1.9 engine started hampering the game with bugs and removed features.
2 picks up where those updates ended and includes those expanded ideas into a more seamless game. The zeds have much improved AI and pathing, with animations that add some challenge to actually landing aimed shots. New objective game modes are on the horizon, along with the already included vs. mode. Yes, 2 has lost some of the janky, gritty old-school shooter feel of the original but the game is more cohesive and balanced now. All of my time with it has been since day one of early access and the series has stayed pretty faithful to its core, with major attempts at expanding gameplay and perk synergies. Not all of them have been pleasant, but it's far too hard to judge a final release based on a beta build.
Tripwire has been communicative about development throughout the early access phase and is updating at a faster pace than the quarterly patches of KF1. With much improved mod and mapping support the game should be able to thrive on a larger scale than the previous game. The veterans of KF1 are just a tough lot to please. This game has even more content than the final version of 1 after it had over 5 years of updates.

Shadowverse VS Hearthstone
I love both games to death, here's what I think (I'm new to both games though).
- Shadowverse seem to have faster pace than Heartstone because in SV there are many turn 4-5 cards that come with complex abilities while in Hearthstone you get something simple like 3/6 with taunt as turn 5 minion.
- Hearthstone UI and battlefield background look clean and neat while everything in Shadowverse's screen look so messy.
- Shadowverse animated cards is far more pretty than Hearthstone's animated cards by 10000000 times because animated cards in SV don't have that ugly golden frame like what they have in HS.
- It's much easier to get legendary cards(also epic cards) in Shadowverse, I got 10 legendary cards after playing this game for 3 days, while I got 2 Hearthstone legendary cards after playing the game for 1 and half months.
- Shadowverse give you free 40-50 pack after a short tutorial, and give you free money everyday. You'll get packs faster than Hearthstone. Some events will give you 5 packs multiple times, all you need to do is just logging in to the game
- The daily quest of both games are similar, but I think it's much easier to beat the quests in Hearthstone.
- Shadowverse cards have better arts, Legendary cards frame is very pretty, they looks like those shiny foil cards in real world.
- there are many OP cards in Shadowverse. although they can be countered by some simple way, but there are not enough cards to do that simple task.
- you can replace leaders(your class avatar) in Shadowverse for 500 rupees(equal amount of 500 gold in Hearthstone) it's easy work you can do by grinding for 1-2 days.
In Hearthstone you will have to buy class Avatar with real money, or do some achievement for some class.
-  Shadowverse game menu is very confusing, took me awhile to know where to see daily quests, create decks, or buy card packs.
- both game have arena mode and they work in similar ways. You pay gold to enter arena and win as much as possible to get better prize in the end.
- male characters design in Shadowverse are mostly pretty face teen like cliche fantasy anime protagonist such as Kirito in SAO or male character in Fire Emblem. There are no cool and badass male characters with a lot of tattoo like western games.
- all cards in both games have voice over, you'll be able to choose JP voice in Shadowverse soon.
In conclusion, Hearthstone is more balance, and quite better in gameplay system and pacing. UI looks more clean, golden cards(similar to foil card) are ugly because golden frame. Harder to get epic and legendary cards.
Shadowverse give players many free packs and money, easy to get epic/legendary cards, a bit faster pace. Gameplay is fun but some cards are too complex and overpowered. Art style is great, tons of waifu and sexy characters. Male character are meh, no badass characters at all.

I figured I should write a review on this game before anyone asks for my opinion on it, lol.
I just wanted to say straight off the bat that I absolutely loved Saints Row 3, and that makes this recommendation extremely biased, so people should probably look into the game from other sources besides this one if contemplating on picking this game up.  In my opinion, I think this is a great successor to Saints Row 3.  This game has hooked me to the point where I have put in 23 hours of playtime out of the 72 hours of owning the game, which is ridiculous.  I have not been eating or sleeping much because I just want to keep playing this game!
This game is fantastic if you want something fun to play, where the game does not take itself that seriously, but still has a plot and character development to the point where it is still interesting.  If you did not know beforehand, this game was actually started out as an additional DLC to Saints Row 3, but the developers realized how much they could branch off of this and it ended up turning into a full-length game.  This should not detract anyone from wanting to play this game, but it should be known that this game fully has the Saints Row 3 feel over the game that Saints Row 2 was (which a lot of people complained about when they went from 2 to 3).  Essentially, this game is Saints Row 3 with a lot of changes, which makes the game a blast to play.
One of my complaints thus far are that some of the minigames are back from Saints Row 3, which are some that I really hate (like Fraud), but they do not detract from the game unless you are going for 100% completion.  Another complaint is the currency you need to collect around the map for upgrading your super powers, which is an absurd amount of items for a treasure hunt.  There are over 1000 items to collect from the map, and that is just counting the item just previously mentioned, although they are in plain sight most of the time, which is why there are so many.
One of the things I really like about the game is the level of customization that has opened up.  Like in Saints Row 3, you can customize your character much more than you can in most other character creator games.  The biggest difference in customization is that you can now customize your weapons, although they have set designs, it is still a nice change of pace.  There is a decent amount of selection to choose from, and I have not had any problems on finding a weapon that I enjoy in terms of ascetics.  Another thing that I have loved is the humor of the game, as there have been several segments where I was just dumbfounded at how many references to a plethora of other games can be stuffed into a few seconds of dialogue.  I love all the characters, including the villains, and it is just a generally really fun game to play.
A lot of people have been complaining about the length of the game, but I have not finished the main storyline and I am over 23 hours in.  I know some people that 100% the map within 14 hours, but I have just been exploring and creating whacky scenarios using some of the super powers and my weapons, and have been doing all the optional things before moving on in the story.  I kind of expect I am nearing the end, but I do not regret throwing down the full price for this game, as I have had a lot of fun with it and am expecting to play it again after I beat it whenever they start adding DLC to it!
I would write more, but I do not want to spoil anything, and I want to get back to playing.  Pretty much the bottom line is that if you enjoyed Saints Row 3, you will probably enjoy Saints Row 4 as well.  If you haven’t played a Saints Row game before, if you enjoy third-person action games with a huge variety in customization, with a setting that never takes itself too seriously, then Saints Row 4 is a definite pick up whether it is at full price or discounted.

Toukiden is about as close as Steam users will get to playing Monster Hunter on PC besides God Eater. That isn't a bad thing at all, because Toukiden is a super enjoyable game. Its very easy to learn how to play and extremely challenging to master. The PC port had a ton of issues at launch (most of which have been fixed) and I had a few crashes using Windows 10 but once I switched on Windows 7 Compatbility Mode I haven't had a single issue with performance including crashes, frame drops or anything of the sort. The 30 FPS cap may cut some people off from buying it but after playing Monster Hunter 3 Ultimate, playing at 30 *without* any drops was a nice change. It doesn't excuse them from not putting in the extra effort to make it 60 but personally it just doesn't bother me enough to not pick up the game. Theres very bad keyboard support but to be honest games like this should be played with a controller anyway. All in all, its a pretty good game and a lazy but playable port. Here are the issues with the port:
- Locked to 30 FPS (All versions of the game are 30 FPS so it isn't a downgrade for PC)
- Will crash alot unless you have Windows 7 Compatibility Mode on (Hasn't crashed for me since)
