This is some GROTESQUE mutant murder mayhem, so I don’t know what possessed me to purchase this game. Just kidding! I love torturing myself with scary games. That's why I clicked on the Store Page thumbnail in the first place.
I first tried out Episoide 1 when it was on sale under $5. After deciding it was interesting enough and scoping out the positive reviws, I purchased the entire episode pack for around $20 on sale.
Visuals (art, graphics, character/map design) and sound are both great, as expected from the RE series. They do their job of paralyzing me with dread and occasionally getting me to scream my head off. The maps, although linear, are well designed and hold enough secrets (a.k.a achievement opportunities) in the nooks and crannies.
Gameplay is also quite fun due to the dual layer of POV switching. First, each chapter has a Part A, in which you play as Claire and Moira, and Part B, in which you are Barry and Natalia. This introduces an interesting factor for storyline progression: The player must piece together parts of the story and how the main character’s actions relate to one another. Furthermore, it is interactive in the sense that what you do in Part A might affect exploration opportunities in Part B, and vice versa.
The other function of POV switching is to give the player access to the wider variety of weapons that each character specializes in. This suits different play style preferences (stealth, melee, ranged, and environmental kills), although some situations will force you to adhere to one. For the boss fights, there is always a “creative” option (find and exploit its weakness to do large damage), but there is also the “Resident Evil” option: Empty enough bullets into it, and the thing will die.
Second, you can POV switch to control different characters, i.e. you can choose to lead as Moira or Natalia rather than as Claire or Barry, and you can command them to wait or follow. Activating this mechanic is central to solving puzzles, and it is quite fun. It reminds me of Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons, except everything looks hideously terrifying and is trying to kill you.
Leveling up for skills was relatively easy for me due to the fact that I loooted many gems for BP (skill points), and I replayed a few chapters ifI didn't like the grade that I got after completing them. Scarcity of resources was also not an issue in normal mode--perhaps only in the very beginning when you are quite defenseless.
Controls can be buggy at times. For some reason, I found it significantly more difficult to pull off stealth kills as Claire than as Barry. Moira also let me down many times by failing to blind enemies with her flashlight when I set up what seemed like a opportunity. Not to mention, there was a handful of times in which the enemy pyramid head had seen me while I was crouched behind cover, far away! Lastly, I was forced to restart one time when I was controlling Moira, but Claire jumped next to me, got stuck on the ceiling, touched the floor, and promptly DIED.
The story ended up being somewhat stereotypical of the genre, and of what you expect for the Resident Evil series. It was decent, and the ending culminated in a satisfying boss fight for me. Furthermore, I think the writers did a good job of creating not only likeable characters, but also convincing rapport between them. I enjoyed the writing and found several interactions endearing. Unexpected sassiness also created some unintentionally funny moments for me.

If you try to load your save it will freeze you up again once you walk into the boss room.
Once you do a retry you will need to go in and set the FPS to 30. Enter the boss room. Once the cutscene is done you can move and all is normal. I then went in and set the FPS to variable like I had before, It works fine after that. I dont know what happens if you die again because I won the second try.
Overall I had a lot of fun playing this game.

takes your favorite characters from the Marvel universe and puts them into one fantastic game. The end result is what may be my favorite Lego game to date.
The story of the game is simple; the Marvel superheroes team up to to stop the Marvel villains from taking over the planet. Even if you have no idea who these characters are, you can just hop right in and enjoy yourself. The gameplay is similar to the other
Lego games, meaning that you'll have to complete each level by building Lego pieces and fighting other Lego bad guys. Playing through the main game is fun, especially with a controller and a friend with you.
There are over 130 characters to unlock and play as, ranging from popular Marvel characters like Deadpool and Venom, to more obscure characters such as Squirrel Girl and Captain Britain (you can even unlock Stan Lee later on). In addition to these characters, there are also many alternate outfits for some of the main characters, such as the many different suits of Iron Man.
But what makes this game really great is the New York City hub. When you're not in a mission, you'll be placed in the big map of Manhattan to do whatever you want. Do tasks to unlock characters, undertake sidequests given by civilians, or just fly around as Iron Man: the choice is yours. There are many hidden unlockables, missions, and objectives to do so you should be occupied for quite a while.
You don't need to be a Marvel fan to see that
is a blast to play. Whether you're flying a jet through New York or fighting Red Skull, you will always have fun with this game. It's often on sale for $4.99, so grab it when you have the chance.

Another game from IF. I must say I was a little worried when I got sent back in time. I thought the game "Yeah, you got sent back in time and you gotta do everything over again so you get girl." And boy, was I wrong. I mean the general idea is still revive the Goddess but with the way the story was written, it seems like it's actually sub-plot. That said this is the story of a lazy boy named Fang who prefers slack off in bed or eating Bahus' cooking and he is roped into reviving the Goddess by circumstance (and lots of peer pressure). And that's basically the gist of it.
Onto gameplay. At first glance I thought this game would live up to the brutal difficulty of Re;Birth but it sadly didn't. However, I later realized that the game was designed to be played a certain way. And that is by stabbing furies various place in the world map and making use of what is called "world shaping". Let me give you the quick rundown. World shaping is an ability that fairies use when they are stabbed on the ground. They have a certain radius that are dictated by their level. Let's say that a fairy has a world shaping ability of -10% P.DEF and +10% M.ATK. This means that every creature in that dungeon (including you) have their physical defense decreased by 10% while all magical attacks are 10% stronger. There are various world shaping effects that help increase damage (taken and delivered), boost WP, experience, and even seal off skills which is accessable through Godly Revival provided you have the necessary fairies.
Overall, I really love the amount detail put in the making of this game. Both story and gameplay wise. All characters have these quirks that make them stand out and provide an entertaining experience. There are some sexual innuendos, as well. Only one actually. It's a case of take 'em or leave 'em.
I don't like saying that "If you like anime, you will like this game." I don't like being that person. it's simply unintelligent. You may like anime but you may outright hate turn-based games. But if you do, it will add to your experience.

This is not a music game about quick reaction or visual perception. The music is nice, but doesn't help or motivate. This is a pattern-memorizing game about mastering crappy digital controls. This could have been a lot more fun with analog controls support, like e.g. Soundodger has. At first I thought maybe it was fixed to buttons for moving in order to give nobody a disadvantage, but the high scores seem to be limited to Steam only anyway here, and the game isn't even available on consoles. So I see no reason to not enable mouse controls except to artifically increase the difficulty. And that actually makes it less equal-footing, because even the type of keyboard you have could influence the result. Because I quickly get what's going on on the screen, I know exactly what I'm doing, but the triangle doesn't end up where I want it to go because I might have pressed a button a millisecond too long. Especially in higher difficulties this probably intensifies. And when I do my best to accurately steer the triangle, I'm pushed out of THAT flow because the game has some instances where the triangle hits a line at the edge but it doesn't register. So it expects you do be extremely accurate, but the game isn't.
I don't feel any satisfaction about training my quick perception in this game, because without knowledge of the levels through repetitive game-over and advancing bit by bit, you'd not stand a chance.
I don't consider this skillful game design, because it's damn easy to make a game difficult through 'cheap tricks'. When you hear "This game is difficult", don't confuse it with it being a challenge. Unless you consider surviving torture a challenge and giving you a sense of pride.
That doesn't mean this game doesn't have its place. It's just not at all smart. Mastering controls that are unoptimized for the required purpose isn't that rewarding. Trying for how long you can hold your breath for example is way more rewarding, more useful for real life and comes for free.
Soundodger raises my pulse considerably and makes me be on edge, really boosting the adrenaline. Super Hexagon on the other hand didn't effect me at all that way. It's more about subconsciously rewiring your brain, creating motoric memory. This game trains you to be an excellent Super Hexagon player and nothing else. I bet if they made a similar game with just a different controls behavior, all the masters would suck again.
I won't play this long because I don't want to waste brain space with stuff that is of no otherwise use.
I have to say though, THIS is a game where all its Steam achievements DEFINITELY deserve the name "achievement".

This game could be awesome. But it has two serious problems.
Let's start with the really great sides of Mirror's Edge. The art design is just astonishing. The looks of the city with their different color themes, the asia touch and the fitting music create an interesting futuristic scenario. These components established the same feeling which I had in Deus Ex: HR before. If you played it you will know what I mean.
Also the parcour running is just pure fun. When you are able to chain multiple moves in a fast run you feel SO good! If the game would feature parcour runs only, it would probably one of my favourite games of all time.
the game also is higly frustrating. There are several sequences where you have to fight armed policemen. And it is possibly the most horrible thing I have ever experienced. You will die. You will die so often. And that is not all, it will also feel unfair. You know this feeling when you think you are doing the best the game has to offer and you still die almost randomly? At one point I even thought about quitting completely.
Another con is that the controls are sometimes not precise. If you played the old Tomb Raider games you will remember deaths because you jumped 5 degrees in the wrong direction. Overall the controls are good, don't get me wrong, but I had several moments where I definitely pressed the right button in the right moment and still somehow fell down or the character didn't grab the ledge.
Nevertheless if you are interested in the game you should grab it for this price. The good sides of it are worth experiencing the frustrating ones. In reflection I feel positive about Mirror's Edge. And from my personal point of view everyone who is interested in video games in general should know this title.
You should also use a 360 Controller, the game even supports it.

Stick of Truth was a guilty pleasure. I loved the game but I also love South Park. I can imagine many people who haven't watched South Park being put off by the game since there are so many references to their episode catalog. I can also see many South Park fans not enjoying it if classic style JRPG combat is something they don't enjoy. It's a weird title that is geared for a specific niche but if you aren't familiar with JRPGs or South Park I think there is still plenty to enjoy to give it a shot.
The story is classic South Park starting innocently enough with the boys play-tending a battle between humans and elves with tons of references towards Lord of the Rings and Skyrim. Like many classic South Park episodes events spiral quickly out of control involving aliens, nazi zombies, and a journey up a depraved mans♥♥♥♥♥for the sake of saving the township. It's all surreal and ridiculous but funny to see in action. You'll meet plenty of characters from the show along the way and see the whole town of South Park mapped out for the first time with most locales fully explorable.
Bringing me to the graphics. It's not pushing the envelope of technology but that is what the show is known for. It faithfully recreates the artistic aesthetic down to the construction paper textures of the cutouts for the characters and evironment. Animation is also faithfully reproduced mixing the construction paper style with photoshopped looking real world and and computer effects harking back to the early glory days of the shows initial style as well as their modern animation updates. The movement, the attacks, everything just oozes the South Park style. And just wait until you get to Canada so see exactly how intense the graphics can really get.
Of course we couldn't properly talk about this game without mentioning the combat. It does follow a very traditional turn based japanese RPG style. It's what I grew up with so I of course loved the nostalgia. But for a group of boys play-tending a Lord of the Rings/Skyrim mashup universe it was odd to see that king of combat for the game. It may have been an inside joke but an exceedinly risky one.
Granted the combat was never that difficult and many fights are avoidable if you take advantage of environmental hazards. The combat is very akin to an elaborate rock, paper, scissors metaphor. Just using your basic attack is going to yeild little results really quick. You need to be aware of your oppenents stances and what attacks will be successful against that stance. Once you obtain plenty of bleeding inducing weapons and spells it becomes a moot point. Just get your enemy bleeding then heal and wait them out. Eventually bleeding damage does more per turn then your specials.
I can't recommend this game highly enough, especially if you are a South Park or JRPG fan. Even if you don't like turn based RPGs but like a good raunchy comedy then this game is worth slogging through the combat system. It wasn't laugh out loud hilarious the whole time but I got pleny of good laughs every hour that I played. Get this game and hopefully next time the creators will give us a nice South Park beat em up akin to Castle Crashers.

Step in the shoes of Fang, a lazy young man who, through the miracle workings of destiny, becomes a fencer, charged with gathering furies and removing the seals of the Goddess, who has been at war with the Vile God for centuries, both of which are now sealed away in another world.
Fairy Fencer F is a typical JRPG, that means there’s quite a bit of talk, and a bit of grind. It’s also a console port, and as such, it has some peculiarities.
Fairy Fencer F is basically a turn-based RPG with beautiful anime-styled art. When you’re not dungeon-crawling, you have a view of static maps and Visual Novel styled conversations with other characters. When you are dungeon crawling you get those same anime characters in 3D view. You only see the party leader until you enter a battle, and you can only choose so many of your friends to battle with you.
Battles are turn based, but not static. You can move freely around a predesigned circular area of reach (and sometimes enemies will be outside this area), which gives you a sense of freedom despite the limitation, something move-by-places or only-x-steps type of turn based games don’t give you.
The sound and voices are very nice and very fitting to the whole anime/fantasy theme, and I’m particularly fond of the song used when you use “fairize”; it reminds me lots of the songs in Persona 3 and 4. By the way, did I mention you can choose between English and Japanese voices? Because you totally can. It had my heart right then and there.
Now, I’ll try to explain this as best I can. Basically you play as Fang, a Fencer, that is: a person who can wield Furies, which are weapons that contain fairies that add powers to the weapon/wielder. Your job is to go out and search for more furies - each one you get will grant you a new fairy. You can add these to your own weapon as “resonance” to make it stronger and give you some extra stats. The fairies you’re currently using gain experience along with you and level up. Fairies are also ranked - the rank is used to remove the seals (swords) on the Goddess/God. While the story tells you to remove the Goddesses’ seals, after the tutorial you can choose to remove the Vile God’s seals as well, which is a neat touch! Each seal removed successfully adds different boosts/stats to the fairy used to remove it, which in turn adds it to you if it’s the one you’re using as resonance. Fairies that aren’t currently being used in your weapons can be stabbed as their fury forms on the world map in order to provide various boosts, buffs and debuffs in the nearby dungeons (for instance, earn more exp, or gold, or drop rate… ). Since you can stab more than one fury into the ground, you can get quite a few boosts while on a single dungeon.
You have combos for physical attacks which you can customize, and you can at a fly switch between three different ones while attacking by simply pressing one key instead of another, all comfortably close by. Because you have so many ways to affect stats and boosts, the system ends up being quite flexible and enjoyable to play with.
It’s a very interesting concept and I feel like I don’t do it justice explaining it thus briefly.
Saving is done through specific spots while inside a dungeon, or at any time within the world/city maps. While in the city you get to speak with a lot of characters and take up quests that can give you some prizes and can also be repeated (indefinitely, as it seems). The quests are fairly typical, but quick to get done, and go along with what rank you are. You can also craft some items to help on your journey. There is some romance in this game.
Because this was a console port, the controls at first can be a bit awkward (for instance, you can’t use esc to exit menus, you must use backspace; you can use the mouse too, but it’s really more of a hassle than using only the keyboard); however, once I grew used to them they were actually very sensibly placed and quite comfortable to use. I ended up using just the keyboard all the time.
I do wish the game was free-roaming rather than turn based, and the fights do get a tad repetitive after a while, making the fighting aspect of the game feel a tad like a grind. However, the story is nice and full of funny moments and the characters are cute and extremely likeable, all of them with their own personalities, doubts and insecurities.
The game really makes you want to collect all the fairies and remove the seals to see what will happen, keeping you hooked with the story. It also offers a New Game Plus + mode upon completion, which I always love but haven’t yet reached. Fairy Fencer F is a delightfully long game (with 30+ hours if you’re playing through just the main storyline, and over a 100 if you’re going for completion), but from what I’ve seen so far I’m confident in recommending this game to everyone who is into JRPGs.

Russell Stone is a Jewish Rabbi at a poor synagogue in New York City. He is a devout man with a problem. Membership is way down and he lacks the funds to keep his synagogue open. Things are looking very bleak, and he has grown progressively more cynical and bitter with the passage of time.
Just as he is on the verge of packing it all in, he receives some interesting news. A former member of his congregation has died and left the Rabbi a significant amount of money. A blessing? Or the start of something far more sinister? Can Rabbi Stone just accept the money and move on? His conscience says no. Step into his shoes as he travels all over Manhattan in his attempt to uncover the truth.
Features rabbinical conversation methods, a unique method of fighting, an original score, and three different endings!

Pixelated graphics.  If this bothers you, you should probably be playing something that relies on its graphics, and not a game that relies on content and atmosphere.

If you like rogue-likes, buy this game.  It's worth it.

Risk of rain is a fun game at times but is ruined by inconsistent gameplay and lack of key features. There is no save feature, which is a pain in the nates since one run can take over an hour. Gamepads are hard to set up (esp. on a mac) and most often do not work. There are very few characters and not much variation in enemies, resulting in very repetitive gameplay. Runs are very inconsistent (which is to be somewhat expected in a procedurally generated game) but a good run depends on what items you find in the beginning. Some items are simply necessary for survival but might not be aquired until way late in the game. Risk of Rain looks unique and the gameplay looks enticing, almost like a mario-infused Spelunky shoot-em-up, but it does not feel that way at all. There are so many great platformers on steam and this one simply doesn't impress me. Controls leave something to be desired, while player movement is very slow, making it a chore to get from one side of a level to the next. I have had a little fun with the game, and the idea is promising, but it simply failed to make a lasting impression.
This game was not for me, but it has a large following on steam, so try it if you'd like. I'd at least wait for it to go on sale though.

Looking for a new card game after Hearthstone, Magic Duels and Magic online, i tried Shadowverse.
Starting out in the game you are rewarded with plenty new cards to try out, which is good. I jumped into ranked mode and tried playing other players. I discovered that (at the lowest level of the scale), I was only playing against decks filled with rare and legendary cards. Since i had no cards like these, i obviously had no chance at winning. With 20 years of playing diverse collectible card games, it is my opinion that i can build a decent deck with the cards provided.
The game is is fairly simple in its mechanics. Easy to understand. If you are looking for a more complex game like Magic the Gathering, this is not the game for you. If you like Heartstone but are fed up with Hearthstone's randomness, this might be a game for you.
Pro's:
+ Easy to learn
+ Rewards plenty of cards at the start of the game
+ Logging in daily rewards you with some ingame items.
Con's:
- Probably needs some financial investment to be competitive
- expensive cards overwhelmingly powerful
- animations take too much time if you want to quit a match and start over. (which can't be turned off)

The main issue is that Enemy uknown is that it's out of date... I'm not talking about graphics or the genera of the game. It's out of date because it's already been remade as Xcom: Enemy within, which is package as a DLC.
Enemy unknown is outdone by Enemy within, which is the same game for the most part. Enemy With in fixes all the glitches and bugs and of course the sudden freezes in the game and adds new content.
You can upgrade your soilders gene's, see if they are PSI powers, or take a member of squad and make him into a Mec, which is fun.
Enemy within has a few more set missions as well as fighting a human orgnization called Exalt. The Human's you fight aren't anything to write home about, Generally you can plow right through them, they are more interested in securing a location than actually fighting you at times. Once you fight them once or twice you know to protect the point and they will be more concern to get to that point than trying to fight you. However it's a fun concept.
However the game is the same, the main story line doesn't change and I haven't beaten the game yet, but from what I read, the ending is no different.
Xcom: Enemy within actually comes with with the slingshot DLC, you can give your soilders different colors and new hair cuts, or even other head gear.
The reason I'm giving Xcom: Enemy unknown a thumbs down isn't due to the fact I didn't enjoy my 40 hours of game play, but xcom: Enemy within is better. Between all the add on's and the game not being buggy you get a better experince.
Here is the catch for PC gamers, which latley I been playing more PC games.  To play Xcom: Enemy within you have to buy enemy unknown. Your basically spending another 30 bucks for the same storyline. If you own a console you can go buy Xcom: Enemy within which has everything Enemy unknown has. However I feel a game of this nature is easier to play on the computer. They don't make it clear that DLC is actually just a newer verison of the game. I don't fully understand why you can't just pick up xcom enemy within without having to buy enemy unknown where in the land of consoles you can. I'm not saying it's a rip off, but your pretty much just buying a better less buggy verison of the game.
It prolly doesn't help that I basically played them back to back.
On a side note, in both games a lot of the upgrades come way to late. Such as the imrpoved arch thrower. By the time you can get it, or afford it you pretty much captured everything. The Shiv units even in the first one are dumb. They are even more outdated in the second one because you have mec's. Most of the game you are straved for money, using satlities can be tricky. Once you give a country a satilite they give you money every month, yet you want to hold off on giving out satilties  because once you launch them, and you can only launch them once for each country it lowers the panic and generally saves a country leaving the xcom project.

I'll start by reaffirming what others have said, if you enjoyed Neptunia then you will enjoy this game. I'm almost at the end so I may change some things upon completion but I'll just note how I feel so far.
Story: It's nothing to write home about, the plot twists and the like are really obvious. That being said, just like in Neptunia it is really the characters that make the story enjoyable. The humor is good, and unlike some Rebirth 2, it doesn't really use whole lot of memes. The character interactions are fun and Tsunako is responsible for their designs which is always great in my opinion.
Gameplay: Again, see Neptunia. There can be a lot of grind depending on what you're trying to do but if you just play through you should have no trouble. In fact, the only time I felt there was a difficulty spike was on certain side missions when attempting to get extra furies. You have your level ups, increasing the strength of each character but beyond that there is the Weapon Points system, which allows you to choose extra stat bonuses as well as customize progression through choices in combo moves, as well as extending both combos and weapon range. The fury system serves the duel purpose of prividing both character boosts through stat upgrades as well as allowing you to change each area in subtle but noticable ways. You could increase both the weapons points gained while at the same time doubling the damage BOTH you and your enemies put out. Depending on how you use them, you can speed up some of the grind in game.
Controls: I mainly played with an Xbox 360 controller. Despite this the controls were very repsonsive. I only add this because I recently went through the PS3 version of Neptunia Victory and found the controls to be somehat lagging in comparison. I breifly used KB+M to get a feel in that regard, and for the short time I used them if felt just as good.
Music: Enjoyable, like most jrpg's if you like em the music is usually good, and Compile Heart always does well in that regard.
If you typically enjoy a lot of the jrpg's that have been coming out lately, you'll no doubt find this a charming and enjoyable game. I've still yet to beat it so I can't say much for replay value, but judging from what I've played it doesn't seem like there could be much, at least until more of the DLC is released. It's worth the time and for those still on the fence, if you catch it on sale like I did, it is more than worth the money. Between the characters, story, and gameplay, you'll find a very comfy rpg.

I don't know how to define this game. A First-person action where your main purpose is to run. That's right, run! One of this game's strenghts is, among all and in my opinion, its freshness! But let's talk more in details about the game...
The plot is based on a city (which apparently hasn't got a name) where information is constantly controlled and supervised (reminded me of "1984", for those who know the book!). This kind of society brought to the birth of the so-called "runners", who are rebels who do stunts taking advantage of the environment between buildings, pipes and platforms; are deliver information even at the cost of their lives. Our protagonist is the runner Faith Connor. The story begins when Faith's sister, Kate, is trapped and subsequently indicted for the murder of a politician. This will push Faith, to break the boundary of the city in which the rebels are ''crossing in the mirror's edge'' (reference needed). From here we will investigate to try to exonerate her sister.
The gameplay is very hectic, which makes everything much more exciting and unfortunately short-lived given that, I finished it in a few hours. First of all I'd advice EVERYONE, even the expert players, to complete the tutorial in order to understand the game mechanics, because as I said it's a different game compared to the others! However a lot of It is about observing the landscape in order to notice any path you can take to move forward (it isn't always easy to identify them, even though they are highlighted in red, especially if you are running). In case there are policemen nearby, you can use the attack to beat 'em up, to steal their guns and to quickly shoot the rest of 'em (we still available a few bullets, also if we had taken the charge weapon). Still you'd better avoid all of that, 'cause it slows down the run and makes you more vulnerable (if they shoot you even just three or four times you can easly die).
The characters are poorly characterized, little is told about Faith. The graphics are very pretty and fits in the context in my opinion!
In conclusion I think it's a game that everyone should try. After that you can like It or dislike It, but as It's a different kind of game-experience that still allows the player having fun!
Non so bene come definirlo questo gioco. Un gioco d'azione, in prima persona, dove lo scopo principale è di correre. Esatto, correre! Uno dei punti di forza di questo gioco è proprio questo, a parer mio, la novità! Ma parliamo più nello specifico del gioco..
La trama parla di una città (senza un apparente nome) dove le informazioni sono costantemente controllate e vigilate (mi ha ricordato molto 1984, per chi conoscesse il libro!). A questa legge si ribellano i cosiddetti ''runners'', ragazzi che correndo e facendo acrobazione tra palazzi, tubi e pedane trasportano informazioni anche a costo della loro vita. La nostra protagonista è la runner Faith Connor. La storia inizia quando la sorella di Faith, Kate, viene incastrata e successivamente incriminata per un omicidio di un politico. Questo spingerà Faith, ad infrangere il confine della città a cui tanto si ribella ''varcando il bordo dello specchio'' (citazione necessaria) in inglese appunto Mirror's Edge. Da qui la vedremo indagare per cercare di scagionare la sorella.
Il gameplay è molto frenetico, il che rende tutto molto più eccitante e purtroppo poco longevo dato che, almeno io, l'ho finito in poche ore. Inizialmente consiglio a TUTTI, anche ai più esperti, di fare il tutorial, per capire bene le meccaniche di gioco, perché come ho già detto è un gioco diverso dagli altri! Comunque il tutto sta nell'osservare bene il paesaggio per notare eventuali percorsi da poter fare per andare avanti (non è sempre facile individuarli, nonostante siano evidenziati in rosso, specie se si sta correndo). Nel caso ci siano poliziotti vicini, inoltre, è possibile usare l'attacco riavvicinato sia per stenderli sia per rubare la pistola e far fuori velocemente il resto della polizia (abbiamo comunque disponibili pochi proiettili, anche l'avessimo presa carica l'arma). L'arma comunque è meglio evitarla, dato che rallenta la corsa e ci rende più vulnerabili (non abbiamo molta vita, se ci sparano anche 3-4 colpi in pochi secondi siamo morti).
I personaggi sono poco caratterizzati, viene dopo poco anche di Faith. La grafica è molto carina ed adatta al contesto a parer mio!
Concludendo secondo me è un gioco che tutti dovrebbero provare, poi può piacere e non piacere, ma è un gioco diverso che comunque può divertire, quindi lo consiglio!

My death count as of stopping this game was at 299, most of these deaths involving the many ways you can die on spikes.  This game lured me in with it's art style, retro charm, and solid music.  It's a great concept, a very polished attempt to recapture Simon's Quest.  And once you get over the initial learning curve--and it's a doozy--and actually start getting weapons and spells, the game's fun.
Then it throws off the disguise and before you know it, you're knee deep in merciless precision platforming.  I tried my best to move on past the nightmarish, pointy labyrinth of the Torture Chamber.  But when an unseen ceiling spike fells on me for the umpteenth time after getting the already difficult to find book pages which then forces me to get it AGAIN, I start to realize I'm not having fun.  I was hoping for a fun action-adventure game, which I almost got.  However, in the end I got a game where the HP doesn't make anything in the face of deadly triangles.
If you're a fan of frustration, and raising your blood-pressure, go for it.  As for me, I think I'll move on.  There are just aren't enough boss hearts.  At least the music and art were stellar.

The game's story is a pretty solid murder mystery, and reminds me heavily of the Ace Attorney investigations. You collect clues to progress, and can combine them in a sort of logic system.
But, throughout the entire game, you'll only actually recieve one inventory item, and collect 4 total clues.
The Shivah's length absolutely is it's own worse enemy. While there's no filler or downtime to chug through, the game can easily be completed in less than an hour if you know what you're doing.
The only real length to the game would be the trial and error combat sections. You fight two different people in the game, and both of them can only be beaten with an exact choice of words.
Over all, the game wasn't bad, just extremely short. You don't really have enough time with Rabbi Stone to really resonate with him, which is a shame, because the premise at the start seemed really interesting.

I don't know but I keep coming back to this game and after playing it tonight again I decided to do a review of it.
Well I first came into contact after watching a Youtube recommending it, and I thought "why not" and bought it, and I haven't since regretted it.

I want to talk about the mechanics of this game that makes it pretty unique. You play a rogue lite 2d sidescroller  with one of many different  and interesting characters. Even the standard Commado soldier character you start with feels really good he is still one of my favorite dudes together with acrid (a disease riddled seamonster). All the characters starts with four different abilities and the hav very different playstyles, so you can play characters that specializes in long range for example the sniper with his insanely long range and precision tactics or you can jump around like a crazy person with a pickaxe with another character.  Also you pick up different powerups during the level and you often have a ridiculous amount of  stuff like most other  "rogue lites" which is always fun in my eyes.

Also the implemented a cool type of modifier that makes the enemies tougher the longer your run is. So it is in most cases worth to stick around in a level to get all stuff because if you keep doing that the first enemies on the next level will be so strong that they will immediately kick your♥♥♥♥♥so fast that you will have no idea what just happened.
I will also talk a little bit about the level design that is in most cases levels that are pre made but have some different random elements as spawn and portals that will activate the next level.Some issues I have to inform you about is that there is some levels that if you get them in a run you will mostly loose because that they are so much harder than the rest which feels pretty sad when you think about how good most maps are.

To summarize this review I Can recommend this game to people  that loves "rogue lite" games and people that need to just occupy their hands and mind for some time when there are listening to some great music or the fantastic soundtrack of this game.

This game is made by Techland, the devs of the popular game, Dead Island. But don't expect to find the humor from Dead Island. This game takes itself much more seriously. It also borrows from a lot of other games. This review will be split into three categories:
Graphics,
Gameplay,
And last but not least, (well maybe for this game) The Story.
Graphics:
This game is beautiful. It has lush trees and plants, and you can notice how crisp and realistic the buildings look. Humans, although recycled, look very good as well. But there are (at least in my experience) lots of moments with jumpy frame rate. For example, if you have particularly high graphics settings, and this even happens for me with a GeForce GTX 770 GPU, you'll have 60fps one minute on the rooftops, and 30 the next during cutscenes and moments when you're running through forests or seeing way too many entities on screen at once. The film grain in this game is highly noticable for the eagle-eyed. Turn this off. If you had this game at release, you know how horrible the film grain looks. Thankfully, they updated the game so you can turn this off. You can tweak antialiasing and how good things like models and buildings look. The only thing that looks really ugly and is impossible to change, are the electricity lines. You know, the lines that droop from pole to pole. They'll always be ugly regardless of your settings. Unless the make an update for the game, hint hint. Oh, and also, the character models for the player/ main protagonist look emotionless and the animations are really, really awkward. Play multiplayer and you'll see it. Overall, I'd give the graphics part of this game a 9/10, a 10/10 would be there if the player models and electricity lines weren't so awkward.
Gameplay:
This aspect of the game is probably its best, what with parkour and the combat system. In the beginning of the game, you start out scavenging a lot and finding zombies very difficult to defeat. Also, the amount of hits you can take and give are really punishing in the beginning. Later, this changes drastically. You'll be OHKOing just about anything you see. For the parkour aspect, this is amazing. Probably one of the best games that implement parkour, next to titles like Mirror's Edge. And if your game's parkour can compare to Mirror's Edge's parkour, that's something to brag about. In the beginning, you won't be able to sprint for a particularly long amount of time and you'll be climbing very slowly. But later, you can sprint for an unlimited amount of time and you can vault over enemies. You can also climb very fast and do challenges that put your skill to the test. There is a Survivor rank in this as well where you'll use your backpack more effevtively and repair weapons without using up it's durability for repairs. You'll also learn how to craft double the items you'd normally make with the normal amount of items needed. Also, to add to the parkour, you'll get a grappling hook later in the game. You can make your weapons even do more damage. The possibilities are endless. Remember when I said that this game borrows heavily from other games? Well, here is where I'll explain it. The freerunning borrows heavily from Mirror's Edge, the lockpicking is the exact same as Skyrim's lockpicking and the looting system borrows heavily from the Borderlands series. Defeating enemies is SO awesome. It's very satisfying when you hear your weapon hit them and the amount of damage it'll make. I found it especially satisfying when you kill an enemy by cutting their heads clean off, or using one of the more advanced takedowns later in the game. The gameplay here is SO rich, the explorations and secrets here are endless. If you're here for more than the story, you will not be dissapointed. For me, the gameplay deserves a 9/10. The only thing holding this back that I didn't get to explain are very minor glitches that you may find only one of in your first playthrough. Last, and probably the least,
The Story:
This game has probably the most dissapointing story out of any game I've played over the past year. (well, maybe not THE most dissapointing, but still) The story here hits almost every movie cliche. There are even videos on YouTube that picks on how cliche this story is. The characters here are not that in-depth. Throughout the game, I found myself forgetting the names of most of the key characters. The characters in this game really only show their badass moments during their untimely death. Also, prepare to become Harran's errand boy. In this game, you play Kyle Crane, a man that works for an operation called the GRE. Their focus is to get back a highly confidential file from a GRE rouge named Kadir. And that's pretty much it. You find this guy, experience a bunch of cliches, get the file, and get out. Not to mention the main character is a huge ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. He sarcastically says "You must be fun at parties" after a guy tells him about a terrible ordeal that nobody should have to go through. The story here is average at best and the hero in this is some guy that says a bunch of one-liners at the worst moments. Overall, this story deserves a 5/10.
And that's my review of Dying light. In my opinion, the overall game deserves a 7/10 because of it's horrible story but is held up because of how good the gameplay and graphics are. But I won't recommend this game for you if you like the story. Don't buy this if you wanted a good story. But if you came for gameplay and graphics like I did, definitely buy this. If you're somewhat minimalistic like me, go ahead and give this a try.

Dota 2 is one of my favorite games of all times. When this documentary was announced and I watched the trailer for the first time I got so hyped. Now it's finally here and just like everything else Valve does it turns into gold.
This documentary is about 3 professional e-sport gamers and their journey to "The International", the world tournament in Dota 2 . They are from different countries and compete for different teams for the prize pool of 1 million dollar.
We get to see a detailed backstory, hear interviews with their family members and see how the pro-teams work and communicate. If that isn't enough for you the documentary also comes with "behind the scenes" and "making of the movie" that everyone can watch and even some achievements.
The most important part is how they managed too explain Dota 2's mechanics in a good way that everyone can understand. Even the players who haven't played at all or very little will get a hang of it. This documentary is not some cheap advertising for the game as some people thought, its actually not that much about the game, it's about the pro-players and their lives.
This is really good for being absolutely free. I would strongly recommend it to fans and players of Dota 2 but also to people interested in learning the game and for others that simply like e-sport and want to know more about it!

Assuming they proceed with making one, I'd hope the developer polishes some of the game-play, adds way more weapon modding options and ends the story with an actual conclusion.

I've been following Techland since around 2008ish when they first released footage on youtube about their zombies and the tech involving decay and such. Then silence before Dead Island got released. Of course I had high hopes for it, but it fell short of the promises of the earlier video.
Dying Light has more visual fidelity than Dead Island, much more detail and better lighting. In fact, the lighting has to be on of the best at the moment. From the use of molotovs, to the subtle spark of an electric based weapon; the lights do effect the world. The sunlight does compliment the environments, from midday to sunsets.
What is exceptional is techlands approach to night. Most open world games leave the light on with subtle hue of blue to emulate moonlight; but most of the time it falls short and has world just as illuminated as it were in sunlight. Now this is no problem to games that use corridors. However Dying Light is an open world game, and does not fall victim to the former. In Dying Light, when the sun sets, night becomes night; it does become dark, nearly pitch black. It makes flashlights invaluable in this game despite it attracting the now more aggressive zombies. At night however, the player really gets to see how substantial lighting is done in the game. Fire barrels glow in the distant, and molotovs thrown do illuminate while the fire is still going, often times illuminting the area more than the flashlight.
Now the gameplay is much more refined than dead island. Melee is predominant, whilst firearms are not uncommon. They are rare in the beginning and become uncommon towards half way through the game. Each item has a rarity, but rarity alludes to how many times it can be repaired before it breaks. Don't fall in love with on weapon as it probably would not last you through out the game. Crafting is simple, adding elemental modifications to a weapon, and having minor upgrades. There is loot to be found everywhere, and most items are useful.
Parkour...free running, or what ever you call it
is very intuitive, it does get you places, and get you off the streets. It is a bit to get used to, but once you do, you can outrun and get to safety faster. Sometimes the flight in "fight or flight" becomes more satisfying.
Zombies. Well they are zombies as you would know them, and they get aggresive at night. There are different species such as the boomer, witch, ta....wait thats Left 4 Dead...well all the special zombies are akin to the specials in left 4 dead. Zombies react to sound and light. But zombies are half of what you should be worried about, there are bandits as well. Zombies do take a good chunk of your health each time, but you are never without healthpacks and you do not get punished if you die.
Multiplayer, the zombie mode has you invading peoples game and leveling up your skills. Simple, like left 4 dead, and the co-op is the same thing. Drop in, help a friend out, and drop out. You probably won't be invading a lot of people because you can opt out for online.

I don't know how to define this game. A First-person action where your main purpose is to run. That's right, run! One of this game's strenghts is, among all and in my opinion, its freshness! But let's talk more in details about the game...
The plot is based on a city (which apparently hasn't got a name) where information is constantly controlled and supervised (reminded me of "1984", for those who know the book!). This kind of society brought to the birth of the so-called "runners", who are rebels who do stunts taking advantage of the environment between buildings, pipes and platforms; are deliver information even at the cost of their lives. Our protagonist is the runner Faith Connor. The story begins when Faith's sister, Kate, is trapped and subsequently indicted for the murder of a politician. This will push Faith, to break the boundary of the city in which the rebels are ''crossing in the mirror's edge'' (reference needed). From here we will investigate to try to exonerate her sister.
The gameplay is very hectic, which makes everything much more exciting and unfortunately short-lived given that, I finished it in a few hours. First of all I'd advice EVERYONE, even the expert players, to complete the tutorial in order to understand the game mechanics, because as I said it's a different game compared to the others! However a lot of It is about observing the landscape in order to notice any path you can take to move forward (it isn't always easy to identify them, even though they are highlighted in red, especially if you are running). In case there are policemen nearby, you can use the attack to beat 'em up, to steal their guns and to quickly shoot the rest of 'em (we still available a few bullets, also if we had taken the charge weapon). Still you'd better avoid all of that, 'cause it slows down the run and makes you more vulnerable (if they shoot you even just three or four times you can easly die).
The characters are poorly characterized, little is told about Faith. The graphics are very pretty and fits in the context in my opinion!
In conclusion I think it's a game that everyone should try. After that you can like It or dislike It, but as It's a different kind of game-experience that still allows the player having fun!
Non so bene come definirlo questo gioco. Un gioco d'azione, in prima persona, dove lo scopo principale è di correre. Esatto, correre! Uno dei punti di forza di questo gioco è proprio questo, a parer mio, la novità! Ma parliamo più nello specifico del gioco..
La trama parla di una città (senza un apparente nome) dove le informazioni sono costantemente controllate e vigilate (mi ha ricordato molto 1984, per chi conoscesse il libro!). A questa legge si ribellano i cosiddetti ''runners'', ragazzi che correndo e facendo acrobazione tra palazzi, tubi e pedane trasportano informazioni anche a costo della loro vita. La nostra protagonista è la runner Faith Connor. La storia inizia quando la sorella di Faith, Kate, viene incastrata e successivamente incriminata per un omicidio di un politico. Questo spingerà Faith, ad infrangere il confine della città a cui tanto si ribella ''varcando il bordo dello specchio'' (citazione necessaria) in inglese appunto Mirror's Edge. Da qui la vedremo indagare per cercare di scagionare la sorella.
Il gameplay è molto frenetico, il che rende tutto molto più eccitante e purtroppo poco longevo dato che, almeno io, l'ho finito in poche ore. Inizialmente consiglio a TUTTI, anche ai più esperti, di fare il tutorial, per capire bene le meccaniche di gioco, perché come ho già detto è un gioco diverso dagli altri! Comunque il tutto sta nell'osservare bene il paesaggio per notare eventuali percorsi da poter fare per andare avanti (non è sempre facile individuarli, nonostante siano evidenziati in rosso, specie se si sta correndo). Nel caso ci siano poliziotti vicini, inoltre, è possibile usare l'attacco riavvicinato sia per stenderli sia per rubare la pistola e far fuori velocemente il resto della polizia (abbiamo comunque disponibili pochi proiettili, anche l'avessimo presa carica l'arma). L'arma comunque è meglio evitarla, dato che rallenta la corsa e ci rende più vulnerabili (non abbiamo molta vita, se ci sparano anche 3-4 colpi in pochi secondi siamo morti).
I personaggi sono poco caratterizzati, viene dopo poco anche di Faith. La grafica è molto carina ed adatta al contesto a parer mio!
Concludendo secondo me è un gioco che tutti dovrebbero provare, poi può piacere e non piacere, ma è un gioco diverso che comunque può divertire, quindi lo consiglio!

So, first off. This game is still kinda buggy and crashes a bit too often. Not enough to completley ruin the experience, but it can be very frustrating. These two issues don't destroy the game but they do dampen one's enjoyment. Now onto the pros and cons of the actual game.
Graphics: Pretty good and the constant rain really helps to bring a good sense of atmosphere...even if it hardly ever seems to stop. The character models are all spot on and I thought the hair for the characters were up to standard. Explosions look good and textures only flaked out on me rarely. Overall, decent to pretty good.
Gameplay: Still fun though it does feel a little like you've been here before on the fist fighting with not much new brought to the table. Stealth is still a satisfying pursuit as it should be in a batman game but there is a new mechanic where if you build enough fear in the thugs you are facing you can take out up to 3 of them at once. Might ruin the stealth for some. The batmobile is the biggest addition to the gameplay and if you don't like well...that's half the game right there. You spend a ridiculous amount of time driving around in the bat mobile, either battling drones, using it for boss battles, or attempting to figure out how the riddler got all the resources needed for all the puzzles he set up for you that require the bat mobile. Not that all of that isn't fun, but it does get bit old. Still gameplay is pretty solid.
Open world: The world is vast with a lot of side missions to do but the fact that Gotham was evacuated at the beginning of the game leaves the places feeling a tad empty or more like a giant version of Arkham City than Gotham City. Missed opportunity. The side missions vary in how fun they are as you go up against some of Batman's classic villians while also duking it out with some of his lesser known ones.  Overall, a lot of content but maybe a little to much.
Story: All over the place in quality, as the reveal of the Arkham Knight is obvious if you know anything about Batman and the best part of the entire story is...a spoiler. Let's just say, it upstages everything and kinda makes you wish you were dealing with it more than the rest of the story. There are some good moments throughout but there are some annoying♥♥♥♥♥pulls that cheapen prior moments. Overall, the story has its moments but has too many drone battles and can be a tad weak. Decent overall.
Overall: I recommend this game, but be aware its not as good as Asylum or City.

A nice mix of Far Cry 3 and Left 4 Dead 2, with a hint of Fallout 3. If you liked any of those a significant amount, and you have the desire to kill zombies, this game will satisfy you.
Pros:
-It's really fun killing stuff.
-Lots of weapons and throwables to give you options in your arsenal.
-Open world exploration of a well crafted landscape. (For those who think the map is on the small side, it isn't all you get)
-Lots of interiors to explore in the world.
-The freerunning works well and is super fun.
-Big skill trees to unlock perks and skills from as you progress (running, fighting, surviving)
Cons:
-Lots of random swimming parts in missions. I've never liked those.
-Lots of cutscenes that are long enough that you'll want to skip them.
-Occasionally you'll fail to grab a ledge or something and fall to your death. It's rare, but frustrating.
-There is no map (apart from the minimap) while you're indoors. What the hell?
-The story is a tornado of cliches, which is kind of funny so it isn't all that bad.
-Not a huge selection of guns, and they aren't really necessary unless you're up against big zombies or humans with guns. Far Cry 3 had more precise gunplay, but this is still pretty good.
-Some missions drag on way too long.
-During missions, sometimes your inventory is removed and that can be extremely annoying.
-Lots of random crashes. Like, several daily random crashes. It's really irritating.
-When you go underwater, or water drips on your face, the droplets make your vision extremely blurry and this effect lasts waaay too long. It gets very annoying during missions because there's a surprisingly large amount of travel through sewers.
-(Possible spoilers) During one of the last missions (story at 92%), you're required to travel from the 2nd town back to the 1st. Rather than prompting you to fast travel there, it directs you to yet another sewer system to run through. On top of that, there are multiple pathways, some of which can take you all the way back to where you started. Since there's no map indoors, good luck finding your way.
Even though my cons list is longer than my pros list, I still think that this game overall is a very enjoyable experience. I expect to get at least 60 hours of it.

I have completed the main storyline, 3 of the side missions and about 10-20% each of the other side missions.
Batman Arkham Knight is the final game of the Arkham series. If you've played the other Arkham games, you know what to expect here - you are Batman, you fight the bad guys using the fluid combat system, you take bad guys out one by one in the stealth missions, all with some new bat gadgets to play with as well as the ones you've used in the past. But you get to play with one big new toy - the Batmobile!
.
What a shame that the game got the shoddy PC release that it did, because this truly is a magnificent game. The technical achievements behind this game simply amazed me throughout. Throughout the game I continually questioned myself, "Is this really the best one of the series?", and for the most I thought it was. But it has flaws, most of which became apparent near the end, which for me makes it fall short of being the best of the series.
The great stuff - even on my 760, it is a great looking game. The combat system I would say is my favourite of the series, lots of variety, and the environment takedowns were super cool. Also,
. The stealth missions were a lot of fun, with the new gadgets adding new dynamics. Needless to say, driving the Batmobile around a post apocalyptic Gotham City gave me lots of joy, and some of the puzzles were very cleverly done. The general mood and atmosphere are perfect.
Two gripes with the game - while getting from A to B in the Batmobile during the game is very cool, and some of the Batmobile missions are equally as fun, it became apparent to me near the end of the game that you in fact perhaps spend a bit too much time in the Batmobile. The Batmobile combat scenes also started to become a little tiresome and even overwhelming at times. My second gripe is the story. I felt during the game that the story was developing nicely and was becoming one of the best. But, and again especially near the end, I felt the story dragged a bit. A couple of scenes were unnecessary, and certain elements of the story didn't do much for me.

I think of Koei-Tecmo as a kind of two headed ogre, the ungainly fusion of two wholly separate giants I remember roaming the land of my memories of youth. On one hand, Tecmo is known for over-the-top, unforgivingly fast paced games like the Ninja Gaiden series and cheesecake/beefcake heavy fighting franchise Dead or Alive, while Koei is best known as a publisher of borderline educational and contemplative "historic simulation" strategy games, such as Nobunaga's Ambition, with some forays into action like the Samurai Warriors series.
When the planets align just right and both heads on that ogre manage fuse their respective interests juuuust right, you might just end up with a game like Toukiden.
To spite being accused of, "just being a clone of Monster Hunter," Toukiden has a number of strong differences, both cosmetic and functional. The combat is *far* more straight-forward, centering around direct action sequences and easier to approach equipment and movement sets. This is probably the influence of the Tecmo head of the ogre. From the Koei head, however, we have a setting and visual motif that are influenced by classical Japanese mythology and history.
The end result is a system familiar to players of Capcom's Monster Hunter games, but wholly different in many key respects. Gone is the need to stop partway into key battles to resharpen weapons and chow down a hotdog to avoid exhastion, along with the cumbersone inventory management system. Still here, however, are the fights including foes of massive scale, the limb-damaging and severing mechanic, and the collection of specified enemy part drops to manufacture weapons and armor.
Koei's head of the ogre did have one more interesting word on the matter. Toukiden employs significant historical and mythological figures as equippable "Mitama," sort of a guardian spirit, which change the support spells and buffs that the player has. Each of Toukiden's playable zones are based on one or more specific era or "Age," in Japan's history, and hosts notable Mitama from the corresponding ages. The character designs also do that strange Koei-Tecmo thing, where they just barely split the difference between modern and classical fashion. Not many women showing off tons of cleavage, though, as one might expect.
The bottom line is that, somehow, all of this comes together and *works.* And it works surprisingly well. Some hardened Monster Hunter players will definitely complain that Toukiden lacks gameplay-complicating features like hunger and weapon degradation, but I feel as though the game is better without such distractions. The two-heade ogre certainly thinks so.

A great game that stands tall with other games of its kind. The whole game is set in a version of feudal Japan whose timeline has been distorted and land twisted up by the Oni, the demons of Japanese folklore. Though many will call Toukiden a Monster Hunter *clone*, it feels more apt to call it a Monster Hunting *game*. It's very different from Monster Hunter and in a good way.
+ Mitamas = Spirits of historical figures of feudal Japan. Load them into your weapons. Get stat boosts/special abiulities. Using Mitamas to create your own unique loadout is gratifying. Bonuses for using Mitamas historically related to one another. Incentive to play around with different combinations. TONS of bonus effects.
+ Gathering items to create consumables has been replaced by stock powers that do the same things as Potions, Antidotes, Cool Drinks, etc. and then some! Your abilities change depending on the type of Mitama you have equipped. Less prep work, more demon fighting.
+ Great weapon choices and fighting styles. Each weapon plays a little differently than the other. Skill plays a moderate factor in the combat; the better you know how to use your weapon, the better slayer you are.
- (I'm coming off of MH4U's almost-G-Rank HR stuff) Monster AI is a little too dumb in the beginning, and by the beginning I mean SEVERAL hours. Probably only highlighted by the fact that teammate AI in the single player campaign is VERY good. Monster AI does get smarter at a much faster rate than the teammate AI, so it balances out, but be prepared for some lazy demons early on.
- The PC Port comes at a rocky recommendation as the multiplayer apparently has issues, but if you're still interested in a strong solo Monster Hunting experience this is definitely something you should give a go.

The process of slaying a large Oni starts with destroying its body parts (legs, tails, etc.), then purifying those parts (otherwise the Oni regenerates it) then attacking the Oni true form (transparent, blue or purple). Oni's behavior changes during battle.
AI companions are adequate and helpful. Chapters and Phases are similar, but the former is Offline Story mode, while the latter is Online mode.
Graphics, sound (warning, there's no English VA) and controls (customizable key bindings) are fine.

First off, let me say this; I'm a filthy casual who can't even get to world 4-4 in the classic super mario bros!
That being said, I was far more stubborn in this game than any other game I've played, why, bragging rights. I'm proud to be one of the 9.4% of players around the world who actually 100%-ed the game.
This game does a very good job at being 'Nintendo hard' with modern conventions, however what it doesn't do a very good job at is letting you know where you could get stuck in places if you advance and save at that the next checkpoint.
There is one thing to keep in mind, most of this game was made by one man, in his freetime making with artistic help from a couple of other people. As a budding indie developer myself (I'm working on a humble little RPG that's my idea of what Final Fantasy The Sacred Stones was SUPPOSED to be) I gotta hand it to Matt Kap, he's done some amazing work.
Difficulty wise I would put this game somewhere between NES/SNES era megaman games and Super meat boy, that being said, there's an area called 'torture chambers' in this game. I'm just going to let that sink in a moment.
What's great about this game (and what some people seem to miss) isn't that it's classic 8 bit platforming with a lot of modern ideas, it's that the backtracking everyone's complaining about isn't 'forced' on you.
Think about how a metroid or similarly structured game allows you to reach an area and find out that in order to progress the story you must go back to x area and gain x item to defeat x boss.
This game is the exact opposite of that, it's more like Link's Awakening, with much, much more freedom in what to do first, once you get the Wing boots (your double  jump) the whole world is a clam, now go find your pearl.
The best part of the game is also the most frustrating part, getting 100% means going to hell and back, having a beer, and doing it over again, until you get the prize you seek. This isn't what makes it good, what makes it good is unlike other 'ZMG hard as balls' platformer ( Super Meat Boy, I wanna be the guy, etc) every mistake feels like it was legitimately your fault. The developer took great care in making the platforming challenging, but not unfair or impossible. If you're dying a lot to one thing, take a deep breath, go after something else; and come back once you've gotten better at the game. The frustrating part is that even after you complete whatever platforming challenge you faced to get your prize, you still have to go all the way back to the nearest save point, which is sometimes five or more screens away with a multitude of those beloved 1 hit kill spikes of doom littered about.
If you're super into looking deep into every nook and cranny of a world, you'll enjoy this game. If you're not into that, well, it's only $6 man, give the indie developers some love!
Also, if you love 8 bit music, you will enjoy this game.
Note: If you are going to go for 100% you may encounter a 99% glitch even if you do get the achievement of Lvl 2 Treasure Hunter.(Finding all items) You can go to this website:
drag your save files (found in the filepath mentioned on the website) to the box, and download what files it creates to replace the original. Until Mat Kap fixes this bug, unfortunately this is the only option at the moment.

Don't let the start of this game fool you, Castle in the Darkness is a strict game with precision platforming elements. While the graphics are a love letter to 8-bit NES games, like Castlevania and 8 Eyes, the gameplay itself soon becomes an experience in perfectly jumping through spike floors and platforms, attempting to survive from save point to save point.
There's a big exploration and collection aspect to the game as well, with a variety of items and spells that one has to travel off the beaten path to find. Playing through on New Game + I was surprised about how much time I actually spent investigating the side paths and trying to find all the possible items. There's a good amount of secrets to be discovered as well.
The game is a little buggy. Entering a door when wind is blowing you away from it can result in a soft lock, the hitbox on some floor spikes can hit or miss you from odd angles, trying to jump at the very edge of a platform can result in the weaker double jump instead after you get that upgrade. NG+ gives you a fast attacking weapon that, if you wear with certain armor, won't attack if the projectiles from the armor are still on the screen. I got a hard lock once, but couldn't reproduce it.
Despite these issues, the game was a blast to play. Even though it dips into being a masacore game later on, it definitely has a better Metroid-esque design than most games labelled as "Metroidvania."

I have to admit I know next to nothing about the original Shadowrun, but this game was good enough to intrigue me about the setting. It really harkens back to the games of yore - turn-based tactical gameplay (refreshingly enjoyable), all-text and no-audio dialogue (IMHO, no voice acting is much better than bad voice acting), and somewhat arcane levelling and inventory management systems. Surprisingly, the writing is good, and dripping in flavor. The plot was ok, but my eyeballs rolled out of their sockets in the last quarter of the game (Spirit bugs? Seriously?). One of the weaknesses of the game, I think, is the hiring of character-less mercenaries to fill out your crew - come on, there are a number of interesting side characters I've met, why can't they join my crew instead of these people I don't care about? Also, while running around in the Matrix was cool at first, after a while the novelty wore off and it became a grind - I'm glad I went with my charismatic elven rigger/decker instead of the decker I first thought of rolling with - the times when decking had a true impact were just too few. In the end, it's worth it for the setting - looking forward to exploring more of this world in the future.

Castle in the Darkness is one of those games that some people will love, a game clearly inspired by Zelda could be appreciated as a throwback to fairly hard platforming. Other people simply won’t have the patience that you need when you’re playing this game, especially if you haven’t played many platformers. This is your typical new Mario platformer. This is almost a pixelated 2-d version of dark souls.  Clearly my nearing of 600 deaths will show you that I was not prepared in many ways for this game. This however doesn’t mean it’s a terrible game.
The game starts you off with a fairly plain story. The king of the land has fallen ill, and in his weakened state monsters attack the kingdom. All the castle guards are defeated besides you! So you go off on a journey through the kingdom to save the princess and the king. Of course if you’re playing this game it isn’t for the story so it’s good enough to get you out and exploring.
So what can your little knight do? He can jump a use a sword. The first bit of the game for me was getting used to how my characters hit boxes were and how far the sword could swing out. Literally if something hits the feather of your helmet it will damage you. Throughout your adventure you will acquire new weapons, armor, and magical abilities to improve your chances of survival. 1 thing the game could have added to help would be a map. Many parts of the game require you to go back and use new abilities like double jump to find hidden areas and gain new powers. If rather few teleport areas in the game it would have been nice to have a map to make sure I was done looking everywhere rather than traversing the entire map only to find out I might have missed one turn somewhere. Without backtracking with new found abilities this game will be a lot harder than it already is.
If they were going to rename this game they should call it The castle of trial and error because that is what you will be doing most of this game. If you don’t get in the habit of saving right after you kill a boss that took you 20 deaths to beat you will find yourself facing it again if you die before the next save point. If the bosses don’t irritate you the instant deaths of spikes will. Spikes are used in this game to much for my liking. You will learn to cautiously approach every room because many deaths will result in unexpected spike deaths or not jumping the correct way, and it is because of that fact I recommend playing this with a controller. Trying to jump through death traps with the keyboard could be rather frustrating at times.
The variations of enemies is astounding in this game. You will learn how to approach all of them after a couple encounters fairly easily. Bosses require skilled timing and memorization. After realizing how to defeat a boss the pattern might seem fairly simple. If you don’t have the right weapon however the task can be very agitating. After beating bosses though you will be filled if a huge feeling of relief and you will rush cautiously back to the last save point so you don’t have to do the encounter again. The soundtrack fit the game perfectly and I wish I could enjoy it more if I wasn’t constantly hearing the small tone that plays after you die.
Overall the game has a super large variety of enemies and bosses for players to face off against, there is no lack of content to be found here. The soundtrack fit this game perfectly. However lack of a map made backtracking a hassle and spikes felt slightly over used for my taste. If you’re into a nice challenging platformer then this might be what you’re looking for. If you don’t have a lot of patience, aren’t that good at platforming maybe you should pass this one up and come back to it later on.

Valve's documentary, "Free To Play" is a beautiful insight into the world of the competitive pc gamer through the medium of the E-Sport game Dota 2. For everyone and every game, what we see through our point of view is our own perspective. The documentary is orchestrated to allow true gamers at heart to know, and to a limit, share the struggles the three heroes that the documentary follows. All gamers would go through the same story in different places, different times, and different lives. If you  played video games, you gave up time (usually studies) to indulge in entertainment where you can be someone else. In the doc, the dedication was taken a step further and with good reason. Fear (Clinton Loomis) had played for the love of the game, yet it is mentioned he wants to provide for his mother who has sacrificed so much for his family through her hard work and especially since his father abandoned them. HyHy (Benedict Lim) seemingly played to prove his family wrong. He wants to show his time devoted was useful, as well as show his girlfriend she isn't a distraction to him. Dendi (Danil Ishutin) devotes his time in absence of his father. Once he began Dendi just felt he has to show his late father that he will become something to be proud of as well as get rid of his sadness for him. Another account the documentary follows is China's participation. They are the favorited country that was expected to win absolutely everything. Unfortunately we don't get the backstory for their teams. One in particular that is interesting is Lanm (Zhang ZhiCheng) of EHome. He actually went through his own struggles of stealing "Juliet" from her family and trying every way possible to make their life livable. However the insight isn't given and instead, their country is sort of a unified enemy that the three main characters share that is standing in front of their dreams of winning The International. The last thing I want to mention is that the contrast this doc gives in comparison to today. It has been three years since the start of this documentary and we are now seeing tournaments fighting each other in order to provide prize money for players. Every day, more and more hosts and organizers are thinking of their next event to provide resources into the E-Sports scene. There are tons of speculations as to what the goal Valve was thinking this film could reach: promotion, boasting, profit, and player recruitment. For me, the perspective I have is that it is to motivate other gamers and let them know they don't go through struggles alone. Gaming is a legitimate choice to use your time on and Valve is supporting the community as much as they can through backing Dota 2 and hosting The International.

I've been following Techland since around 2008ish when they first released footage on youtube about their zombies and the tech involving decay and such. Then silence before Dead Island got released. Of course I had high hopes for it, but it fell short of the promises of the earlier video.
Dying Light has more visual fidelity than Dead Island, much more detail and better lighting. In fact, the lighting has to be on of the best at the moment. From the use of molotovs, to the subtle spark of an electric based weapon; the lights do effect the world. The sunlight does compliment the environments, from midday to sunsets.
What is exceptional is techlands approach to night. Most open world games leave the light on with subtle hue of blue to emulate moonlight; but most of the time it falls short and has world just as illuminated as it were in sunlight. Now this is no problem to games that use corridors. However Dying Light is an open world game, and does not fall victim to the former. In Dying Light, when the sun sets, night becomes night; it does become dark, nearly pitch black. It makes flashlights invaluable in this game despite it attracting the now more aggressive zombies. At night however, the player really gets to see how substantial lighting is done in the game. Fire barrels glow in the distant, and molotovs thrown do illuminate while the fire is still going, often times illuminting the area more than the flashlight.
Now the gameplay is much more refined than dead island. Melee is predominant, whilst firearms are not uncommon. They are rare in the beginning and become uncommon towards half way through the game. Each item has a rarity, but rarity alludes to how many times it can be repaired before it breaks. Don't fall in love with on weapon as it probably would not last you through out the game. Crafting is simple, adding elemental modifications to a weapon, and having minor upgrades. There is loot to be found everywhere, and most items are useful.
Parkour...free running, or what ever you call it
is very intuitive, it does get you places, and get you off the streets. It is a bit to get used to, but once you do, you can outrun and get to safety faster. Sometimes the flight in "fight or flight" becomes more satisfying.
Zombies. Well they are zombies as you would know them, and they get aggresive at night. There are different species such as the boomer, witch, ta....wait thats Left 4 Dead...well all the special zombies are akin to the specials in left 4 dead. Zombies react to sound and light. But zombies are half of what you should be worried about, there are bandits as well. Zombies do take a good chunk of your health each time, but you are never without healthpacks and you do not get punished if you die.
Multiplayer, the zombie mode has you invading peoples game and leveling up your skills. Simple, like left 4 dead, and the co-op is the same thing. Drop in, help a friend out, and drop out. You probably won't be invading a lot of people because you can opt out for online.
