The fourth 12 Labours of Hercules game is undeniably made for those who are familiar with the series, but they will find probably the best combination of level design and gameplay mechanics so far.
While I was playing though Mother Nature, I couldn’t shake the feeling that it was made only for the long-time players of the 12 Labours of Hercules games, so this review is written for these people as well. If you are a newcomer, I advise to start the series from the beginning.
For the returning audience, they’ll find probably the best game in the series, combining the level variety/design of Cretan Bull and the expanded gameplay mechanics of Girl Power. The bulk of the work is still done by servants, but by assigning a much more prominent, active role for both Megara and Hercules, there was enough change in the gameplay balance to make it feel fresh and challenging again.
Speaking of balance, a lot of small things were tweaked: for example thieves (and a new enemy, anti-Hercules) are less annoying or farms are more manageable. These seem insignificant on their own, but added up they make the game a lot more fun.
As a final bonus, there is now even some semblance of a story: Megara and Hercules start on a journey to regrow the Hellenic forests before they go on a well-earned vacation, struggling against the meddling gods all the time. It’s a bit silly sometimes, but it shows that the developers really cared.

Now, I'm a big fan of these hidden object adventure games, and I can safely say that there are some amazing ones out there. Sadly, "Crystals of Time" is not one of them.
First of all, the game pretty much leaves you to your own devices for the most part. It's hard to tell which rooms you're supposed to go to next; I kept having to press the hint button to figure out where I was supposed to go. Not only that, you can't easy-jump from room to room using the map; it only leads to certain general areas of the house, the garden, etc. As a result, there's a lot of backtracking involved, and it quickly gets annoying.
Second, the so-called story in this game really has no bearing when you actually start playing. First of all, why does a thief need to break into an abandoned mansion? And those "crystals of time" that are supposed to be super-important? Yeah, you spend most of the game looking for the crystals, but actual time traveling literally only happens in three rooms of the game. Nowhere else! This results in the ending being one of the most anticlimactic I have ever seen. We're introduced to all these characters and pieces of a story, but they don't seem to completely fit together.
As for the puzzles themselves, they're fine. I was pretty much able to figure them all out without any difficulty. But if you like a good story to go with your hidden-object adventure games, I do not recommend this one. At least, not unless you like sitting for thirty seconds waiting for the hint button to recharge.

By now I think we all know what we're getting with these hidden object games and what they're all about, so let's dispense with the foreplay and get straight to the nitty-gritty.
Crystals of Time is just about as middle of the road as you can get - there's nothing amazingly mind-blowing about it, but nothing exceptionally bad, either. Most locations and scenes look nice, if unspectacular, artwork is decent enough, music is OK, if not ever so slightly tedious since it's just the same two tunes played on a loop from beginning to end. There's no voiceover, little in the way of real story to sink your teeth into, very little in the way of bells and whistles in any form, in fact. Everything is just as much as it needs to be for it to be functional and adequately serviceable. It's a budget title through and through.
There are frustrations, though, like a map that isn't as useful as you'd like and forces you to hit the Hint button far too often to find the next location to visit, which could be anywhere since you'll be forced to replay some scenes multiple times and even collect some of the same objects. And sometimes the game can be temperamental in registering your clicks on an item since it needs to be exactly on an object, not a single pixel away from it. It's also annoying that you can only interact with some things at very specific times once you've reached a certain point, or that some sections aren't locked out once you're finished with them, making you wonder if you've missed something or if this will be useful further down the line, when it pretty much never is.
There's also a time mechanic in the game which allows you to travel back to a certain point to see an area as it used to be, but this is only used in two or maybe three rooms in the whole game, and even then, never to any creative end. They're just two different versions of the same place. You can't do anything in the past to change the present, a real missed opportunity for some clever puzzles.
It's times like this I'd kill for a Neutral button to rate this game. As I said, it's completely middle of the road and a largely inoffensive distraction with little in the way of real challenge either in hidden object scenes or in puzzles. Had I run into any of the bugs some others have encountered then maybe I'd be writing a very different review, but for me, it was a pleasant enough, if not forgettable distraction for a couple of hours. If you were lucky enough to grab it during one of its many free giveaways, or got it cheap or as part of a bundle, then I doubt you'd have much cause to regret your time with this game.

Generally a good game and enjoyable to play.  I got about 80 hours of game play out of it to complete the main story and all side quests (still have some challenges and quarantine zones to do).
The beginning of the game is better, some aspects do get a bit long in the tooth towards the end.
Overall I'd give it 4/5 and I would recommend it.
Pros;
- was actually quite scary to begin with (the first night was awesomely pant staining)
- the free running is pretty fluid and they don't make a big thing of it, its just a good game mechanic.
- some of the climbs you have to do are truly vertigo inducing and very fun.
- weapon modding is ok (although you can't mod firearms), it requires a fair bit of scavenging and it enables you to make some pretty bad♥♥♥♥♥weapons.
- the map, the detail! omg this game is stunning. I frequently found myself being like a tourist and stopping to take pictures. Especially at sunset or dawn, it really is a work of art.
- combat with the z's is enjoyable at all stages of the game. to start with they're quite a problem, later you can cut your way through whole crowds of them. But it lulls you into thinking you're unstoppable and then they over power you!
- the "volatiles" (which come out at night) are really hard to deal with (and in the beginning pretty scary). For at least half way through the game you don't really stand a chance trying to fight them (1 maybe, any more and your doomed), so RUN! Later on when you've made some powerful weps you can deal with groups of them, but you don't have much room for error otherwise they will overpower you. So I found that a fun aspect.
Cons
- lock picking. I can see what they're going for, making you sit in a potentially dangerous area while trying to pick the lock, but the process gets really tedious.
- DEATH - WORSE ASPECT OF THE GAME. when you are on a mission and not just roaming, dying really sucks. It makes the game FAR too easy because the world does not get reset. So you spawn back in having dealt with half the Z's but now you're at full health and its just way way too easy. You also lose out of some nice scripted sections because having spawned back in the script has already run and doesn't get reset. So try not to die!
- SPOILER ALERT
End boss fight.  Lame lame lame lame lame. Maybe its cos I'm of the generation who grew up on games like System Shock 2 and HL1. But boss fights where all you do is mash certain keys are just so boring and unsatisfying. I want to actually fight, maybe get creative (and perhaps a bit sadistic) in how I deal with the boss.  Not to just hit a key when it flashes up. Breaks immersion and its so darn easy, it's just a pre-rendered sequence (amusing your inner chimp manages to mash the right key on time).
The game does make you feel pretty vengeful towards the boss and you really want to slice him up limb by limb, but all you get is press A press D press W, then masturbate the F key a bit and your done.
If you are south park fan, you will really like this game.

The Stick of Truth is everything you'd expect from a South Park title. The classic characters are present and the ridiculous humor, social commentary, and obscenities are in full force.

As a game, the mechanics are fine. Combat is engaging with timed events in both offense and defense. There are a lot of fun animations with spells and you can switch things up by rotating different team mates in and out.
Doing sidequests can be a lot of fun and I recommend taking a break from the somewhat predictable storyline to experience South Park.
Overall, the game was fine - not great, not horrible. I happen to like South Park. If you don't like South Park, then I would recommend most likely just skipping this.

Begin.
At first, I am thinking, "ok, this is just a skill-based arcade game; that's cool." I figure I will derive about as much pleasure as I can from it in a few days and move on. In the end, it's about momentum, velocity, speed and the calm storm that you feel when you begin to achieve mastery. Super Hexagon is not my favorite game of all time, but it is one of the most simple, elegant, and beautiful games I have ever played. Once you 'see' it, and begin to flow, there is a state of grace that you won't experience in many games. It's $2.99, get it.

Castle in the darkness is an exploration-adventure game that took on the Metroidvania style approach. So what can you expects from Metroidvania style? This kind of approach will have you a lot of places or rooms to explore, many secret areas to explore, finding treasures like keys or power-up, developing a gameplay mechanic with stuffs, and big-scale puzzle/quest in the game to go back and forth. Castle in the darkness able to grants you all above features and a NG+ at a really little cost.
I mean, seriously, this game give you much much contents that worth more than $6 you spend ($4.97 at 17% discount at launch).
So what will you see in Castle in the darkness? This game give you a role of hero to fight his way through a lot of monsters and finding a princess. Monsters and bosses will stand in your ways guarding treasures, spells, equipments, and keys. This is like a traditional setting of adventure games which is fun and Castle in the darkness make a good job to deliver these experience of exploration to players. The first challenge this game throw at your face is 1 Atk, 1 Def, and low help. You can take damage upto 2-4 times at most so first solution to you is carefully advancing the game. Most bosses in this game have only 2-3 patterns at most, actually, once you understand their pattern, fighting monsters and bosses in this game is ridiculously easy.
However the Castle in the darkness does not places it's essence on battling monsters, instead, developer focus on making a challenge situations that will hook player to focusing on precisive control to advance in various haphazard environment design. (Please think of games such as Super meatboy, Limbo, VVVVVV but this game isn't as extreme as those game) So after you able to equip yourself with better equipments and can take more damages you will find yourself in a more extreme situations with lots of holes and spikes, and this is the second challenges this game throw at your face (lol). After this point you may find yourself cannot handle the damage from enemy again but you should also pass several optional paths on the way, that is where the exploration begins.
So the true essence of this game lies in a combining of adventuring, finding treassures, and challenging hardship together. Eventhough this game has many things similarly to the Symphony of the nights and some other game, I think developer make a good job to make Castle in the darkness feel different and unique in it's own way.
Anyway, This game is really cheap at it's full prize so you should give it a try. Have fun.

At first, this game was nigh unplayable. The framerate was intolerable at 5 to 20fps on my GTX 770M which is unacceptable. After scouring forums I found the key to unlocking this gem of a game:
IF YOU HAVE NVIDIA, YOU GOTTA CHANGE THE 3D SETTINGS!
To get this game to run at a high framerame on an NVIDIA card, you have to add it to the 3d Program Settings on the NVIDIA control panel and set the game to run using your GPU (High-performance nvidia processor). Then the game runs smooth as silk. As for the game itself, it's faithful to the PS4 port, a monster hunting squad based game with multiple missions, big bosses, upgradeable weapons and armor, abilities. and a....somewhat decent story. The game is fun: ya just gotta change the 3D settings to find this fun.

Atm the game is only recommended when you fulfill the following criteria:
- AMD GPU, Nvidia GPUs have some serious problems
- 64 Bit OS and DirectX 11 GPU, otherwise blackscreen
- Monitor with a maximum resolution of 1920x1080, no support for higher res
- Xbox 360 or PS4 Gamepad, game is not playable with KB/M
- You can life with 30FPS, unlocking makes the game unplayable
- Always online, even for the singleplayer you need a connection
---
When you "fulfill" the criteria you get a user-friendly Monster Hunter.
It simplified some aspects but brings also some new stuff in the genre.
Aktuell nur zu empfehlen wenn folgende Kriterien gegeben sind:
- AMD Grafikkarte, Nvidia GPUs leiden unter Performance-Problemen
- 64Bit OS und DirectX 11 Grafikkarte, sonst bleibt der Bildschirm schwarz
- Monitor mit einer maximalen Auflösung von 1920x1080, höher wird nicht unterstützt
- Xbox 360 oder PS4 Controller, mit Maus und Tastatur nicht spielbar
- Man mit 30FPS leben kann, eine höhere Bildfrequenz macht das Spiel unspielbar
- Stets online, das Spiel verlangt auch im Singleplayer eine Internet Verbindung
---
"Erfüllt" man nun diese Kriterien erwartetet einem ein benutzerfreundlicheres Monster Hunter.
Einiges wird vereinfacht aber es werden auch neue Aspekte ins Genre eingebracht.
- Eine Geschichte ist vorhanden, anfangs recht flach entwickelt sich diese
- Kluge* NPC Kameraden, sowohl im Singleplayer als auch online verfügbar
- Wenig Grind im Gegensatz zu MH Titeln
- Pet und eine 2te Truppe an NPCs kann man Rohstoffe sammeln lassen
- Pet unterstützt einem im Kampf, wenn man im selben Gebiet ist
- Flüssige Kampfanimationen, ordentliches Effekt-Gewitter
- Gruppen Kombo System
- Passendes Monster, Waffen, Rüstungs-Design (Japan Stil)
- Es gibt 10 Klassen die über die Wahl der Seele** (Mitama) bestimmt werden
- Ausführliches Tutorial auf Wunsch, bei Yamoto (Augenklappe)
- Guter Soundtrack, könnte nach der Zeit aber untergehen
*Im Free Mode, werden (unterstützende) Fähigkeiten gezielt eingesetzt, Angriffen wird ausgewichen, abgeschlagene Körperteile werden "gereinigt", sitzt der eigene Charakter in einer Statusveränderung fest (vereist/schlafend) "schlagen" einem die eigenen Leute daraus heraus.
**300 Seelen um die eigenen Spielstil anzupassen, können gelevelt (lernen neue passive Fähigkeiten) und kombiniert werden wenn sie zueinander kompatibel sind.
- Anfangs deutlicher einfacher als ein MH (ab Chapter 5 zieht er an)
- Statt zu kochen* geht man baden und oder spendet Gold um sich buffen zu lassen
- Eye of Truth Sicht zeigt abschlagbare Körperteile, deren Zustand und Lebensleiste des Oni
- Kein Friendly Fire** und man kann durch Mitspieler durchlaufen
*Vereinfacht die Sache nur bekommt man nicht immer den Buff den man sich wünscht. Beim baden muss auch beachtet werden dass der Charakter nicht immer rein kann. Mal ist die Quelle nur für männliche mal nur für weibliche Charaktere geöffnet. Das kann man durch Freundschaften später
aber auch umgehen.
**Meist hat es gestört wenn man von seinen eigenen Mitspielern umgeworfen, überrannt ect. wurde. Allerdings führte es auch zu mehr Absprache und Taktik. Allerdings macht es auch Spaß sich mal keine Gedanken darüber zu machen.
- Zu teuer
- Altbackene Grafik, dennoch recht detailreich
- Erfüllt nicht die Standards heutiger Konsolen Portierungen
- "Nur" Englische Texte (für einige sicher ein Problem)
- Mäßige Charaktererstellung
- Nur sammeln und töten Aufgaben
- Relativ enge, kleine Kartenabschnitte
- Wiederholend, ist man als MH Spieler ja wie gewöhnt
- Online Modus beinhaltet keinen Chat*
*Zwecks Kommunikation muss auf englische, vorgefertigte Texte in verschiedenen Kategorieren zurückgegriffen werden oder man nutzt Emotes. TS³ oder Alternativen sind dem vorzuziehen.

What happens when a underground style gets so popular that even a game is made using its unique style?
Mirror's Edge happened. With this said, let's begin, shall we?
Graphics: Oh my god, i forgot how i used to love how Mirror's Edge looked like. It had a different visual style, using more red, blue and white than any other color. That's because it fuses together with the universe of the game and give a better personification of who are the heroes and the villains. More than that, textures and overall presentation were pretty sweet. Using PhysicX to make all the details (Grass breaking, heavy footsteeps and some animations) even more detailed was a nice touch and let us experience a game that, even tough is linear and not really open world, gives to the player the sensation of freedom.
Gameplay: Mirror's Edge is like Sonic in first person. You will run and jump, but it also haves a variation of the many challenges/puzzles that you will have to do so you can arrive at your mission objective. The game did a good job at keep motion and mobility of parkour at the same time and it's pretty realistic. No "you just din't survived this♥♥♥♥♥♥quot; falls and no "oh my god, my characther is so weak", it's all up for the player's capacity of thinking fast and making the right decision to either escape from the police or pass through one of the challenges that i mentioned above.
Gunplay is quite okay and, since you don't use it so much (Except for the final part of the game), it's okay for what this game is. The mechanic of making the characther heavier while carrying guns was rather annoying. Why does a single pistol weights so much that i can't even make a straight, low, jump with it? Damn. But i guess it was to keep the focus of the game: Fighting with your own hands and making your way using only your parkous abilities. A bit forced, but okay for me.
Slow motion helps a lot, even more because you can use it on quick time events, and damn, they are fast. I'm pretty sure that there were times that i pushed the defense button but my characther just kept dun goofing. Weird, but passable.
Level Design: Really love. Exploring for secrets, doing time runs and just playing the game for the sake of doing it feels good. All the levels maintain both the interest of the player and variation, always showing new challenges and different ways to use your parkous abilities to solve all the problems that you will face. Sometimes the jumps looks almost impossible, but it's all about using what the game will give you. Sometimes the answer is right in front of you, but you just can't see it. And as i said, combining it with the graphics, it gives the sensation of freedom to the play and always make you think that you're playing a open world game. Even if it's linear, i can remember of 2-3 that i could've taken another path to get to the same place, and it was a nice touch. It could've been more used through the game, but that doesn't take the bright of the effort put in the level design itself.
Soundtrack: Calm while not being seen and really rock hard when being chased or something is happening in the story side of the game. It always add something to the gameplay and it's pretty neat to hear. Based Lisa Miskovsky (Still Alive, credits song).
Story: Even so people said that this was the low point of the game, for it was actually a pretty good CONCEPT of a plot. Mirror's Edge isn't a game that tries to have a lot of twists or a complicated storyline, but it does haves a good plot to follow and it's enjoyable for what it is. I think i liked it for the fact of the animated scenes making me think that i was watching an Anime or maybe because i think the whole thing of "Freedom To Spread Your Way Of Thinking" gives the player a lot to think about. Even tough Faith and her sister are pretty much the only characters that will shine to you (Aside from the main villain, that, being pretty serious now, i din't liked that much), there are other ones that can be explored in the sequel (Confirmed by EA) and may gives new ways of creating plot devices and sub-stories. The universe is like a hole: The more you dig it, more sand you will have outside of it. I really hope that, since the next game in the series seems to be a open world one, that the NPCs will, at least, have a conection with the first one characters (Or just let them be the first game chracters already). TL;DR - Story had an amazing potential, but it was okay for what the first game tried to be.
Overall, Mirror's Edge is one of a few DICE and EA Games that make it into my "favorite games ever" list. Not even Battlefield 2 made it into this one (And it's a pretty awesome shooter IMO). I guess it's because of how this game tried to change the way of using FPS and explored the many possibilites of using parkour in your favor as a game developer. I really hope that the sequel keeps the shine that i still can see in this gem and will be as good as the first one.
If you are waiting for the second game, being afraid of buying the first one, please, don't. Even tough i think you really don't need to play it for the story, there's a lot in this game to see and explore. Even i keep revisiting this game from time to time, always surprising myself with something that i haven't seen before.

By now I think we all know what we're getting with these hidden object games and what they're all about, so let's dispense with the foreplay and get straight to the nitty-gritty.
Crystals of Time is just about as middle of the road as you can get - there's nothing amazingly mind-blowing about it, but nothing exceptionally bad, either. Most locations and scenes look nice, if unspectacular, artwork is decent enough, music is OK, if not ever so slightly tedious since it's just the same two tunes played on a loop from beginning to end. There's no voiceover, little in the way of real story to sink your teeth into, very little in the way of bells and whistles in any form, in fact. Everything is just as much as it needs to be for it to be functional and adequately serviceable. It's a budget title through and through.
There are frustrations, though, like a map that isn't as useful as you'd like and forces you to hit the Hint button far too often to find the next location to visit, which could be anywhere since you'll be forced to replay some scenes multiple times and even collect some of the same objects. And sometimes the game can be temperamental in registering your clicks on an item since it needs to be exactly on an object, not a single pixel away from it. It's also annoying that you can only interact with some things at very specific times once you've reached a certain point, or that some sections aren't locked out once you're finished with them, making you wonder if you've missed something or if this will be useful further down the line, when it pretty much never is.
There's also a time mechanic in the game which allows you to travel back to a certain point to see an area as it used to be, but this is only used in two or maybe three rooms in the whole game, and even then, never to any creative end. They're just two different versions of the same place. You can't do anything in the past to change the present, a real missed opportunity for some clever puzzles.
It's times like this I'd kill for a Neutral button to rate this game. As I said, it's completely middle of the road and a largely inoffensive distraction with little in the way of real challenge either in hidden object scenes or in puzzles. Had I run into any of the bugs some others have encountered then maybe I'd be writing a very different review, but for me, it was a pleasant enough, if not forgettable distraction for a couple of hours. If you were lucky enough to grab it during one of its many free giveaways, or got it cheap or as part of a bundle, then I doubt you'd have much cause to regret your time with this game.

TLDR: Do not play this game, it's pay-to-win and you'll spend double on this card game than you would others.
I tried so hard to like this game. There were some cool things like the anime art styles, the evolve mechanic, a single player mode, and achievements that serve a purpose. Yet through all that, I grew to hate this game.
First off, the biggest problem is that this game is pay to win. Legendaries and Gold cards are necessary to win, no questions asked. The average player is not good enough to progress without them. Whales throwing money at this game will always have the advantage. The power creep in rarity spikes at Gold and Legendary, more than it should ordinarily. With the ability to put three of ANY card in your deck, it makes this problem all the more glaring. Speaking of legendaries...
Card drops are another problem, they never give you any legendaries. I suspect there's some kind of system that gives you better legendary rates if you use crystals, the in-game currency, but I have no way of proving that. What I do know is that Tempest of the Gods has double the legendaries of previous expansions. I saved up 4000 Gold and bought 40 packs. Each pack has 8 cards, multiply that by 40 and I got 320 cards. Of those 320 only 2 were legendaries. I've opened half that amount of packs and got more legendaries in other games. There is some tampering going on. This is the second biggest pool of legends in this expansion and I only got 2? Out of 320 cards? a reasonable game would have seen me with 5, 4 if a pity timer was implemented. And if you decide to bit the bullet and buy packs so you'll get a fair shot at these better cards, you can buy 28 packs in this game for the price of 40 in Hearthstone. Factor in that Hearthstone has a pity-timer to guarantee that you walk away with a legendary every 20 packs and caps it at one per deck versus Shadowverses three per deck with no pity timer.
The RNG in this game is way off. You'll often find that you mulligan a card into your deck just to draw it again or draw your highest cost cards without fail. It's not like I was playing a top heavy deck either. I played Bloodcraft aggro, a deck that relies on getting lots of low cost minions out quickly. I had 4 cards the cost 6 play point and one that cost 7 but those cards would constantly make up half of my opening hand. And any 'random' effects will see the best possible outcome most of the time. This went for me too, a random damage effect would happen and I would have a 1 in 5 chance of hitting the best target. I or my opponent would always hit that best target.
It's just not worth it. There's probably an awesome card game online for hopeless weeaboo trash like myself, but it's not this one. Save your money and patience.

My first go at a Rogue-like game and I was very impressed. The Game handles superbly with a precise SmashTV like control scheme and simple, yet very elegant gameplay and design. The graphics and presentation is also very superb and do go a surprisingly good job of building an atmosphere with text and computer terminal logs building the story and the action is greatly displayed, which is very surprising given its Atari 2600 like graphics. The sound design really helps to build a tense lonely atmosphere with the hum of broken machines and silence of the large dead areas, the weapon sounds are meaty and powerful giving a satisfying edge to the whole experience. The crafting itself is very simple and useful; you can do it anywhere and improvise great powerful weapons that can help you out of jam with basic items found around the levels. Their use only once restriction helps build and maintain tension and serves not make you feels like an alpha & omega.
The only two downsides is a very unforgiving save system and a very bland story. The save system involves the player reaching a certain level so that a start point two levels previous becomes available, once you die your booted back to the menu screen. It could also be seen as a positive as it make the situation all the more tense but the frustration that comes from your character been terminated before the save point can sometimes lead to a rage quit and not the determination to continue. The story is pretty much DOOM (DOOM3 in-particular) mixed with Half Life and a dash of Wolfenstein 3D. The set up; A research station on a remote planet been infested with mutants and zombies, you, a lone space scientist much fight your way out to get home. It’s a set up as old as shooters themselves and I will happily admit that it’s more of a taste and interest issue for me personally but I do feel that everything else in the game could have been used for a great original story so I am a tad disappointed.
But these are small negative new potatoes to the massive Baked potato that is a great little game and I would highly recommend this to anyone who is in for a blaster with great presentation. Paradox Entertainment is a studio with a lot of promise and talent and I look forward to their next project.

After rescuing Megara, after fighting the Cretan Bull and after Megara herself rescuing her husband, what will happen now in Hercules's world? Well, Nature seems to die around, Hercules is sick but recovers quickly before being confronted to his evil twin and after bashing Zeus, Hades and Hera (who were his previous opponents in the previous games), he has to rebuild a resort.
And why does Mother Nature do? Well..., during the five episodes, if you save the nature, you'll uncover some new paths... Well, your servants are still doing the gathering of food (whether from a farm or from bushes or from cheese on the map), gold (whether from mining or the gold on the map) and wood (whether from the trees or from the workshop or from the wood on the map). You still have to repair bridges, holes in the ground, cover lava or acid pit, remove (golden) teeth or horns, etc... You can still upgrade your workshops, farms and mines to have a better recolt, you can still build obelisks to the glory of Demeter, Hermes, Hephaïstos or Apollo for permanent bonus, Megara is still used for growing bushes or pearls and Hercules for removing boulders, Cerberus for scaring ghosts, Pegasus for removing rocks, Medusa to scare Minotaurs, Cyclops to take sheeps, Charon to take floating ressources against gold... And you still have bonus that can be used for a limited time (stopping the timer, going faster, working faster, more ressources, one more temporary servant), during the levels. You still have thiefs, though they're not as common as before.
So what really changed? Well, now, Megara can relive dead trees or washes away oil spills. Hercules can open fire hydrants. And these actions in some levels can unlock blocked paths (because of fire, because of water, etc..). That's the major change in the game. Also, now, the evil twin can block the servants's path and only Hercules can give him a shot in the posterior. Two new characters appear also as merchants: Midas can give gold against wood or food while Epaius or something like that can exchange wood for food for example. And only Megara can negociate with them.
Otherwise, it's still the same way to tell the story, the same graphics, the same music, the same puzzles to unlock bonus levels and the same achievements as before. And for the extras, as it's a special edition, it's only a guide and wallpapers.
So, yeah, I wasn't really expecting a new way of playing. The new additions are nice though. It's changing a little the repetitive stuff (send servants to collect, etc..). Also, where you had a special final level at the end of each world, here, there is none.
So, the price is correct for the game. Those who liked the previous games will enjoy this one too. Those expecting more actions or twists will be disappointed. I've enjoyed this fourth game. And I do think that it's still worthy to be recommended even if there is no big surprise.

For $9.97, it's slightly pricey but I felt it was worth it. I liked watching the South Park shows and this game really made followed the series closely. Permanently missed out on Beetlebot, so I couldn't get complete the Chinpokomon quest.
PROS
1. Combat System
So simple yet so much more fun. Simple actions like mashing AD, WASD, W or clicking when the shiny light comes on makes combat slightly more fun. However, the fun kind of fades away when your abilities power up to ridiculous levels and you want to use the most powerful ones over and over again.
2. Story
So odd, some scenes seem to remind me of people in real life. Despite the exaggeration of the cartoon, I have actually seen some real-life scenarios of what was shown in the game. E.g. 2-faced girls.
3. Puzzles
There are just so many. You don't have to kill monsters if you don't want to. You can just use the environment to kill them.
4. Mini-games
Dancing Goth Game, Abortion Game, All the potential "Sorry Australia" mini-games, You could probably add all the mini-games from the Deponia series (Those are pretty good).
CONS
1. No Multiplayer
I think that you could have created a 2-3 man questing system with a much bigger world with bosses. There are so many things from South Park that weren't shown. E.g. North Korea and the Dinosaur♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Stephen Hawking, Greenpeace.
2. Repetitive System
Monsters level up in the same way, i.e. more HP and more armour. Their attack patterns are basically the same. I was hoping for more variety.
3. Missable Quests
It's not really fun to know that there are quests that you have missed and can't return to. You don't really want to look at a guide and replay the whole game again.

Dear Resident Evil 2,
I have loved you for many years. Though many Resident Evil games have come after you, they were but a fleeting moment of enjoyment before I swore again that no one could rival you. Well, I'm sorry to say that I've met a game. While you will always own a big part of my survival horror heart, it is not completely yours any longer.
With fond thoughts always, Pointnclickster
Claire, I have missed you! You are now older and wiser and helping Barry Burton's daughter survive and teaching her what it is to be a great young RE hero just like you were 19 years ago!
Resident Evil: Revelations 2 is probably one the most overlooked RE games. Each main entry of the Resident Evil has its own fanbase and critique's corner, but I never saw much discussion about this one. This game needs more press. I feel that this is Capcom's offering to the lovers of the original trilogy. The story fits quite nicely between RE5 and RE6.
Where to begin? Lets get the technical out of the way. The gameplay between the various heroes is awesome! Great AI! Claire and Barry are partnered with the most unlikely of partners, especially Barry. The combat is fun as you play off your partner for combos. The menu systems were very straight forward and a lot of things we loved from the originals were back: limited inventory, the ability to combine items to create secondary weapons. I loved finding little holding packs. The soundtrack was exciting but mostly very eerie. I felt the game was wonderful to look at. The locales....oh my goodness they were disturbing at times. I felt that Capcom thought, "Hey, lets see what Konami did with its well known psychological horror franchise ;) and see what we can incorporate!". There were times when I wondered if my RE heroes had accidentally dropped into a Silent Hill backdrop. I also saw glimpses of Outlast and Saw, in terms of setting. The settings for me at least, really moved this game from B horror camp to creepy disturbing horror, which I never associate with Resident Evil.
While the story is good, creepy, and disturbing, this game is all about the characters. If I've said it once, I've said it a thousand times, "Claire, you have been missed! Why don't we see more of you?!". She has grown up a lot since RE2 and Code: Veronica. She is partnered with young Moira Burton, whom I believe could be the Claire Redfield of this generation. Moira has attitude and a mouth that goes with it. Her one liners touched with profanity are hilarious and are touched with RE memorableness. While Claire has the gun, Moira likes to bash stuff with her crowbar ( loved playing as Moira). Barry really shines in this game. In previous titles he is known for his famous one liners. Here, he is much more fleshed out. He is looking for his daughter Moira and is accompanied by Natalia. Natalia is a walking cliche: young girl with dark hair that has powers of knowing when enemies are around. The nice change is that Natalia isn't evil, which makes her slightly less creepy. She is a great help to Barry in helping spot enemies. The relationship that develops between Barry and Natalia really got me in the parent feels. It's a beautiful relationship that grows as the game progresses.
The delivery of this game is great on a few levels. First, the episodic nature and the finding of treasures and easter eggs ups the replayability, since achieving certain goals unlocks goodies like guns, or outfits, or character perks. Yes, there is a character/ability tree to improve your characters! Also the Claire/Moira campaign happens
before the Barry/Natasha campaign, so seeing the decay of the various settings is really neat. There are puzzles! They are not difficult but it was nice to see some return to the original trilogy. There are two endings! I intend to go back for the good ending since the bad ending is very very pessimistic.
Amidst RE 4,5, and 6, Revelations 2 seeks to say, "Fans of the originals, we have not forgotten you." This game was a nice return to survival horror. This game knows its roots, and it honors it accordingly from the characters to the script. It took it beyond Resident Evil as far as setting and aesthetics. For me, this was the perfect modern Resident Evil game.

Castle In The Darkness, developed by Matt Kap, and published by Nicalis of Cave Story fame.  In it, you are the lone surviving royal knight, and it is your quest to find the princess and save the kingdom from the hordes of invading monsters.  Sounds familiar, I’m sure.  The story is minimal, but still manages to throw a few unexpected twists at you.  The writing, such as it is, is funny and incorporates many tropes, gags, and in-jokes from gaming history.  Much of it is conveyed visually and will be recognized immediately by any seasoned gamer.
I know it will be compared a lot to Shovel Knight, and they are similar in some ways, but this does not feel like a clone at all. Whereas Shovel Knight leans more toward the Mega Man/Mario 3 end of the platforming spectrum, Castle In The Darkness draws more inspiration from Castlevania:SOTN and Metroid.  There is no map, as NES era games often did not. That might be a problem for some, but I haven’t had much issue with it yet. The music is great and always complements the overall aesthetic of each area.  The art style is great and really captures the NES’ essence.  It is clean and consistent throughout.  I never saw a single out-of-place sprite.
There are a ton of bosses. Most of them are pretty varied and interesting. Some I killed in one life fairly easily, but a few required 5+ attempts. When you defeat one, you are rewarded with lots of coins and a heart that increases your total health.
During your adventure, you will find Armor, Weapons, Magic, and Relics throughout your quest. Some are needed to proceed, and others are optional.  Killing enemies causes them to explode into coins for you to collect.  These can be used for purchasing new equipment from NPCs.  Mostly though, it seems new gear is found in chests.  Plenty of stuff can only be found in cleverly hidden secret areas.
The controls are tight and not the least bit floaty. I used a controller, but keyboard controls worked well for the short time I used them.  I see some people on various forums and websites complaining of cheap, unavoidable deaths. Yes, you will die frequently, but in my experience, each one is my own fault. This isn’t like I Wanna Be The Guy where the goal is to make you rage quit hilariously for YouTube hits. There are crumbling platforms and spikes falling from the ceiling, but you always have a chance to get out of the way if your reflexes are up to the task. And once you’ve seen it, you know. It helps that save points are fairly common and are often placed very near boss fights and difficult platforms.
There are a few technical issues holding it back, though. Each time you start the game, it opens in 2X windowed mode regardless of how you had it set previously. It’s a bit of a pain to have to change it to fullscreen when ever I want to play. I’ve only had one crash (right after springing off a crumbling block), but some are reporting more serious bugs. Hopefully these issues will be fixed quickly. In my case, these have only been a minor nuisance.  While writing this, the game was updated, so this complaint might already be moot.

For the price, I can hardly believe how good this game is. There is a ton of content. So far, I’ve got 3 hours and 25% complete. New Game+ and 100% completion give it even more longevity.
Seriously, just give it a chance if you like Metroidvanias even a little. It’s cheap enough to be a no-brainer in my opinion.

A few caveats first: I am a casual gamer - I have played a moderate number of games, and most of them have not been completed.  I have played a few MMOs but mostly play non-MMO games in either single player or co-op modes.  Some of my fav games have been Lost Planet, Halo, Mass Effect, Need for Speed, Burnout, etc.  I like using a gamepad controller.  I don't generally like heavily detalied games and favor sci-fi and some balance between story / action.  So now you have some idea of my "GP" (gaming perspective).
I LOVE THIS GAME. Not surprising b/c of sci-fi element. Story, voice acting, etc won't win academy awards - but is good enough to be enjoyable, if not a bit redundant at times.  Nothing is perfect - but I thought it was pretty well done.  I actually read most of the research conclusions, etc.  If not your cup of tea, just skip it.
The thing is, this game has something for everyone.  Play it your way! And adjust difficulty to your liking.  Hate the story, skip it and turn off dialogue.  I am not a huge fan of turn-based strategy games, but I love this one.  I actually liked controlling the save system so I could play with different stratedgies.  And base management - IMO fine balance between resource management but not over-bearingly so.  Well done. Simple enough to understand quickly, but involved enough to give a certain sense of reality (well, to some degree - use your imagination :) to the game: You are the commander, after all.
The game becomes easier to play the farther you progress - not that the alien waves don't become a little harder (sometimes)... which I like.  After all, the alien's didn't ask how leved'ed up you were when they arrived, did they? They were what they were - and you had to learn, adapt, research, build, get better !  So be careful early on and pay attention to resource allocation.
Graphics: Good to better-than-good.  Fine for what the game is.
Music:  Very well done - I thought it set the mood well.
Voice:  Repetitive but ok - filled out the story ok.
Controls:  I am biased - I like controllers - and they implemented gamepad control (xbox mode) very well.  Fairly intuitive.  Cannot comment on keyboard/mouse control.
Issues: Yep. Its a game.  Written by humans with limited budgets sold to a lot of people with no limit of preferences and opinions.
1.  Its a numbers game, with shot percentages adjusted randomly.  90% hit chance means you will miss 10% of the time (at least, by definition) - so don't think b/c you are 20 ft from the alien with a ranked-up soilder ensures you'll hit the stationairy target - you might miss.  But, sometimes you should then die, and it will miss also.  It evens out.  I guess. Didn't always feel like it.
2.  Repetitive dialogue.  Get used to it - or turn it off.
3.  Reverse challenge model. Takes some getting used to. I actually agree with this model, just took some getting used to. Not really a bug ,,, just aggravating at first.
4. The tutorial portion is ok, but doesn't tell you everything. Some nuances of resource management will either need to be experimented with (might use save points first) , or read a guide or whatever.
Note: I have not played the first XCOM game yet (plan to) so I cannot compare it to the original.  I also have not purchased the Enemy Within extension yet - so cannot comment on that either: I am looking forward to it.
Last comment: Some games drive me nuts with save system and reply value on episode defeats, etc.  I screwed up a few times and had to replay long sections of the game.  I not only didn't care, I kinda enjoyed it again!  The only sad part of the game for me was the last mission - b/c I knew it was about over.  And then it was.  Sigh.

When I first saw Dying Light on Steam I was suspicious that it would be a Dead Island clone, and I was not entirely wrong since the gameplay, crafting and the special zombies are really similar.
The thing that makes Dying Light better is the survival aspect and the difficulty you will experience in the first half of the game and during the nights when the super zombies from hell roam the streets seeking to eat you.
I have never played a game that immersed me so much in a Zombie apocalypse like this one : the zombies are really numerous, dangerous and attracted by noise, there are numerous encounters with survivors fighting zombies, selling stuff or just resting on roofs, supplies are frequently airdropped on the map containing medkits, emergency packages and flares (useful during the night) and you have to hurry to get them or the bandits will be there to take it.
I should also point out that the firearms are really more powerful and easy to use than in Dead Island, for instance a single bullet to the head with any gun will OS most of the zombies and humans you will encounter making them really useful during the day (during the night shooting will draw all the volatile's attention).
The only thing that bothered me was the story, interesting in the beginning and then really lame the more you progress in the campaign, which is quite short to be honest. On the bright side the optional quests are fun to do and compensate for the short campaign.

- OLD THOUGHTS - UPDATED THOUGHTS BELOW -
THOUGHTS:    02.07.2015
I haven't finished the game yet, but at almost 8 hours in, I feel I've played enough to share my thoughts. I'll update this if/when I finish the game to update/finalize my thoughts. Here's what I feel right now.
This game is fantastic. It really captures NES-style fun, platforming and frustration.
- PROS -
- Great art direction; I really like the look of the backgrounds and characters.
- Great understanding of contrasting colors. Oftentimes a cool color will be in the background and a warm in the foreground (or vice versa ). Really makes the game pop (so many games get this wrong. It's great to see it done well here).
- Gameplay is fun and varied. The jump feels great too (not *fantastic*, but very good).
- Wide variety of weapons and items to keep gameplay from becoming bland.
- Really good music. When I entered a certain area - I had to pause for a second and just listen to it. It sounded *very* familiar (I'll leave it at that). Once I got the reference, it made me grin from ear to ear.
- Lots of cute, interesting nods to other games (Mega Man, Castlevania, etc.).
- Interesting, challenging boss battles. I hate boss battles that are *just* long. Here they're challenging and varied - but not too long once you get the pattern down. That's cool.
- CONS -
- It took me a while to get used to the screen transition. In Super Metroid, The Binding of Issac (or a host of other games  - Shovel Knight, even) when you enter a new screen, the character pauses and slides across the screen as the new area is introduced. It helps to keep everything clear: here is the character; here is a new area. In 'Castle in the Darkness' the new screen just kinda pops into existence. Then it takes me a half-second to find where the character is. I have to admit that I found it rather jarring for the first few screens. I got used to it...and this may not affect everyone - but just thought I'd mention it here.
- No map system - and the game is HUGE. I may have to break out some graph paper and draw my own...
- (As far as I know) No 'current objective' slide to look at. So, if you put this game down for a week and come back you would be COMPLETELY lost.
- 'One-hit kill' spikes abound.
-NOTES-
It has to be mentioned (as I'm sure you've read in other reviews) - this game is *hard*. I think I have over 300 deaths already. It's cool, though - having a blast doing it. What's important to note is that this game uses a design philosophy that some players may not like - what I call "playing from save point to save point". It reminded me of a saying I hadn't thought of in years - "It's not real until you save." Beat a boss? Go back and save. Got a new item? Go back and save. Unlocked a secret room that's really cool and you want to explore it? For the love of all that is good GO BACK AND SAVE YOUR GAME. This is not a game where you run carelessly past save points as you vanquish foes with ease. This is a game where you jump for joy at save points, thank them for existing, give them a huge hug and kiss and then step cautiously into the next room. I grew up on games like this, so I understand this design philosophy - but I can see how others could see this as annoying or grindy.
Also, as I get further into the game, the amount of 'one-hit kills' (i.e. spikes) seems to be increasing exponentially. I hope the endgame is not just jumping through like thirty rooms filled with spikes - and if you slip up and touch ONE of them - you gotta go all the way back to the beginning. I mean, Super Meat Boy has one-hit kills as well - but that game has a super-fast reload time and no level is more than one screen long. That level of difficulty in this metroidvania structure would NOT work well. I hope that doesn't happen. >_<
- OVERALL -
So far, I'm really enjoying the game. Great NES-style action and great music. If you love platformers and you're ready for a challenge, I say pick it up (it's less than $5!). If you want something light to beat in a weekend, though...this may not be for you. I, however, am thoroughly enjoying it and look forward to seeing what other craziness the game has to offer (and I've seen some crazy rooms in it already). I hope I'm able to finish it. *fingers crossed*

Short Review
Great game. Fun Open World, Cool Charcters most of us will know, fun levels and worth the money. Better than the Avengers edition of the game. Voice actors are good, but not the same as the ones in the movies. Controlls can be wierd and has a some bugs .Save system is wonky, but you figure ot out eventually. Great game.
Long Review
Great game. The Open World is by far the strongest feature. NYC is full of hidden places to explore and has so many things to do, find, and enjoy. I cannot stress this ebough. If you like open world games, this game is great for that. Compared to games like Skyrim of the Witcher 3, the world is a little small, but it still decent size on its own and is jam packed full of stiff to do and characters to unlock. Even if you beat the game, the open world is a fun place to run around, destroy things, ride cars of bikes, and just have fun. The storyline is OK, albeit a bit short (15 levels), but the levels are long, and you can save at specific parts in the level. It is a bit buggy and the controls can be a bit goofy and cramped. The best way to play is with a controller, or spacing out the WASD movement keys from the action keys. Otherwise, it feels like your hands are cramped together. If you are not a Marvel nerd and dont know all the heros and villians, dont worry. The game isn't really full of random heros. If you have seen any modern day Avengers or X men movies, you will be mostly fine. There will be some characters you do not know, but it doesnt detract from the game. The game does a really nice job of blancing heros and villains in the story, and playble ones. The more common ones are used in the storyline, and the more obscure ones are used in free play annd are unlockable. And if you are a Marvel Superfan, it does have easter eggs, hints, and other things you will enjoy as well. Extra levels and usage of the gold brick make this game have even more replayability. Deadpool and Stan Lee  cameo a lot, adding to the funny atmostphere of the game. The chrarcters, while not voiced by the actors from the modern day movies, still are well voiced, and drop a lot of puns and jokes, customary to all lego games. The fact that it is a Lego game makes it even better. Definetly worth the money and better than the Avengers edition of the game.

At this time, I can't recommend this game to anybody. I also own this game on PS4 and there it works very well, i've almost completed the story and I have dozens of hours sank into it. I was worried what with this being a port and the track record the company has concerning ports, but I took a gamble and bought it anyway. Luckily I have two weeks to get a refund, so i'm waiting for any information to be released shortly before that deadline concerning any patches they have in mind to solve this port's many issues before I submit my request for a refund.  On console the game's great.
The two most glaring problems at the moment in my personal experience make the game unplayable.
The first is that when I run this game in fullscreen, it will either freeze at a black screen permanently or crash. Fun!
Second, if I used windowed to work around this problem then the game performs terribly. The framerate is nowhere near static; I doubt it's ''locked'' to 30, 30 is probably just the best it can do, if you have the seemingly random requirements and specs it takes to have this actually work at all.  The tutorial fight and first visit to town that followed was like I was playing the game in slow motion. It was slow and choppy.
As for a final statement, avoid this game. It's ridiculous that this company can just keep tossing out poor quality ports and not keep anyone updated on if they plan to rectify their mistakes. I may change this review at a later date if they put the work in to fix this, but if not, then it's just another tally on the list of bad ports from the company. It's honestly a fantastic game if it would actually work.
EDIT: By running the game as administrator in compatibility mode with windows 7, I was able to rid myself of most of the problems presented. Now that I can give an actual review of the game (sans the online component, haven't tried that out yet) I can explain some things.
Story: The story of this game is stronger than the counterpart series, or at least from what i've played of it, meaning Monster Hunter. You play the part of a created Slayer, a militarized demon slaying individual that has the ability to speak with and work with the souls of legendary heroes who grant you abilities, called Mitama. There are NPC characters with their own personal storylines to follow, though most of their personalities are somewhat trope-ish. It has more in the story department than most Monster Hunter games, but it's nothing groundbreaking; be a big hero, you're a unique snowflake, yadda yadda and so on.
Gameplay: I like to think of the gameplay as a cross between Monster Hunter and Dynasty Warriors. Combat as a whole is more fast paced and aggressive. Weapons swing faster than in Monster Hunter, combos are in general longer and easier to perform, and the Demons in this game are more aggressive and more durable than most I remember fighting in MH3U or MH4U. You kill demons for materials, use said materials to craft gear, and kill bigger demons. It's a hunting game. There is also a teamwork component. One side of this mechanic is that if you go down, you don't immediately ''cart''. You go into a bleedout and allies can help you up, but if the demon is angry enough sometimes this isn't very possible to perform. On the other side, there's Team Destroyer moves. Each weapon type's Team Destroyer is different in animation, but generally just deals huge damage.
Before I go any further with that, the combat in Toukiden revolves around you dismembering large demons, cutting limbs off of their physical bodies to reveal a ''spirit body'' underneath it. You can purify physical limbs, which works a lot like carving, and prevents the demon from regenerating that limb. Hitting the spirit body is what does actual damage to the demon. Back to Team Destroyers. Basically, as you fight, you have a normal Destroyer gauge, which is a one man super move that instantly hacks off a limb and does high damage, and the Team Destroyer gauge fuels a move that when the gauge is filled allows you to approach allies and connect to them with lines of electricity. The more connections you have, the more limbs you sever with a team Destroyer if your aim is good enough.
Speaking of weapons, there's something for everyone.There's the melee category, with the Sword, Spear, Knives, Chain Sickle, Naginata, Fists, and Hammer, and the ranged category with Bows and Guns. Each one obviously has its own moveset and and specialties, so there's pretty much something for everybody.
Graphics:
Sound: The music I feel is fairly well done and fits with the mood of what you're doing at the moment. The town theme is peaceful and calm, while when in the field the music will switch between standard battle music and more intense music when fighting a large demon. The sound effects for the most part are done well, with each hit you deliver, take, or evade having an appropriate level of volume. You hear your feet hit the ground when you sprint, you hear impact noises when landing hits with your weapon, and standard stuff along those lines. The music of the game fits the mood and setting well.
Controls: Unfortunately this is one of the areas the game falls short. If you don't have a controller, I would suggest holding off on buying this title until you do. The keyboard controls are godawful and from what I understand can't be remapped. I use an Xbox 360 controller, though, and I didn't struggle with any controls. Everything was pretty much exactly where I had expected it to be upon plug in. Being a hunting game, the controls are very responsive and there's almost never a moment where you'll take a hit you feel like shouldn't have connected.
Replay: Being a hunting game, replay value is up in the air. You have three characters slots, but if you really wanted to, you could build every weapon and armor set in the game along with all Mitama on one character. It'd be a grind, but it's totally doable. With that, replay would be a pretty optional thing here. Being it's the only game of its type currently on steam that I know of, i'll likely do several runs through it myself.
Final: If you'd like a hunting game on PC, check this out if you have a controller. I can't guarantee the solution I found will work for everyone, but assuming it does, this is a good game in its own right that sets itself apart from being a clone of Monster Hunter. It has its own pacing and flow, not to mention its own features and quirks that make it fun all on its own.

Mirror's Edge is unique, fast and unforgiving, putting you in a strict governmentally-controlled city where the "Blues" are controlling everything and the only group standing between them and the total control of the city are the "Runners", highly trained and fast free runners that are doing their best to avoid the blues for as long as they can and live from the shadows, undisturbed by the oppression of the blues, which seemed to work just fine. You play as Faith, a young girl who was trained to become a runner after her mother died in what was the last attempt of revolution, and whose only relative that she cares about is her sister, a cop who was framed for the murder of the only man capable to make a chance, Robert Pope who was soon to become the new mayor of the city. She then starts a mission of clearing her name and finding the ones who were truly behind the assassination as it is not only about her sister going to jail, but also about the future of the city which now seemed to remain under totalitarian oppression for a long time. This game isn't your typical open-world adventure, mostly because it isn't exactly open world: you can always see the city and how big it truly is, but you are limited to the area where you current task is, simply because you will spend most of your time jumping from a rooftop to another, and reaching to a different direction than the one where your objective is, is impossible. This isn't a bad thing, as the game will automatically move you from one area to another as the story progresses and even with its limitations you can still choose which route to take, even though sometimes the obvious one is the only one available. The universe created for this game and the possibilities are enormous, however it never reaches its full potential; the campaign is indeed a powerful story about family and honesty, but the anime cutscenes between missions don't favour the plot at all, as they are merely dialogues between a few characters with some movement that most often feels out of place. The cast of characters is also impressive, but in the same way it feels disappointing as you never get to meet all of the runners and find more about their stories or the previous events and the conversations that you do have are just small talk without anything interesting to say that would affect your view of Mirror's Edge' universe.
The entire city is made to be your playground and so the game chooses to focus on just a few primary colours, with the white being predominant for almost anything around you, using red for objects that you may interact with and blue or green for secondary objects that are not necessarily a part of the free-running concept. Using this mechanic, the game manages to deliver a fast phased gameplay where the colours are your guiding instruments, but can sometimes become your disorientation tools as well as some objects such as stairs which will always be painted in red can be put on top of some cranes which will also be painted in red, making it hard to see where the stair is. Aside from those small issues that are isolated to certain areas only, the free running mechanic runs smoothly and the entire game takes no more than five buttons + directions to control, making it easy to move fast as the game originally intended. Aside from the free running, there are certain shooting sequences where you must disarm one of the opponents and use his weapon to kill the others, and even though those work just as smoothly, they are not the thing that makes this game shine, but thankfully some of them are optional as you can avoid certain encounter with the enemies pursuing you and those that are however mandatory will be over before you know it. Throughout the game you will use almost any combination of parkour manoeuvres, from wall jumps to flips, dodges and lots of jumping, and even though at first the entire thing will look hard to do at high speeds, once you get the hang of it you will amaze yourself with the tricks that you managed to pull off and a somehow impossible gap between building will suddenly become a piece of cake once you learn to use everything around you to your advantage. Aside from the free running that is exceptionally made, there is little to change the phase of the game, aside from turning a valve or pressing a button here and there in order to open a door and even though the hidden bags which act as the game's main and only collectible are a significant part of the game itself as you will be alerted by the game's logo on a wall when a bag is nearby, they will only distract you for a few seconds, and after that you're back to see where the story leads you.
Mirror's Edge looks awesome without the smallest doubt and seeing the entire city from the rooftops is impressive, even though you can't access most of it, but for a short game that is meant to take you from one corner of the city to the next one the environments look pretty much the same wherever you go and that is mostly due to the heavy use of white and red to favour the gameplay and even thought it does look unique and amazing at first, seeing the same white and red everywhere you go will eventually make everything seem dull. The PhysX effects do a great job, making glass shatter in realistic ways and explosions or water effects look even more amazing, topping that off with the superb character design makes the game look beautiful wherever you go, no matter who you interact with.
The game sounds as good as it looks, with effects realistic enough to make you feel each fall or wrong turn when you fail a jump and accidentally drop down a few meters or water splashes when you step into a puddle. The gun effects might not be as top notch as the ones you would see in a first person shooter, but they get the job done; the voice acting is decent, but aside from Faith you won't hear anything spectacular, and she doesn't even talk during the actual gameplay, only in cutscenes. The soundtrack is rhythmic with the action and always perfectly bonded with whatever is going on the screen, and the good part is that most of it will unlock as an extra once you finish the game so if you liked it you can listen to it how many times you want afterwards.
Sadly, the entire campaign only takes around 5 hours to complete and even though you do have a time trial and a speed run mode, you only have the playgrounds from the campaign at your disposal, so you will eventually grow tired of running around the same tracks, but at least you have online and friends leaderboards, so you can brag about your scores.
With its minor flaws, Mirror's Edge is still a must play, especially for those in search of a unique, eye-view experience, but unfortunately the game will only last for a few hours and after that aside from the time trial and speed run modes that might keep you busy for a couple more hours at best, there is nothing else to do.

I awake in a storage closet after months of living off of nothing but what I can only describe as wet Cardboard preserved only by this metal encasing that misleadingly says 'Meat'. I have been emotionally and psycologically been pushed further than i ever thought a human being could withstand but despite all I have gone through I know I have to do something. I am not dying here without doing something. I pick myself up off the floor and step past the invisible line that sets off the motion sensor and the door opens; It's time to begin.
I step outside and try to find my bearings but nothing's the same. The Hallways have shifted, the once bustling control center is covered in different Growths. I try to identify some for different sustanence but to no avail; I know what these are, and there's no way I want to be around them much longer. These are part of the experiment sector C was working on, they were trying to biologically modify life forms for military applications, They asked my department to run some tests on these to see exactly what would be the benefits if they infused them with some sort of Mammal. They proved to have poisonous and acidic qualities. As I rememeber all those months ago I feel weak. I put my hand on a nearby table to support myself but it slips and I fall, I look to see what My hand slipped on and I see it's a small handgun. I pick it up and assure myself I won't need it but I take it nonetheless-For security. I tand up and venture down mislplaced hallways until I hear a voice coming from a Room nearby; I can't make out any words but I know I have to see who's there. I once more step past the invisible line to open the door and what I see I couldn't have possibly braced myself for.
There's a man Infused with the same plant life that I saw in the other room stroking the decaying corpse adonned with the same white coat I myself wore for years in this Facility. Although the creature isn't using his body at all; he's completely in control of the Vines that suspend his body in the air. The shock finally subsides when I realize that he hasn't noticed me yet and I reach for the Gun I Have tucked away in my belt. I reach around, as slow as I possibly can as not to draw attention. I feel my hand wrap around the cold metal, take a deep, silent breath, draw it in front of me and turn off the safety. But as I slide the top part back to chamber the bullet the gun may as well screamed as the click it produced caused the monster to drop the corpse, whip it's half-decayed Face at me and Scream 'DROP IT. DROP IT. DROP IT. DROP IT. DROP IT. DROP IT. DROP IT.' As it was chanting the command I nearly complied out of sheer terror but I stood my ground, Aimed and Fired. It recoiled and Released a scream of Agony right before it Charged at me with speed I'd never seen before, Chanting the same commands as it's old body was being dragged across the floor, leaving a red trail behind it. I shot at it until it stopped moving and my handgun was empty. I stared at the mangled, hole ridden clump of vines, blood, and slime until i was brought back into conciousness by a far too late echo of it's final scream that came from somewhere deeper in the facility. I know they're coming, and I need to prepare.

A poorly conceived Hidden Object Game (HOG) whose only redeeming factor is its beautifully drawn, hi-res & detailed environments. (I played this on a 1920 x 1080 screen without any comprises in graphic quality.)
- The narrative is godawful and poorly translated into horrible English.
- The so-called "story" is supremely boring and badly presented.
- Hidden object scenes are uninspiring and tedious, and often a time require repeated clicking to be "found", because their "active areas" are too small.
- Movement is dumber than a box of rocks: e.g. after clicking left to reach a new location, you'd expect that clicking right will bring you back to the previous location, but no, it takes you to a different location! And some scenes have more than one direction arrow, which all lead back to the same location!
- Puzzles are completely lacklustre and many a time just involve random clicking till the solution is reached.
This is another of those HOGs that have a "story" and puzzles just for the sake of doing so. If you're like me and play games primarily to enjoy the plot, skip this one completely.

One of the best puzzle games you could find.
The concept is to guide your character(s) to the end of the level, using a limited number of actions to program their movements.
+ There are quite a number of different mechanisms, from one character to the other (one will be able to activate switches, other will be able to burn boxes ...)
+ The adventure is rich, with more than 200 levels, with various difficulties (going from the tutorial to the brain scracher).
+ Furthermore, there are also "bonus" content that you unlock during the adventure, with some other extra levels, and some other modes with slightly different gameplay.
+ The music is calm and soothing
+ There is a scenario (well, not the most exciting, though)
+ A way to make actions go step by step, and undo/forward as much as you want (or restart the level if you prefer)
+ 3 "Skip level" (compasses) if you're stuck so you can continue (don't abuse of them, you've got only 3, though)
- Characters and other sprites don't blend very well with the rest of the graphics, but well, that's absolutely not a problem !
Overall, one of the best puzzle games I have in my library, and glad to have it !

They should call this the Earth Day edition.  No longer are we cutting down trees with abandon.  Instead we must recultivate the land, grow more trees, and unleash the power of...fire hydrants?!  Yes, fire hydrants.  Who knew they had hydrants back in ancient Greece?

It is a very basic hidden object game you can play to pass the time, but don't expect any major challenge.  On the positive side, you also won't find yourself stuck and ripping your hair out either.  The game has a hint crystal which you can use to guide you along to the next part of the mission.

As is common with many hidden object games, I frequently hunted for the final hidden object in a scene and when I finally had to resort to the hint I was often left frustrated because the object looked nothing like it does in real life.  Other times I clicked on an object 12 times but it didn't pick up... after using the hint it would turn out I was clicking the right object, just not the right pixel.
Another time I needed to find the object "nuts" and there were at least 5 of them visible in the scene, yet none would register.  Had to wait on the hint multiple times as a result of the lack of Quality Control in the game.
Sometimes there is "mystery meat" navigation where you wave the mouse around willy-nilly looking for something to click on.  Bad design to be sure, but not as bad as I've seen in other games.
OK for fans of the genre, but it's only maybe 4 / 10 score
