Preface: Despite having one of the most horrible launches in video game history, the issues have been fixed and the game is very playable.
Warning: This game has unavoidable major spoilers from past Arkham games. If you are a story purist, Play Asylum, then City, then this game.
Performence: 8/10. My system rundown: fx 8320e (4.2GHz), 8GB Ram, R9 380 4GB, 1TB 72000rpm. On max settings (minus GeForce and AA filters) I got on average 50-70 fps and rarly dipped below 45fps, which is actually awesome considering how much detail and extra fluff they put into this game. It does max the fps out at 90fps, but there are some tutorials online that can help you raise that to 144 or eliminate it entirely. This game will use on average 3GB of Ram (which usually isn't a problem for most people) but never went above 4GB Ram. It uses all 8 of my CPU cores pretty equally. My hard drive holds up pretty nicely considering there are no real abrupt scene changes or cut scenes. However when im crossing a bridge entering a totally new part of the vast city it will do some minor stutters for half a second so an SSD is strongly recommended. My gpu was maxed out the entire time, but there were very few if at all stuttering. However the 4GB VRam is a total must. You could maybe squeek by with 3GB if you turned down the settings a ton, but this game uses up (maxed out) around 3.5 GB of Vram. It also uses 60GB of storage (55GB download with dlc) with all the dlc. Overall it will runs smoothly on most decent systems.
Gameplay/Soundtrack: 9.5/10   This gameplay is the best i've seen/played on any game. Its highly responsive with no animation delay. After a couple hours with this game you will have no trouble manuvouring around in anyway you want. Although a controller is strongly recommended (I used a 360 controller), I used a mouse and keyboard for a couple hours and felt extremely comfortable. Controls are intuitive (although if you've played any other Arkham game with a controller they did move detective vision from LB to dpad up). Grapeling and gliding through the city felt like an experience, rather than a chore as you can smoothly grapel and glide across the city with no dead zones. Upgrades to gadgets are not arbitrary and make you seem like you progress through the game. The batmobile is a little clunky at first, but after a few hours with the game, you get very used to it and know a bit of tricks to make you feel more comfortable. As mentioned before, the game has no major scene changes (totally pausing the game to load a different portion of the map) nor any cinema type cut scenes (like half life 2) which adds to the engagement and fluidity of the game. Some harder combat/preditor moves take time to learn but are overall worth the time to learn. The soundtrack of this game is as usuall by Nick Arundel, amazing. Not as classic as City or Asylums, but still amazing. Off topic, but its great to have on while studying. Overall this game is fluid, intuitive, and pushes you forward in terms of progression.
Graphics/Map: 9/10  The graphics in this game are downright incredible. The map is outright huge with tons of little knooks and crannies to go discover in. Textures are amazing if not passable. The water/rain effects are freaking amazing. Even if the textures were mediocre, just the amount of stuff going on graphically in the city blew me out of the water a couple times. The amount of complexity this game has with the overall design and details is downright astonishing considering how big the map is. Also the water/rain effects. It didn't look like they skimped out on anything. Eveything also looks like it fits and flows with the suroundings and theme of the game. Animations are nice and fluid. Lots of detail went into how the animations looked and how believable they were. And did I mention the water/rain effects? After over 100 hours Im still finding little graphical details that I over looked. Overall the graphics will not disapoint you, even on low settings. Its not battlefront or Crisis calibar, but it takes its own lane graphically.
Story (Ill try not to spill any spoilers) 7/10.  I though the raw story was really really good. Conflicts truely gripped you into the story. Characters you cared about were in truly serious danger. You really got to dig into the heart, mind and conflict of Batman. Character development is well done across the board. Suspense moments are actually worth it and gripping. The villains actually do some damage along the story unlike most games. You feel like Bruce Wayne with a mask on, rather than Batman. However some side missions were really great (Mr Freeze, Perfect crime), but to me most are barely above mediocre. There are only a couple real boss fights in the game (atleast nothing to write home about like Freeze in City or Deathstroke in Origins). Also TOO MUCH FREAKING BATMOBILE MY GOODNESS! AND (minor spoiler) YOU DONT GET TO FIGHT DEATHSTROKE HEAD ON??
Extras (not judging): There are a lot of little challenges throughout the map and of the map that you can challenge yourself to do if you're bored or need some easy Wayne points. They are not required to complete the game, and some of them can be really fun. You can also choose a large variaty of quality Batsuits (holy frick that Batman Beyond skin is frickin amazing) and variaty of batmobiles, even past canon iterations like 1960s and Dark Knight Batmobile. Dlc is pretty good if you can't get enough Batman, but its not required. Get it when its on sale.
TLDR: Fantastic performence, gameplay, main story and graphics. Side missions are great if not OK. Too much freakin Batmobile. Great addition to a top five video game franchise. Would strongly recommend to any since issues have been fixed.
Overall if you love Batman (especially the Arkham franchise), and have the system to run it, I would get this game, especially if its on sale. The season pass can wait if you dont want to spend $16 right out of the gate (it occasionally goes on sale outside the steam summer and winter sale). If you're a story purist, play Asylum, then City (Origins is good, but optional since its more of a prequel), then this game. Its not a absolute must play like Arkham City, Portal or Half Life 2, but I strongly recommend that you give this game a shot.

Note: At the time of typing this review, I only have 45 minutes clocked on it. Thats because ive owned this game since 1999 on N64.
When I was a little kid, all of my friends played either Silent hill or Resident evil. Well, Not me. I played Shadow man. There aren't *tons* of things to say about this game, BUT I'm trying to type as detailed a review as possible, so I'm gonna stretch it out. And I'll just break it down into sections and just say what it does right, and what it does wrong. Story: The game starts off by showing you a cutscene ( None of this is spoiler, it's the first five minutes of the game. ) of Jack the ripper talking to himself, explaining that he's killing women because he's looking for immortality in his murders. ( Figuratively speaking, I assume. ) Suddenly, a man appears in his door and offers him the immortality he seeks. But in a literal sense. Jack asks who the man is, and the man replies with: " My name is legion, for we are many ". He tells Jack that hes aware that he's an architecht. To which Jack confirms it. Legion says he's building an asylum in Deadside ( Hell ), and he wants Jack to work on it. And in return, he will give Jack something that will make him immortal. Dark Souls ( Remember, this was 1999, and it was a comic book before that.) Jack accepts his deal, and upon realising he has to die in order to go to Deadside to work on the asylum, Jack shouts out " FOR WE ARE MANY " before impaling himself through his chest. ( The souls would make him immortal in the real world after hes already died. ) And now the game switches to the main character. You play as Michael LeRoi, the most recent host in the lineage of the Shadow Man. ( If you've ever played "The Darkness", it's comparable to that.) The Shadow Man is an ancient Voodoo warrior, whose able to travel back and forth freely between the world of the living, and the world of the dead. You find out that the asylum has finally been finished in modern day, and its funneling all the dark soul energy from dead side into it. You also find out that five serial killers have each acquired immortality through the souls, and are going on murder sprees on earth. So you have to collect as many souls as you can, Kill the serial killers, and deal with the asylum. Gameplay: It's VERY similar to classic tomb raider. So if youre into that stuff, you'll like this gameplay. Setting: I love the setting in this game. Deadside looks and feels like what I imagine hell would look and feel like. And this is a 1999 game. Hell is where everyone goes in this game. Without exception. And it looks like a place of pain and suffering. Lakes of blood everywhere, People turned into twisted demons, Writhing in pain, Butchers with chainsaws hunting you down, Etc Etc. It looks pretty similar to the Hellraiser movies. If youve ever seen that. Controls: Are awkward. But they work just fine. You walk with the arrow keys, and you use you're weapons with Z and X. Voice Acting: Is really strange. In that it varies. Some characters have AWFUL voice acting, some have decent, and some have really good voice acing. Like Jack the ripper, and the snake, Jaunty. It isn't anywhere near the worst voice acting i've ever heard in a game, but it isn't great either. Graphics: Bad. Not REALLY bad, Just bad. But it's old. Things it does right: It is VERY scary, The gameplay is fun, It's challenging, It has a really good story, Jack and Jaunty have REALLY good voice actors, and it never gets boring, even when you're stuck. Things it does wrong: The graphics, Some characters are very bland ( though only a few ), at least a third of the voice acting sucks, It can ONLY run in window mode if you're using windows 10, but it's actually acceptable window mode. It still fills 80% of the screen, only you have a white bar across the top of the screen. That's it. So it isnt a huge deal. And aside from all of that, It has mildly awkward controls. The Last Point: The most important thing to say about this game, is that holy hell it is extremely hard. It's a huge game, you die very easily, and it has very difficult puzzles. You may need to google or use a guide, and if you arent good at remembering locations betwen game sessions, you may need to google up or even print out a map. In Closing: I loved this game as a kid. And even as an adult today, I still kinda like it. So while their ARE other games that are worth alot more for your Five bucks, If youre looking for a classic game, or a new horror game, there's really no reason to not pick this game up. It's scary, It's cheap ( especially if you get it for $1.25 on sale like I did. ), and it's long. Fun for horror fans, puzzle fans, and fans of the classics. Alot of people call this game mediocre, and while I CAN see why they feel that way, I disagree. I think its above average. And I think saying " OH I COULD JUST BUY RESIDENT EVIL 2 OR SILENT HILL 1 INSTEAD " is a poor arguement. If you like those games, there's no reason to not try this game as well. This is a pretty good cult classic horror game. 7/10.

Shadow Man is a great game that is very atmospheric and creepy. The gameplay consists of platforming, combat and exploration.
It's a very unique game and in my opinion, very underrated.
You are the Shadow Man who is a voodoo warrior walker between Liveside, which is our own world and Deadside, which is the resting place for those who have died. An evil demon assembles a team of serial killers called The Five and begins the construction of an army to take over Liveside and you're on a quest to stop him.
It follows the same sort of structure as games which were out at the time like Tomb Raider or Legend Of Zelda. You must adventure through Temples to gain items that help you progress throughout the game. There is a lot of collectible items that can give you advantages as you play through the story.
This game is very dark and almost has a gothic edge to its world. It's great value for your money (which is already pretty cheap, even cheaper when sales come around) with the game being packed with content and also offering hours of gameplay.
There is some small issues with the game in terms of the controls being very awkward (I'd recommend a gamepad as it would probably be easier) and even though I haven't had the issue of compatibility with my PC, others have.
If you can look past the dated graphics (give it a break, it's from 1999) and the slighty awkward controls, you're in for a treat. Plus, as mentioned before, it's extremely cheap in the sales and also, you get the cracking soundtrack for free. I'd strongly recommend this game.

Zombies and Parkour. One of the best new matchups I've seen in a game. When I first heard about Dying Light over a year ago, not only was I excited at the gameplay but also the possibilities and potential that this game has.  Now with it being finally released I was hoping to see that the game promised on what it would deliver... and it really did.
You can definitely see the Devs inspiration throughout the game, taking focus from Left for Dead, Far Cry and (obviously) Dead Island. Personally I could not believe the difference that this game gave me within the first few hours to the rest. To start off with I felt a bit.... A bit like I wanted to run before I could jump (in terms of Parkour) I didn't have the moves and it would take me forever to run around and scale across buildings. I was slow, low on energy and useless with weapons. It would take me from anywhere between 6-10 hits to kill a zombie, going through my stamina bar twice before eventually dislodging the undead brain. Towards the start of the game I was dreading that this was what the game was like - but further on when you learn the ranking system and start to level up and earn points to redeem skill.... it is like a completely different game. It is absolutely fantastic and a breath of fresh air for anyone that wanted to experience the zombie gamestyle again but with a different slant.
Character progression is excellent in the game, and im happy to say that I was fairly pleased with the way that the story went - but more so impressed with the optional missions/side quests in the game, for me this is where the game shines. Very interesting and a diverse range of different challenges await. Alongside all these positivities are some negatives - noticeably the fact that in Harran you will see a certain head model put on 25% of the people throughout the game (you all know who Im talking about!) and the fact that some parts to the story are extremely predictable and a bit tedious.
Dying Light is gorgeous, there are many moments where you just want to stop what you are doing and appreciate the environment - the sun rays, the shadows, the change of weather... it really is nice. Just make sure to check your back before you do though as Harran is littered with the undead! Before game patches came out I had to manually edit the files to Dying Light to remove parts that I didn't like, the film grain being my main gripe. Now though its nice to see the Devs listening to the community and seeing what they want - now there is an option to remove film grain in game settings.
Melee, dismemberment, blood, screams, satisfying? More than ever before. The first few hours of the game I felt like a fat slob that had never attempted to swing for anyone in his life, shortly afterwards through level progression I was becoming more and more the ultimate ninja warrior that I knew I could be one day! Delicately carving up zombies with a variety of highly modified & rare weapons. Maybe use my electrified sledgehammer to take out the knee caps? then move to my Korek Machete to aggressively perform facial deconstruction? Sure why not. Through a variety of weapons and equipment there always seems to be fun around every corner in this game.
So much more to talk about but I tend to leave my reviews at a similar level of depth, the last thing I wanted to mention was that Co-op with this game is an absolute blast and I would recommend all newcomers to give this option a go. The availability of drop in drop out with up to 4 people makes it really easy too. You can simply toggle your game to "Public" and within moments  you will see people looking for games and coming in to join your fight.
Overall, really pleased with how this game has started and its provided me with so many hours of entertainment. I am looking forward to DLC to continue my Dying Light experience. Its rare to find a game that can mix different genre's so successfully but through this combination of horror and action, Dying Light is a solid recommendation from me and a great base for future games in the series.

Interesting game that's otherwise plagued with technical issues, least of which being the inexplicable 30FPS and 1080p cap. I also had to replay the first mission about 5 times because it kept crashing on the first level transition.
Combat is very similar to Dynasty Warriors 8, only without the satisfaction that comes from levelling entire armies. There's no passive lock-on like you would experience in other character action games, so manually locking on is a necessity when fighting one-on-one, otherwise you are liable to miss your opponent entirely, or slide past them halfway through a combo. Normally that wouldn't be a problem, but you need to hold the lock on button for a second or two before it will actually lock onto an enemy, and there's no way to quickly switch between targets (at least that I've found).
I wasn't able to get very deep into the other mechanics of the game (see above with the crashing issues) but I suspect they are quite simplistic. Koei Techmo has a habit of making interesting gameplay mechanics, but not taking them far enough (looking at you, Empires).
Overall, I doubt this game would be worth the full price, even if it ran properly on PC. I wouldn't recommend it until the technical problems are fixed and the game goes on sale.

It really is a decent enough game, if a bit misled and misleading in terms of what genre it is or tries to be.
With the long expositary texts, its character creation tool ripped straight from the tabletop rpg roots of the licence and the turn-based combat system that plays in an isometric view, you would swear to your own grandma that it is a role playing game. It looks like it, has the same overal mechanics, and vibe to it. But really, it feels more like a point&clic adventure game.
First of, the game is really fixed on one story to tell. Though it is a pretty cool story, filled with nice enough dialogues, there is no exploration here. Not only the places you go are small in scale and practically free from interactions almost all the time: you can't visit building except if the story leads you there, you can't search for stuff, loot etc, or even random fights, anything to just interact with this world, except when the games needs you to do something. Not only that, but there is no side-quest to speak of, except maybe two that I found out afterwards while searching on forums about branching paths in the main quest.
The other problem is that it doesn't seem that your type of character really matters much. To be fair, I played in "normal" which felt a bit like an "easy mode". I made a character around charisma and intelligence, and not really combat, and though I lost few encounters, I never felt really in danger of being blocked by the combat. Even though the game often forces you into it. And that is the other gripe I have with it: it's not really an rpg in the sense of creating a character that solves problems a certain way. Most of the time, whatever I said, it felt like it didn't matter except for the "role playing" in the sense of speaking like my character would spoke. And certain capacity, like the "security" bonus for dialogues, felt like they were much more useful than others.  And it is a pretty short game too (didn't re-finished it on Steam though).
But you know what? It still is a nice and enjoyable game to boot. The aesthetic is nice, the music is cool. The story and characters if not absolutely memorable do there job find. And I had a good time playing it overall. I recommand it! Just know that you are not in the path of a Fallout 2, and more in a pretty linear straight forward point&clic with combat game.

Even with all the day 1 bugs that will be fixed in a matter of a week, this is the only globally released monster hunting RPG in existence for PC, so pay that price and be happy.
Seriously though, the game runs smoothly, plays amazingly, and is as challenging as the monster hunter franchise.
You will notice that 30fps =/= 30fps because you are probably used to "30 fps" meaning that the game will run at 30 frames per second and below. Which it doesnt, its completely fluently capped at the framerate, so me as a guy who has a 144hz monitor would actually say that my modded skyrim @45~ fps runs actually worse than Toukiden: Kiwami.
The price seems absolutely justified to me, even if i had to pay in pounds or whatever the heck currency you want me to pay in. Far as im concerned i will play this game for hundreds of hours and will get my moneys worth no matter what.
In terms of direct comparison to MH, this game has more exciting bosses once you are around 5 hours into the game. The first boss you get that you could qualify as a fire breathing wyvern (to compare to i.e. rathian or qurupeco) turns into a lanky kong-esque mantis with fireflower powerup that slings around its arms and makes fire rain all around it while dancing when down to 1/3 of its health. And pretty much all the bosses afterwards do these ridiculous transformations once their HP gets below a certain threshold, which really makes the fights epic in comparison to MH uhhh, making the mobs simply faster and perhaps give them one or two special attack patterns while raging they wouldnt use when calmed down.
The game also scraps the tedium of carrying a varied assortment of pickaxes, bug nets and what the hell just to crunch the RNG because you need whatevertheheck ore to craft that one cool equipment set. Instead you pick up shiny sparkly lights that are easy to find in each area, and thats as far as collecting materials goes.
The weapons are also very fun to play and you also are free to use any weapons right from the get go without limiting your progress speed (i am looking at you, bowgun). No need to pay for ammo or all that crap that makes being a ranged character a complete pain in the monster hunter universe. This game streamlines everything that needs to be streamlined, and thats great.
Also the soundtrack is great.

I'll be honest here. Just listen.
Antichamber was a game that I found by accident. Saw the trailer and was "Oh my it looks so cool!"
But then, the puzzles started to become dificult, I reached dead ends and quickly became frustrated.
The only reason I played it again was because I payed for it, so I was going to finish it.
And it was worth it.
Playing this with my mind open made me realize that it's more than just a game with blocks and puzzles.
It's a game with puzzles, blocks, and challenges. Challenges that made my brain work on them for days to reach a solution that was so simple that I became embarrassed.
Those "tips" could be used in real life too, and I wonder if the developers did it on purpose.
But anyway, I spent too much time trying to reach some things that weren't supposed to be reached the way I was trying.
This game is about that "ooh!" moment, the spark of a new idea generating in the brain as a new solution is revealed to the players.
When I finally reached the end, I was happy. I felt like I completed a challenging quest and... It's over.
I'm not kidding when I say that it made me look a the world with different eyes.
Opening the game again and seeing all those images flashing before my eyes brought a smile that said: "It was worth it."
To close this, I'm putting one sentence from the game: "We can appreciate the entire journey by looking back at how far we have come."
yeah, I really recommend this game! :D

After replaying this game in its various different iterations, be they hl2:update, cm2013 and the original over and over again, I can still not understand what makes this game so special.
I thought it might be the storyline, but that seems to be nothing particularly complicated - in fact,
I considered that it might be the gameplay: The gravity gun allows so much interaction with the world that you become a part of it, but the fact is that that weapon is only available after several hours of game, and I enjoyed the time before as much as the time after.
The aspect which stuck with me the longest was the art style - hl2 is probably the most amazing visual experience to be had in a game, surpassed only maybe by Bioshock Infinite. It has fairly low detail textures and models, but everything is designed to work together to create amazing atmosphere and immersion.
No, the thing that makes hl2 special is not something so solid. This game is refined and perfected to such an extent that most fpses made since have tried to mimic its character, and most have failed. Even so, it is not perfect - the start of the game may be it a bit long for those with a short attention span, the first boss fight is just way too hard, and it definitely isn't the right game for everyone.
But hl2 is a world, with character, with beauty, (and with the best reflections evaaaaaaa) and if you play it, you become part of that world. The special bit of hl2 is that it feels real.
I could not recommend this game enough.

The Arkham series will always hold a special place in my heart, Asylum was a genre defining game with a superb beat em up style that marks the beginning of a great franchise, City improves upon the first game in every way imaginable and has a kicker of a story to boot, Origins offers a strong cast of villains and highly memorable boss battles. With the release of Arkham Knight, fans of the franchise are expecting a proper sendoff to the Arkham franchise, did it deliver?
For the most part it did, the game looks absolutely stunning and plays incredibly smooth without any problems whatsoever, granted I played this game over a year after its horrendous launch plagued by a myriad of bugs and crashes, among other issues. But after the updates, the game has little to no bugs whatsoever. You can tell that Rocksteady put all their hearts into the creation of this game, every bit of Gotham is brimming with detail and feels colorful despite the dark and gritty undertone of the game itself. Character models are beautifully designed and the voice acting from each character are superb. Despite all its positives, most people found the game to not be a proper sendoff to the Arkham series as it did not meet their expectations. Why?
For starters, my main gripe about this game is the heavy emphasis on the bat mobile, sure it’s fun to drive every once in a while, but the game shoves it at your face every 15 minutes and create stupidly complex scenarios that requires you to use the bat mobile. For example,
These are just a couple of examples of the stupid scenarios the game puts you in. This brings me to the next problem the game has, memorable boss battles, because the game doesn’t have any. This is a huge disappointment since we got the terrifying Killer Croc battle in Asylum and creative Mr. Freeze battle in City. Boss battles either involve you doing beat em ups with another character or employs the use of the bat mobile, it isn’t fun and definitely not memorable, heck, there isn’t even a final boss battle which imo is really disappointing. The next problem the game has is the lack of a character arc, the only one worth mentioning is Batman’s, which is okay, but this means the rest of the characters get set aside. What made the villains in Asylum and City so memorable is that they have character arcs and interesting side quests that gets you to learn more about them, side missions in this game are the same missions over and over that leads to a boss battle that leads to Batman putting them in jail, end of story.
In conclusion, the game is fun and plays well if you’re just looking to play as Batman, but if you have been a fan of the Arkham series like I’ve been; the game falls short, but is an okay sendoff to the beloved Arkham series.

I initially gave this game a negative review, because I could not get it to run, but I thankfully eventually did, and in terms of gamplay, and the story with scarecrow (not the arkham knight as the villain) it has become my favorite arkham game. The title here is once again "be the batman" and let me tell ya, when you get past the drone tank sections this game delivers on its slogans promise. Arkham Knight by far has the best mechanics out of the entire series, with arkham origins right behind it. If you cannot get this game to work simply troubleshoot it, select the option where it won't launch, or run correctly, and select windows 8 for compatibility mode. Worked the first time for me on my new laptop, but it might be because my hardware is strong enough to not be bothered by the terrible optimization of the game. My laptop is an asus fx53 with a gtx 1050 and 12 gb of ram. Once again, this title will not dissapoint in terms of gameplay, and graphical fidelity. All in one title Arkham Knight gives us the batman games that we have always dreamed of, providing us with the skins of each installments batmobile, iconic sounds, animations, and character costumes. I know that the season pass has recieved a lot of flack for having extremely short content, but its worth it just for the skins alone. You can purchase the skins seperately which I highly suggest doing, because the price is still too much for the length of each mission. BUT I will also say that if you simply search the free roam mod and ALL batmobile and character skins unlocked on Youtube you will find multiple videos where people have linked their season pass content in their descriptions and you can easily download it via dropbox, one drive, or google drive. Yes, its that easy to recieve all the skins for EVERY character from all the films, and all the batmobiles. Follow the instructions on how to download them, because those are seperate videos in their descriptions. I can honestly say, despite how much the arkham knight is shoved into the campaign you can just ignore him entirely. The real conflict happens between batman, the city, the gcpd, the (SPOILER SPOILER SPOILER)-----------------------------------------------------------------------Joker (inside of Batmans concious via the toxin, and jokers infected blood from arkham city,) and the scarecrow that wants to cover gotham in fear gas. When you reach the end of the campaign and you play through the final section that is stories high point. You truly see Batman for who he is and its a wonderful representation that has pleased many fans, including myself. Even though we FINALLY get to play in gotham city its a shame that Rocksteady and WB for some reason decided to lazily have the city evacuated AGAIN, because if their were citizens, other than just the police officers, we would have more motivation to protect them, and defeat the criminals. Walking around as Batman and being greeted, hated on by citizens, and interacting with them, such as in the spider man games, would have been very fun to see. Overall I believe this game is at a fair price for the amount of content that you recieve, but its unfortunate, and truly unacceptable that Rocksteady and WB have completely abandoned this game since their last patch. Yes, I know they are working on Shadow Of War, but for many the optimization is not allowing them to get past the slash screen, let alone play the game. I hope they have learned their foolish mistake and that they never trust any smaller companies with their future ports.

XCOM: Enemy Unknown is a very well-made game and stays quite true to the original XCOM games. The first thing to note is that the visuals are very good. It makes the aliens looks very threatening and the fully decked out soldiers look "badass".
The strategy part of the game is very well done in a way that makes you think where your soldiers should go and whether or not it is worth any of the risk. This is even more apparent on harder levels with harder aliens and soldiers dying more easily. The "Ant-farm" look of the XCOM base is very intriguing and is more simpler than the old XCOM (in a good way).
However, there was a point which could be improved upon which are the hangars having more use in the game. I found that the hangar had little to no use to me until later in the game where it was more important but apart from that, I never really thought about doing anything in the hangar.
XCOM: Enemy Within is a brilliant expansion to the XCOM Universe as it spices things up and makes it more interesting with the introduction of Genetic Manipulation in soldiers and mechanizing your soldiers as well. The Mechtoid is a formidable opponent towards the MEC troopers and was enjoyable to fight against.
In conclusion, XCOM: Enemy Unknown is a worthy successor to the XCOM series in a strategic standpoint and is worth your time and money. The visuals are great, the combat and strategy is tense most of the time and the expansion is refreshing and adds more interesting content to the original game. The hangars were not a major part of the game and was quite boring to do any of the swapping of the weaponry. Either way, if you're a strategy game fan, this isworth your time and money, go buy it.

A great game but has a really poorly designed questing system which forces the player into loading/reloading dungeons countless number of times in order to get rare drops in order to synthesis stones to complete rank quests, these quests are extremely grindfest and incredibly frustrating especially if you get unlucky with crappy RNG, and to make matters worse these Collector Quests just get worse as you rank up,  Rank C is pretty bad - I shudder to think how bad Rank B and A will be,  but these shouldn't be designed this way - Compile Heart you disappoint me here,  you're better than this to throw in a really unnessary grindfest in order to progress your questing.
Some stones are somewhat 'easy' to find with Item Sonar as they as the potential areas are close to the entrance, like with the ice cave so the re-loading of the dungeon isn't so bad, but other dungeons on the other hand, the hidden treasure could be far away and that takes a significant amount of time finding the hidden treasure, and thats even 'assuming' its not a useless sprout inside.    Basically, if there is a DLC or any cheat/feature that clearly displays the hidden treasure on the map immediately without having to use item sonar, then this is clearly NEEDED in order to keep your sanity after your 1000th dungeon reload and you still haven't gotten your stupid stones yet.
Clearly, this quest system just doensn't work very well at all, and unfortunately this heavily impacts the games fun factor once the tedium sets in.  Compile Hearts, please do not do this again with future releases - stick with the tried and tested methods that worked with the HDN series.
As for the rest of the game, I haven't had any issues - everything else is good.  Good characters,  good story lines with humorous dialogue and the voice acting is up to high standards.   The graphics and drawing are on par with the HDN series.
Whilst I honestly enjoy the game, and story - I just can't get past the mistakes made with the quest system, and thats the only - repeat ONLY reason for the not recommend review.   *IF* you don't mind a more hardcore approach to grinding and farming, especialy farming for stones so you can synthesis then you will enjoy Fairy Fencer F,  if your like me and have no patience at all these days for farming and/or get easily frustrated then I would do more research first before buying into this game.
Closing statements here is that the worst problems that Fairy Fencer F suffers from are insane grinds require for portions of the game, especially in farming for stones and stealing quest items which have a very very low success rate.   Another minor issue is that halfway though the game, the difficulty unusually spikes with monsters doing alot more damage, plus you'll face more in battles + boss battles get more intense, I'll not reveal anymore information on this because it'll potentially spoil it for anyone reading, but the spike feels like it wasn't tested enough and makes an already grindy game, feel even more grindy.
Alot of content is also highly missable, such as recruiting extra characters which first time around, is more or less impossible and really aimed at NG+ so expect to play through multiple times in order to unlock alot of the extras.  Finally, if anyone doesn't believe me about the drop rates being really bad - just check the forums yourself and read all the posts regarding this - Don't take accept anyone saying that they are 'fine' because they are clearly not.
Whilst reading through my review and reading through peoples responses, I think I came off as highly critical.  I make no real apologies here since everyone has their own right to post how they feel about any game they play, whether its a hateful comments or because they just really love the game and cannot stand any negativity.  However,  I think I was wrong to give this game a 5/10 and I will admit, that was a mistake - however, my previous statements I will still standby them.

This is a simple game.  Push right to move clockwise and left to move counterclockwise.  However, it's a difficult one to master.  There are six levels in Super Hexagon.  Each level is very challenging and requires practice to navigate the traps that will fly towards you.  You will need to learn to look towards the edge of the screen to see what is coming next while also looking at the center of the screen to guide your triangle away from death.
What puts Super Hexagon above other similar games is how addictive it is to play "just one more round".  Beating a level takes a lot  of practice, but only takes 60 seconds to count as a victory.  Restarting a level only takes pushing a button and you're right back in the game.  This combination of short levels and quick restarts greatly reduces its frustration factor and teaches the player to practice, practice, and practice more to learn the tricks and traps in each level and finally hit that minute mark.  Once you do pass a stage, you will have that feeling of accomplishment.  This feeling seems to be missing from other, more complex games which makes Super Hexagon a great experience.
The feeling of progression is also stronge here.  At first you will die within seconds of starting the first stage.  It'll be hard to judge what the game is going to throw at you and how much to move left and right to safely dodge the obstacles.  With repeated attempts, you will begin to last for 5 seconds, 10 seconds, 20 seconds, and on and on until you finally reach that minute mark and beyond.  Even after you think you have reached your peak skill, you may set a new personal record that will surprise you.  Super Hexagon trains your brain and hands to react immediately and the improvement over time is noticable.
The music is another highlight for the game.  The soundtrack consists of three chiptune tracks by the artist Chipzel.  All three are very catchy and add to the game's style.  One great detail about the music is every time you restart a level, the song starts at a different part.  This is a great feature since you will be restarting many, many times and listening from the the beginning of a song would get annoying really fast.
For a few bucks, it is worth it.  Even better if you get it on sale.  Also grab the mobile version for when you're on the road.

Currently, there are a large number of problems with the game. It is a direct PS4 port, which means the keyboard and mouse support is non-existent. If you want fluid gameplay on the PC, you'll need to find a way to use a console gamepad on the PC. The online game play has its own problems, monsters are out of sync with other players, more often than not you will see your allies swinging mindlessly at nothing. You will only experience this problem if you can even find an online lobby.
There is no communication options with other players besides pre-set messages that you have to scroll through a menu for. If you are lucky enough to have an enjoyable time experience this game in a random lobby with other players, there is no options to add fellow Slayers on Steam. In addition to this, the online game hub is very limited, it's a message board room where you can pick up missions, quests, and change equipment. If you want to do any sort of gear upgrade, you must leave the online lobby into single player mode to craft items. You risk losing your place with a possibly very good Slayer party.
There is no way of playing with friends on your Steam friends list, unless you live close enough to one another and you just happen to find the other person's lobby when searching online. I tested this with a friend of mine from Hong-Kong and it was not going to happen. We created games with passwords, and there was no way of finding or joining one another's lobbies.
There are, however, positives, not many, but they are there. The game is fun if you can get into a lobby with other fellow Slayers who know what they are doing and are competent. The 30 frame-rate cap is not as big of a problem as all people are making it out to be, the game is pretty, the 30 frames is very playable. The removal of the cap would be a huge improvement for the experience though.  The gameplay is nice and polished, no graphical glitches, no gameplay glitches thus far.
For $60, and the immensely poor optimization, the game is not worth your money. Save your money until the game is patches and fixes these basic issues. Considering that it is not playable as a PC port, I will not recommend this game to anyone as of yet.
I will recommend this game to the die hard fans out there looking for a Monster Hunter equivalent on PC. If you have a console game controller and know how to use it with your PC, definitely give it a go, the game is fully playable with a console controller. If you have any questions about the actual gameplay or would like to see the game play, feel free to drop by my twitch stream at
. Hope this review was helpful, and happy hunting!

OK, get past the XCOM Purist arguments, this game is fun!  It is fun, if infuriatingly difficult at the upper levels of difficulty.  Oh yes, it is FUN.  XCOM: Enemy Unknown is a rendition that pays tribute to the X-COM franchise that was released in the 1990's.  It was not trying to be a total remake, but instead was a very good game that blends elements of the original into a more modern short-attention span version. I have not played the Enemy Within DLC yet, so this review is based on the original version with the first few DLC's, including Slingshot, Second Wave, and the Elite Soldier pack.
I love tactical turn-based squad combat games.  I played the original X-Com series all the way through probably 3-4 times each, and still have it loaded on my machine despite the many upgrades and transfers. (It was one of a few games that made me learn how to tweak Dos-Box.)  I like letting the original game run in real time mode in the background while I go about doing real work.  Back to X:EU, I really like the 3D environments, and the obvious references to the originals.  The base layout was a bit goofy initially, but I got used to it, and eventually I pretty much ignored it.  Sadly the bases were one of my favorite things to plan in the original.  I liked second wave options specifically for dealing with rookies, giving me a far more challenging variance when the team went out.  I understand why you can only get up to 6 squaddies, but 14 would be awesome!  However with 2 snipers, 3 assaults and a support, my teams mostly dominated especially in the end game with a fully psionic squad.  It was always fun to capture the first little squad of aliens and run them through the map to draw fire. (Made stocking up on weapons easy and cheap!)  I liked the cover based tactics, when they worked, and did enjoy the plot.  I was trying to envision what the game would feel like to someone who had never played the originals and did not know the progression of the plot.
I did not like three main things.  First, the difficulty levels were drastically different, Normal is almost a joke.  Classic is frustrating, and feels VERY much like the original.  Impossible requires the patience of Job.  The Ironman option is not for the faint of heart. Ironman Impossible is completely nuts, and having started several games of this that I then blew on one mission early on, will require restarting often.  I would like a challenge between normal and Classic, maybe Veteran, to bridge the huge jump in the challenge.  This challenge translates into what I hate, in that if your soldiers panic, they are likely to shoot each other.  If you create panic in the aliens, they are likely to shoot you guys too.  Therefore panic is BAD, and the higher the difficult the more likely for panic.  Second, several of the levels have really bad tracking for the placement of your cursor.  The harvester level and two of the cityscape levels specifically have areas you can't go, or even see into, but you enemies can sit on an upper level and snipe at you.  At least let me target the aliens who are in those areas.  Third, the cover seems to be non-existent for a few levels.  The fountain in the office courtyard made me furious, when I was shot and criticaled in a I/I level from behind two walls and full cover where it took me 2 full movement turns to take my survivors to surround him, while he picked off my guys each round.  The rooftop construction level may as well not have any cover, I don't think that the aliens ever missed my guys if they were on high ground, even when they were no where near line of sight.  My only real grief is the losses that occur due to the control problems in the interface.
Over all this is definitely a good game, and worth purchasing and playing several times.  A run through on classic difficulty was very challenging and made the end quite satisfying.

Shadowrun Returns is a first installment of the Shadowrun Returns trilogy (followed by Dragonfall and concluded by Hong Kong).
A kickstarter success, the project led by Jordan Weisman, the creator of the Shadowrun tabletop role-playing game met its funding goal of $400,000 within 28 hours. The game ultimately had gathered $1,895,772.
The first installment in the series comes with one story campaign called “the dead man switch” - which takes about 12 hours to complete. The story itself consists of two distinctive parts: first 4 to 5 hours you're tracking down a serial killer, and the rest 7-8 hours you are fighting crazy doomsday cult. The story concludes with you stopping the invasion... of giant spiritual bugs representing ancient evil. Sigh.
The combat is weak too- it is extremely slow, repetitive and plain stupid. The only saving grace is that no predetermined class approach guaranties a lot of freedom in character building (same goes for roleplaying as well).
Honestly, the story and combat are pretty weak, but that's not the point. The point- SR R is a prologue, first act, exposition if you will, to one of the best game trilogies in recent years. It misses on story and combat, but it menages to create a feel, to add some context and to set a stage to the amazing second act (Dragonfall), and good third act (Hong Kong)
So in conclusion- if you have some time to spare- start at the beginning, and play Shadowrun Returns first, before attempting Dragonfall or Hong Kong. If you don't- go for the Dragonfall and Hong Kong, you cant afford to miss them. They are THAT good.
P. S. If you re playing Shadowrun Returns first, then lower your expectations and remember 2 simple things: firstly- its an introduction of the setting, and secondly- it gets better with second and third games in the series.
P.P.S. While tracking down serial killer, you come across a suspicious and creepy man at the crime scene. He' s mumbling something about how he loves to strangle kittens and that his mother never loved him. "Leave him" says the game, we still have 10-12 hours to investigate these strange murders.
10 out of 10, would investigate strange murders again.

If you're reading this sometime before the 25th of November, 2014, grab Teleglitch free from Humble Bundle.
This game is hard. As in "taking your hard-earned progress, spitting on it, stealing your bombs, sticking them near you, blowing your face into the ground, laugh at you" hard. And yet it's a ton of fun, provided it is your cup of tea. If it isn't, there's not much of a chance that you'll like it. And I love it.
Teleglitch: Die More Edition is a top-down twin-stick shooter with roguelike elements. These elements materialize in the form of pseudo-random map generation, random item placement, basic crafting, and brutal permadeath. The high difficulty doesn't help. It pulls in the control scheme from it's twin-stick counterparts, using the W A S D keys + the mouse for movement and aiming, respectively. It obviously is in real-time, unlike roguelikes.
The art, while not perfect, is very good, and very nicely accents the themes the game was going for. It's pixeled, but there appear to be several layers of textures, so that the game is not just a grid. When you fire your guns, there's a neat lighting effect that happens to distort the environment; makes it feel like you're really ripping space apart. Teleglitch uses a simple but incredibly effective point-of-view system that hides areas of the environment that would logically be out of view and keeps the player guessing what's around the next corner. My only complaint with the lighting system is that it is rather easy to exploit it a bit to find secrets, but I shan't diverge how it is done here. I also wish that the colors were a bit more varied.
The music is mostly atmospheric, which fits the theme quite nicely. There's really not much for me to say here. The sound for the guns and bombs fits well; not too wimpy or loud. If you're concerned about preserving the theme while you play, you won't want to use music. Otherwise, go ahead and play your tunes if you want to.
There's a nice selection of weapons and items available, guns, bombs, medicine, etc. Much of what you get you have to craft. The crafting system is simple, effective, and (most importantly) usable in the middle of combat. (If you can keep your focus) The amount of ammo you get for your guns is balanced well enough. You never feel as if you have too much, or that you were given much too little. Usually, when you run out of ammo, there were playing techniques you could have used to avoid it. One of my personal favorites is the cangun; useful for clearing a corridor.
Now, with permadeath, there has to be a reason to keep playing. The most notable reason to keep playing is the pseudo-random level generation. It appears that the game has a database of rooms and corridors, and strings these together to create a playable level. Then, secret areas, items, and monitors are placed in the level. The theme is usually the same in the same level, such as the Algae pits for level 2b, but it feels coherent and gives the impression of roaming around in a military complex. Note that some rooms have the Teleglitch in them. I'll leave it to you to figure out what it does and how to deal with it.
Summary: I heavily reccomend this game. It has an excellent mix of shooter and roguelike. That said, there are people from both genres who won't like it. If you don't want the pain of losing all your progress forever, or if the randomness just isn't something you'd like, or if the hectic combat just makes you lose your cool, you may want to consider other options.

I bought this game when it was $4.99 on a winter sale the year before last. Never got into it, or really finished it until this year. However that may be, do not be fooled. This is a great game within itself. Albeit single-player, it did not need to jump on the multiplayer bandwagon for many reasons, and if that turns you off, believe me when I say, buy this game.
Ever want to know how it is to be a parkour ninja badass? This would be a rather accurate representation of that. The gameplay is smooth, while I did find myself lost at times, I merely had to change my perspectives to advance in levels. At only 5 or so hours of gameplay, it delivered everyone hour I spent with more than I hoped for. Every dollar was worth it to be a ninja parkour badass.
If that's not enough, the worlds are stylistically and beautifully crafted. Vibrant colors that games like Gears of War could take a number from. Green, blue, red, yellow, magenta, cyan. It has its dull colors, sure, but all games need that. Whatever the case may be, running through this world feels lovely, and the colors merely reflect it in ways that I find aren't located in many other games.
I wasn't big on its story, but then, I skipped most of it. Allow me to play the unbiased party and say that because it didn't really grab me, or because I skipped most of the cutscenes, they probably weren't all that interesting. That's understandable though, because really I used that $5 to be a ninja. Just like I'd pay $40 to buy Monster Hunter to fight monsters, or $15 to travel the galaxy in Starbound. The story might have been amazing, and I won't doubt it. It just didn't grab me.
The music did. At least, I think so. Nothing felt more badass to me than getting pumped running from those cops, jump kicking them, punching them for their gun, shooting them then the soundtrack. Soundtracks usually are one of the big three for me, along with story and gameplay, and with that, it helped the gameplay tremendously... I also might have been playing too much Payday 2 at the time, and the soundtracks could have been intermixed. So I may not be too credible in that regard. But believe my when I say, I enjoyed the notes played when I played this game.
All in all. I give this game a 8.7 out of 10. Definitely worth the purchase.

Concise and straight to the point: this game is great, but I'm going for a negative review.
Why?
Well, it costs 2€, and it is the SAME game ripped off from Kongregate, where you can play it for free (it's called Vampire Physics there by the way).
I'm going a little bit into the details in reviewing this game, but I'm gonna keep the judgement negative since I'm playing something that I paid for and that I have already played lots of time being a 10-years Kongregate/Flash user.
This game is one of those cut the rope/physics Flash games, and in this case you'll control a vampire and you'll have to touch the humans in order to turn them into vampires; you'll have to cut ropes, time the cutting of the wooden blocks and so on even 'cos you'll have priests (here with some asset change but anyways) that will kill you and of course garlic to avoid, plus the moon which will cover/uncover and trasform werewolves and other things you'll get in the game in case you'll buy it!
The game itself is nice; graphics look a little bit too "mobile-phone" but overall the physics and everything else runs ok.
But it's the same free game that eight years ago three developers freely created for Kongregate and other websites.
I don't know if these developers on Steam have only copied the asset, bought it, made graphics changes and so on - they added a translation which is full of errors from the first phrase both in Italian and French - but anyways, I'm feeling a little bit angry since I don't think it's ok to rip off completely a game that you can play for free on Flash websites with only changes in the graphics and little things here and there.
Back to the game, as I said you'll have lots of levels in which your vampire head/ball will have to touch all the humans and it will require some skills and timing, it's a very nice kind of puzzle/logic game.
But really, since the developers are completely different and it seems that here on Steam they just ported an asset and left everything as you can play for free, I would suggest you not to play this game but to go on Kongregate or ArmorGames or wherever you want and play through 50 free levels without spending 2€, since it's exactly the same; same mechanics, same enemies, same puzzles and so on.
I recognize that they have bought the asset from Unity3D and such but many levels are the exact same, just the graphics differs.
It's an unusual review for me since I usually take into account only the Steam experience of a player but 2€ for a game that can be played for free without any kind of difference apart something in the graphics well, it has to be pointed out.
Nothing much to say apart from this, as I said already the game runs smoothly, the physics and the puzzles are nice, there's everything that I already played on Flash lots of years ago. If you buy this you'll surely do a good thing for your gaming experience since it's a nice physics/logic game, but be aware that you can play this entirely for free on other websites and this bothers me a little bit.
Even if it's not against any law (I think, although the levels are literally the same so.. Idk) I don't like that much that you have to pay 2€/$ for something that on another website you can have for free without any other benefit, it doesn't even have trading cards.. so, my negative review is just for everything I tried to explain. The game is good, but it's not for free and it's available for free (legitimately of course, not through emulation or Idk what) under the name Vampire Physics on lots of other websites.. and to be a little bit fussy, this one doesn't even have R for restart as the Flash versions which is something quite mandatory in physics/puzzle games. Anyways, hoping to have made something good as always for other players, keep it up :)

Vampires the game review
By Mitch Larson
On October 7th of 2017 I can safely say that this was quite an enjoyable game.  The mechanics are easy to control and while there is some puzzle elements to the game I was able to complete the entire game in around an hour or two.
The music itself was designed nicely and while it does come on what sounds like a loop, it adds to the atmosphere nicely. The backgrounds are decent and the overall gameplay is fun.  Ever play the game Angry Birds?  The launches aren’t quite like that but it has a similar feel.  The achievements are fairly easy to get and most puzzles are simple if you apply some careful thinking into them.
I did manage to get into a spot here and there and did have to restart the level. The really nice thing about this game is that it does a similar angry birds technique of saving the game between levels.  And thank goodness for that because during my first run play through of it, my steam account unexpectedly closed.  Now I played this on a mac, but it can be played across platforms for more than one operating system.
I was so seriously grateful that the developer of this game had the sense to install a save feature where all my hard earned progress wouldn’t go up in smoke. Thank you, thank you, thank you!  Vampires was a very relaxing game that you can play for the entertainment.  The little design details to the vampire and citizenry was interesting.  The priest design was curious but pleasant to look at.  Vampires is basically where you go around changing people into a vampire all while trying to avoid priests, other vampires and garlic.
So let’s go now to the scores.  In overall design of the game I give the creator a 8.5 out of 10.  In terms of the mechanics of the game (swinging, rolling, and planning) I give the creators a 10 out of 10 for the controls and mechanics.
In terms of music I give the creator a 9 out of 10, it does loop but the ambiance is great.  In terms of overall gameplay replay value I’ll give it a 9 out of 10 because I can seriously see myself playing this game again, and again.
In terms of overall fun factor I give the creator of this game a 10 out of 10 because it was seriously, that much fun to play the first go round.
I would highly recommend this game to other people who enjoy a relaxing, fairly easy game to pass the time.
My final thoughts are that this developer should make more exciting and fun Halloween games and I hope that they do.  Awesome Job!

One of my favourite games from the Nintendo 64 days, damn this takes me back. I played the everloving crap out of it back in the day. You may have never heard of it, but believe it or not, this game was higly anticipated at the time. Then it just seemed to fade away. It got an unsuccesful sequel on the PS2 and then it just died. Shadow Man fell into the unforgiving depths of obscurity and gathered a cult following. It was forgotten, abandoned. And then it suddenly appeared on Steam. I don't know what this could mean, but I'm silently hoping for the comeback that this franchise deserves.
In case you don't know, Shadow Man is an action adventure game that takes elements from Tomb Raider, Zelda, Metroid and Banjo-Kazooie among some others and sprinkles it with a healthy dose of occult horror. Think of it as a 3D metroidvania with collectathon elements. You play as Michael Leroi aka Shadow Man, an immortal voodoo warrior who walks between our world and Deadside. Suffice to say, the apocalypse is nearing and you're the only one who can stop it. You travel across Deadside in search of Dark Souls, dangerously powerful souls that, should they fall into the wrong hands could bring about the end of the world. There's 120 of them scattered across multiple areas, and collecting them is a real treat. The more you get, the more powerful you become, so it's addicting and satisfying. You'll wanna find them all. Along the way there's plenty of platforming and shooting a la Tomb Raider, unearthing special abilities and items that help you progress like in Metroid, top it off with a lot of freedom of exploration, it's like a delicious mix of the best aspects of several different games and I simply adore it.
Downside? Controls are a bit clunky. Precision platforming can be a bit of a hassle when you control like a tank. No free camera movement either. They're not bad, it just takes a while getting used to.
Sadly, I wish they would have done a better job with the port. No steam overlay, and I often see my taskbar and the game's window flickering in and out. I feel like the game is just barely there, that it could automatically minimise at any moment. No true controller support either. You can use an Xbox 360 controller, but it won't recognise the shoulder triggers. It's useable, but you'll have play around with the configuration for a bit. As far as I know, it's quite playable with keyboard and mouse, so there's that. Personally I haven't had the game crash yet, but I've seen other people complain about it.
Shadow Man on Steam isn't as stable as it should be and it doesn't look like it'll be fixed anytime soon. Still, it works for me and it might work for you too. And it's only 5 bucks. Kind of a steal for a game like this. If you're like me and you wanna get your Shadow Man fix but you're too lazy to plug in your N64 (Dreamcast, PS1), well, here ya go! :p

I've always been a fan of card games, but I kind of suck at them. After trying for a while to find an online TCG that I could get behind, I settled on this.
It's like a faster, more competitive, less grindey version of Hearthstone. If that sounds appealing to you, give it a try. Game gives you a ton of rewards when you get started and gives away free stuff frequently.
It has the same netdecking/meta problems all online TCGs have, but at least this game's pretty accessible to players who prefer not to spend money on card packs. Currently Shadowverse seems to be adding new cards sets at an acceptable rate, and even gives away free packs when a new set launches.
If this game has one issue looming in it's future, it might be card rotation. The meta's constantly changing, but as of now the sets don't rotate out so problem decks/cards tend to stick around. If you're serious about ranking then you'll probably appreciate that there is far less RNG in this game than some other TCGs, but you'll probably have a hate list of cards once you wrap your head around current decklists. I suppose that's just an aspect of TCGs in general though so I won't hold it against this game.
The only bad thing I can think to say is that the majority of daily missions aren't completable in practice games against the AI or in story missions. Kind of sucks for people like me who like to build up a card collection before they start playing other people, but the daily rewards, mission completion bonuses, and card pack give aways help ease the pain a bit and give you a respectable card base to work with when you finally decide to dive into online matches.

Speaking of dark, don't hesitate to put some gamma into the game and up the brightness around 10-20% as with how little light there is at times it can make navigating the larger maps more time-consuming than it has to be. - Controls need to be toyed with at the start to get a comfortable K+M setting, and even then the mouse can be a little sensitive/ receiving conflicting commands leading to some involuntary movements, but when you need precision, you can always leave the turning to your left and right arrows, while keeping a contemporary WASD movement for general application.

Dying light is a bunch of things crammed into one game.  It's a good zombie horror game.  It's a great urban apocalypse exploration game - some of my favorite bits involved just poking around the odd bits and pieces of Harran.  It's a pretty good parkour game - not really my cup of tea, but still very good.
The game is a hell of a lot of fun to play - the day/night sequences were great, and I loved the atmospheric thrill of staying out after dark, making a bit too much noise, and then running like hell from the volatiles.  (Or, on one fantastic night mission, finding one spot where I could brutally killify a pack of them with grendades.  Good times.)  The side quests are often clever, quirky, and challenging.
I have two issues with the game.  The first has to do with the main plot.  It's terrible.  I'd've kicked it into a wall of spikes if I could have, then tossed a grenade on it.  Cliche villain... scenes that take control away from the player at crucial moments... lost inventory mechanics in a game that relies on crafting and inventory management... and a general feeling that the story missions were completely on rails, and perhaps outsourced to an entirely different company.  I had to grit my teeth and force myself to do the story missions - they're so bad that they aren't even really funny-bad, just plain bad.
The other issue is much smaller - the crafting system is interesting, but resource scarcity never seems to be an issue.  Perhaps I'm just a compulsive collector, but I ended the game with 100 of every item that I ever used (or more) and parts to make many dozens more.  It'd be more interesting if resources were actually fairly scarce.  I'm a little dubious about the idea of stores in the apocalypse, but at a minimum I'd've liked to see fewer.
Also - please don't make me manually climb a radio tower when you've already given me a grappling hook... or tell me, on a story mission, that I'm "too tired" to use it... thereby forcing me to jump and climb and crawl for ten minutes.  The parkour is fun... random Mario jumping puzzles... less fun.
This game is still awesome after 15 years.

Shadowman is an action adventure released in 1999. And the age shows. It's not the most beautiful game by today's standards and it suffers an issue most early 3D games suffered: wonky camera controls. The controller support isn't amazing (I couldn't map the triggers of my Xbox 360 controller) but they suffice.
It's also lacking other advances games have made. Games have become more accessible. Nowadays, you always know where to go. It's clearly indicated or there are even markers on the map.
In this game, you will most of the time have no clue where to go. Which for me, was a great thing. You've got a huge world to explore and to figure out where everything is. I do recommend googling "Shadowman Map" when you get this though, since the original physical release came with that map which makes things a little easier. Yeah that's right, there's no ingame map. But it didn't matter to me, it made the game feel like more of an adventure to me.
The basic gameplay is kind of a 3D Castlevania. You run and jump through the different areas and collect Dark Souls to advance your Shadow Level, which will allow you to go through gates marked with a certain level. On your way you find items to unlock areas which weren't previously accessible. So to fans of that genre, I can definitely recommend this game to you.
One point I didn't love about this game is the combat. Bascially, you lock onto enemies and then shoot them while evading their attacks until they are dead. This will mean a lot of running backwards and shooting with enemies that come towards you. At the beginning it seems like you're almost comically underpowered, mostly because it seems like enemies are only vulnerable to your attacks during certain animations. When get to higher Shadow Levels, you can charge your gun and the fighting becomes much easier.
While the voice acting is pretty good, the story is a little clichéd. The atmosphere makes up for it completely though. The soundtrack is amazingly creepy and while the visuals are dated, there seems to have been a lot of effort put into them. The enemies are very low poly, but still managed to scare me whenever I went around a corner and one of them surprised me. There's many levels with different themes and it's a lot of fun exploring all of them, discovering items you might need for your quest.
I can definitely recommend this to anyone who loves Exploration, Horror Games, Metroid, Zelda and so on. Especially since it's very cheap now and you'll get about 20 hours of fun out of it.

Look, I know I'm pretty easy to please. Basically, if a game subtly rouses me from my existential stupor for long enough to snag a lifeless, unfulfilled grin, I will say "itz purdy gud".
This game does that. I know that doesn't sound like a very good review but, in all seriousness, I find myself waking my PC after a long day of work just to play RErev2 for 30 minutes. It's not phenomenal but it's genuinely not a terrible game. Most people love the Resident Evil games. I loved the PSOne games. I enjoyed 4. I tolerated 5. I even played the forsaken RE games (the outbreaks and even the abysmal RE Survivor on PSOne). Each game I would rate based on their individual merits, or lack thereof, rather than based on brand.
That said, I find myself really enjoying this game. There is nothing OUTSTANDING to see here. The visuals are lackluster. The controls are "ight". The story (thus far) is vegetative. However, considering the price and a very specific collection of things done well, I would absolutely recommend this game.
For me, this game does a lot in a short amount of time. Mostly, I've delved into the raid mode: a level-select, objective style game type. You level character skills and jump into difficulty-based levels. The objectives range from "OMG MURDER ZOMBIES" to "OMG PROTECT THING FROM ZOMBIES". Zombies can spawn with skills. Players can level up skill. Weapons can be imbued with abilities. Abilities for weapons can be unlocked and issued to weapons.
Basically, for a guy with a full schedule, what I enjoy is this:
Game loads up quickly, no issues or crashes
Raid mode allows for instant gratification
Inane but satisfying leveling
Violence
Co-op Violence
Some of the most bizarre emotes ever conceived
Weak but intact campaign (complete with skill tree)
I purchased this on sale for some absurb price. If you stumble upon it for cheap, and you're someone who doesn't have a ton of time to kill, I definitely recommend RErev2 (specifically Raid Mode)!

A flawed but excellent game is probably the best way to describe it.
Fans of the original may feel that the game has been dumbed down - and they would be right. The lack of action points, single base, single dropship, massively limited soldier inventories, and 'activating' enemies, takes away alot of the customisation,  replayability, and unpredictability of the game. In return however, the game is a lot quicker to play, easier to get into, has a much tighter story, and just a lot of fun.
Just be aware that at higher difficulty levels, the annoying and frustrating quirks become rage enducing. The computer already manages multiple improbabe shots, but at higher levels every enemy is a crack shot and can snipe your guys that are behind high cover and at insane ranges. That, added with the fact that enemy units always get a 'free' turn when first encountered has made me rage quit multiple times. It's the 'activating' enemies that does it. For example, when a previously unseen enemy unit activates, flanks my troops with their free turn, then immediately one shots half the squad. Do I reccomend it? Yes, I've put in over 100 hours at this point, and for me that's a lot. Normal difficulty gives a good challenge and is fun, high difficulty is good for the massochists.

I'm an old school tabletop rpg player, so the concept of the Shadowrun setting has always been in the background of my hobby. But I'd never played the setting before due to general lack of interest in the small town groups I had available to me. So when I saw the game available on Steam, I had to buy it and give it a try.
~20-something hours later and the game completed, I can say it was well worth the price I paid for it.
The story's setting behind the game, told in small snippets, is intriguing on its own but the actual game story is pretty good as a stand alone tale without a "larger universe." I enjoyed the customization of the characters/playable races, mixing and matching of skill and magic - basically everything that makes role-playing games great to begin with. I'm also glad they went the route of turn-based combat, similar to older games of the genre, as it allowed for better battlefield control during combat scenarios. The graphics style was beautiful if semi-cartoonish which I thought lent a unique charm to the game.
The only real detraction I have is that I wish there was more: more side missions, more chances to explore the world, more skills and their chances to use them. I realize the dev team was fairly small and they could only do so much; I'm hoping the fan community can add to this defecit.
So if you've never given the Shadowrun universe a try, do so with this game. Wait until it's on sale if you really are not sure if a cyberpunk rpg is your thing. You won't be disappointed! Now I'm off to find a tabletop group that plays Shadowrun to get more of my fix.

I've heard a lot of bad things about KF2, specifically during its early access stage of the game. How valid the complaints were I don't know, but I went into the game after it's full release expecting something bad. However, what I got was, in my opinion, a very good sequel to a very good game.
Nearly everything has been improved, from the UI, graphics, gore, AI, weapons, music,  map design, and also the perks, as well as a few gameplay changes. The most notable changes are the blocking and parrying mechanics. initially I was put off by the parrying and blocking abilities but after playing a bit more I find that they're not necessary to use in order to win; they're a nice little utility for a player to choose to use if they need to.
Now there's a total of 10 perks, each with 10 skills. You can have 5 skills at max level, every 5th level granting you 1 of 2 skills to pick from as well as every level giving you minor perk bonuses.
This is probably the best change since it allows players to adjust their perks to better suit their playstyle. It's definitely given this berserker player a breathe of fresh air.
The gore is also top-notch, the blood is persistent throughout the match so whatever room you hole-up in will be completely covered in blood and guts the entire game. The enemies also take visible damage when shooting or hitting them with a melee weapon, it's a very neat feature.
Overall, this game took what made the original killing floor so great, and made it even better, it's what a proper sequel should do and this game does it well.

There's a stereotype that games make you turn OFF your brain, and are a mindless slug through mundane, disengaging setpieces, This game is a living, breathing, tangible contradiction to that claim. In this part turn-based startegy part base management game, you protect Earth from an invading alien force. Sound familiar? Just another alien game? Rest assured, this game is much more than it appears to be, and is a rare treat for tose looking for a game that pushes you cognitive abilities.

I have never felt my brain go into strategic-overdrive as it did when I played this game. Fair-warning, this game does NOT hold your hand, and to avoid losing (that's right, you can LOSE a 20 hour game) you'll have to be both quick-witted and an effective  base manager. Only those who conduct the proper research, manage resources and money efficiently, smartly equip their soldiers, and maintain their relationships with the countries in the XCOM council will succeed in their turn-based skirmishes, where players control up to six marines to eliminate the alien threat.
The duality of this game is one of its strengths, as the ground battles and the base management go hand-in-hand. Didn't invest in the titan armor research? Well I guess your soldiers are going to perish an unnatural death down on the ground. Failed to protect a member of the council on an important mission? Well I guess Nigeria is pulling out of the XCOM project and thus cutting its funding.
Speaking of failure, that is also another one of the game's strengths, and something you'll be deeply terrified of. You can name and customize your soldiers, and eventually you become attached to them (think pokemon), arming your favorite guy to the teeth and giving him a badass nickname. And these soldiers will go through Hell, facing a mulitude of different alien classes, each with completely distinct looks and effective strategies to use againts. However, your precious characters can die permenantly in these missions if you don't do everything with clockwork effiency. That same urgency extends to the diplomatic side of the game. If you screw up to many times, enough nations will leave the council and you LOSE. This sort of challenge is rare in modern games and is a welcome revival.
All in all, if you're looking for a exhilerating game that engages your brain, tis one's for you.
